tags.feature: - The Depths are an entirely new type of dungeon aimed at small groups of players.
- Added three new playable heroes: Queen of Pain, Slark, and Templar Assassin

tags.balance_change: - All healing in the Depths is reduced by 30%

tags.feature: - The Depths introduce Orange Zones, with new PvP rules
- Within the Depths, players can fight mobs and other groups of players
- Souls can be carried to Altars within the Depths
- Some rooms contain Soulgates, which can be opened with a Soul to exit the Depths
- The deepest level contains a Treasure Vault containing valuable loot
Antiquarian’s Dens are new staging grounds for Albion’s hell-themed instanced PvP content.
- Antiquarian’s Dens contain: Entrances to the Depths, Hellgates, and Corrupted Dungeons
- Antiquarian’s Dens contain: A Bank connected to the corresponding city
- Antiquarian’s Dens contain: A Repair Station
- Antiquarian’s Dens contain: The Antiquarian NPC (more on the Antiquarian below)
The Antiquarian is a new NPC located within Antiquarians Dens.
Two new baby spiders, which can be raised into mounts on an island:
- Tier 5 Hellspinner
- Tier 8 Soulspinner
- The Soulspinner has a unique spell, Soulspindle Pounce, which lifts it into the air and allows it to jump to a different location
- Demon Cape Crests
- Hell-themed Avatar and Avatar Ring
This update makes some adjustments to Hellgates and Corrupted Dungeons to make them more accessible, more rewarding, and improve matchmaking.
- Hellgates are now accessible via an entrance in the Antiquarian’s Den

tags.balance_change: - Hellgate Map item salvage value has been increased from 20% → 100%
- Item Power entry requirements have been adjusted: 2v2 Non-Lethal: 800 → 700
- Item Power entry requirements have been adjusted: 5v5 Non-Lethal: 800 → 700
- Item Power entry requirements have been adjusted: 5v5 Lethal: 1000 → 900
- Item Power softcap: 2v2 Lethal: 1100 (20% scaling) → 1100 (35% scaling)
- Item Power softcap: 5v5 Lethal: 1200 (35% scaling) → 1100 (35% scaling)
- PvP knockdown time in Hellgates is now unlimited
- Loot no longer scales with Infamy
- Fame Scaling from Infamy has been reduced from 50% to 20%
- 2v2 Hellgates: Hell buff now adds an additional 10% damage increase

tags.feature: - Removed line-of-sight blocker from various elements inside Hellgates
- After a victory, players now heal and have any negative effects removed
- 10v10 Hellgates have been removed
- Corrupted Dungeons are now accessible via an entrance in the Antiquarian’s Den

tags.balance_change: - Corrupted Dungeon Map item salvage value has been increased from 20% to 100%
- Entry requirements now use base Item Power, rather than average Item Power: Hunter: 800 → 700
- Entry requirements now use base Item Power, rather than average Item Power: Slayer: 1200 → 1100

tags.feature: - Matchmaking has been accelerated

tags.balance_change: - Loot no longer scales with Infamy
- Maximum Fame scaling from Infamy has been reduced from 50% → 20%

tags.feature: - After a victory, players now heal and have any negative effects removed
A reworked early-game experience offers a more structured and streamlined introduction to Albion, while guiding new players through a broad range of available content.
- A new First Steps category has been added to the Albion Journal, continuing the guided experience beyond the initial tutorial
- Upon receiving the Journal from Captain Tia, players choose from three starting Paths that reflect different playstyles:
- Adventurer: PvE-focused, introduces players to different PvE activities and the Marketplace
- Duelist: Emphasizes early PvP with supporting PvE to unlock and equip combat gear
- Gatherer: Centers on gathering and fishing, without combat
- Your chosen Path can be changed at any time
- Once a starting Path has been completed, the full Journal becomes accessible
- Players who complete all three Paths are awarded with a scholarly vanity hat to mark their graduation
- Shortened tutorial, with less gathering and crafting involved
- Text in tutorial quests shortened, and objective lists in quest UIs reduced
- Improved tutorial pacing to gradually introduce players to information
- Various smaller improvements
- Improved readability of tutorial HUD hints
- Several UI and guidance improvements to the Journal system
- New Starter Town selection screen for players who have completed the tutorial and new characters who have skipped the tutorial
- All buildings and various NPCs now display a tooltip that explains their function
- The warning popup when entering a Yellow Zone for the first time has been removed
- The warning popup when purchasing an item from the Marketplace has been removed
- A new Showroom Island has been added
- This is a mockup island which players can visit to preview available features and amenities
- Accessible via the Island Merchant
- An Arena Master has been added to all Starter Towns, replacing the Expedition Master
This update introduces the final two Crystal Weapons, with their own unique spells:
- Truebolt Hammer (Hammer): Hyperstatic opens a vein of magical energy, protecting allies while stunning and damaging enemies
- Stillgaze Staff (Shapeshifter Staff): Transforms you into a Crystal Cobra, able to both spit at your enemies and petrify them with your gaze
This update introduces a new Albion Journal category: Character Progression.
- This category rewards progression on the Destiny Board, encouraging players to explore different equipment and playstyles
- Unique rewards embody themes of enlightenment, wisdom, and mysticism
In addition, two new subcategories have been added: ‘The Depths’ under the PvP category, and ‘Antiquarian’s Den’ under Exploration.
The way Learning Points function has been overhauled to be smoother and more intuitive.

tags.balance_change: - Destiny Board nodes no longer have a 20% threshold at which Learning Points can be spent to complete them

tags.feature: - A new Quick Learn system has been introduced, replacing Auto-Learn
- Nodes which are unlocked through Quick Learn also have Quick Learn applied to them by default
- Auto-Learn settings that were active before the update are now applied to Quick Learn instead
- Progress made on nodes before the update has been multiplied by five within their current level.
- Tracking mobs in the open world no longer change regions during a hunt
- Blue and Yellow Zones now feature Tier 3 Tracking mobs, designed as more accessible, entry-level encounters than Tier 4:
- These are not affected by player crowding and remain available even with multiple players nearby
- Starting a new hunt now clears the markers of other tracks on the Minimap and Region Map, making it easier to focus on the current target
- All active quests, challenges, Destiny Board nodes, and tracked Albion Journal missions are now visible in a single HUD element
- Additional trackers such as the Party Finder, Arena Queue, or Region Queue also appear here when active
- The tracker automatically adjusts based on what’s most relevant to the player’s current state and stage of progression, ensuring key objectives are visible without overwhelming the interface
- The Combined HUD Tracker can be configured via an integrated Settings menu, and in the HUD Editor
- Searching for items by category has been improved in all UIs which support this (eg. Marketplace, Bank Overview, Loadouts, etc.)
- This now uses more intuitive categories and subcategories, making it easier to find and compare items within these UIs
- Vanity item icons now display an indicator of their source (e.g. Albion Store, events, referrals, etc.) in both the Appearance UI and Inspect UI
- Within the Appearance UI, vanity items can now be filtered by source
- Duration of combat displayed extended from 10 seconds to 3 minutes
- A dedicated tab has been added to display crowd control effects
- Albion Journal opening performance has been improved
- Minimap skull indicators are now hidden for 1v1 kills, unless the player directly witnessed the kill
- Improved the food supply UI for crafting buildings to more accurately reflect Silver rewards
- Kill Details in the Kill Trophy UI are now disabled in contexts where kill data isn’t available (e.g. Chat, Trade Window, Bank Overview)
- [CONTROLLER] D-Pad can now be held down to continuously move between elements
- Blue and Yellow Zones in the open world (and Static Dungeons in these zones) have an Item Power softcap

tags.balance_change: - Softcap: 1200 IP
- Item Power & Awakened Weapon Trait scaling: 20%

tags.feature: - Yellow Mists and Knightfall Abbeys mirroring the open world have the same softcap
- Randomized Dungeons are not affected by the Item Power softcap

tags.balance_change: - Durability damage on knockdown now scales down when the Base Item Power of an item is affected by an Item Power Cap
- Repair Costs are also scaled down as a result of this change
- In these cases, the repair cost of an item is equivalent to an item of equivalent Item Power

tags.feature: - This change affects all content that scales Item Power
- Bonuses that provide extra Item Power are not included in this calculation (e.g. from Quality and Destiny Board bonuses)

tags.balance_change: - Knockdown duration after being defeated in PvP in Yellow Zones has been reduced from 180 to 90s

tags.feature: - Rewards from this line are now limited to Expedition and Avatar unlocks

tags.balance_change: - Removed bonus damage and defense against mobs from Reaver

tags.feature: - Mob Power has also been reduced accordingly, so players with Tier 8 Reaver will notice no difference, and new players are no longer gated by Reaver unlocks
- Given the significance of these changes, their impact and player feedback will be monitored closely
- Legendary Resource Mists are now always Tier 8

tags.balance_change: - Resource Wisps are now slightly rarer but have a much higher fill rate

tags.feature: - Multiple artifacts can now be melded at once
- Melding is now quicker

tags.balance_change: - The Fame buff from World Bosses has been reduced from 1% to 0.5% per stack

tags.feature: - Faction-flagged players now receive a protection bubble at the threshold of the city for which they are flagged
- Players now retain their Faction Flag after participating in the Arena and Expeditions

tags.balance_change: - Standard Arena entry requirements have been lowered from 700 to 600 IP, and equipment is now hardcapped at 600 IP

tags.feature: - Carried items dropped near exits are now pushed back to ensure they remain accessible
- Maps to Randomized Dungeons now can only locate dungeons within regions of the same type
- A short delay has been added between allowed gate interactions, to prevent players from accidentally entering and immediately exiting castle gates when double-clicking
- Outlands player count estimates now show 16 - 30 and 31 - 50 ranges, instead of a single 16 - 50 range

tags.balance_change: - Bleed damage dealt by Morgana arbalists has been reduced

tags.feature: - [CONTROLLER] Improved targeting of area target spells
- [CONTROLLER] The targeting speed of area target spells should now be consistent on all frame rates

notes.title: The Crucible Begins!
notes.content:
[img]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4399d02fa33957a74d6c5cab3dc113b9682939ad.png[/img]

[b]The Crucible[/b] is set to ignite! Starting [b]July 5[/b] at [b]00:00 UTC[/b] on [b]Albion Asia[/b], and [b]11:00 UTC[/b] on [b]Albion Americas [/b]and[b] Europe[/b], this month-long, high-stakes competition will bring together [b]over 100 creators[/b] from across the gaming world to battle it out in Albion.

Each creator has formed a [b]brand-new guild[/b] to battle for glory, with veteran [b]AOCP Creators[/b] stepping in as expert guides to help them hit the ground running. For the first four weeks of the Guild Season, contenders must earn [b]Season Points[/b] and [b]Challenge Points[/b] to climb the rankings, with all points earned multiplied by 1.5 after the second week. When it’s over, one creator will stand above the rest as the champion.

At stake is a share of thousands of gifted Twitch subscriptions… and for the winner, the ultimate prize: a [b]real-life Galatine Pair[/b], forged in steel by the legendary weaponsmiths at [b]Man at Arms[/b].

[previewyoutube=irIP9xWm82c;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Follow the Action![/h3]
The Crucible contenders will stream their progress weekly as the race for dominance intensifies, while expert coverage and commentary will be provided throughout the contest by [b]AOCP Creators[/b] and [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url]. Follow your favorite participants, tune in for the biggest battles, and don’t miss a moment of the action.

And a special [b]Twitch Drop[/b] will be available too: from [b]July 5[/b] at [b]10:00 UTC[/b] to [b]July 20[/b] at [b]09:30 UTC[/b], gifting 2 subs to any Crucible participant, AOCP Creator, or AlbionTV will guarantee you the exclusive [b]Brown Alpaca[/b] mount skin.

Tune in to watch these creators clash for glory, and follow the official [b]leaderboard[/b] [url=https://albiononline.com/crucible/][b]here[/b][/url] to track the action. Let the battle commence!

notes.title: Season 28 Begins July 5
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce8b5e9ab7439b9ba58a0be0f6be676744087ce.jpeg[/img]

The last[b] Guild Season[/b] reshaped Albion’s balance of power through betrayal and revolt, and now the stage is set for a fresh contest between guilds eager to settle the score. 

[b]Season 28[/b] kicks off on [b]July 5[/b], at the following times: [b]Albion Asia[/b] at [b]00:00 UTC[/b], and [b]Albion Americas[/b] and [b]Albion Europe[/b] at [b]11:00 UTC[/b]. 

Players can once again take on the [b]Conqueror’s Challenge[/b] to earn exclusive [b]Avatar Sets[/b], [b]loot chests[/b], and [b]Fame buffs[/b]. And this season brings a fiery new twist with the arrival of the [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yiw6yOAFfY8&][b]Depths[/b][/url], an instanced PvP dungeon introduced in the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/abyssal-depths][b]Abyssal Depths[/b][/url] update. 

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/07a9e6649cbde83b27be0b402dfd31fa99801ad0.png[/img]

A [b]dedicated Challenge category[/b] rewards those bold enough to descend into its hellish corridors. To mark its debut, the Depths Challenge will grant [b]boosted Season Point rewards[/b] for the duration of the season. With extra points on the line, now’s the time to lock in your comps, practice your rotations, and push your guild’s progress.

[h3]Season Schedule Highlights[/h3][list]	[*][b]July 5[/b]: Season start and Invasion Day[/*]	[*][b]August 2[/b]: Mid-Season Invasion Day, double scoring begins[/*]	[*][b]August 30[/b]: Final Invasion Day[/*]	[*][b]September 2[/b]: Season ends[/*][/list]For the full season schedule, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/213301-Season-28-Schedules/][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8f3026da394dba42efdf4c4e7e89f7a28f8c8cc0.jpeg[/img]

[/h3]
[h3]New to Guild Seasons? Here's What You Need to Know![/h3]
[b]Guild Seasons[/b] are a key part of Albion's competitive landscape, where guilds battle over two months to claim territories, earn Season Points, rise up the rankings and earn coveted rewards. Participating in a Guild Season allows you to contribute to your guild's success through various activities. Even if you’re not focused on PvP, you can still help your guild gather [b]Season Points[/b] and unlock valuable rewards!

Ready to get started? Use the [url=https://albiononline.com/guides/article/guild-finder+106][b]Guild Finder[/b][/url] to connect with a guild and start your journey to glory, and check out our [url=https://albiononline.com/guides/article/guild-seasons+100][b]Guild Season Guide[/b][/url] for all the necessary information.

If you want to stay on top of all the action, [b]AlbionTV[/b] ([url=http://twitch.tv/albiononline][b]twitch.tv/albiononline[/b][/url]) has you covered! [b]Subscribe now[/b] and never miss a moment – from massive territory battles to shocking upsets, catch live coverage of the season’s biggest moments and relive the highlights that shape the rankings. See you on the battlefield!

notes.title: Dev Talk: New Player Experience and Quality-of-Life
notes.content:
Ahead of the release of [url=https://albiononline.com/update/abyssal-depths][b]Abyssal Depths[/b][/url] on [b]June 30[/b], Co-Creative Director[b] Michael Schwahn[/b] is joined by Combat Designer[b] Nick Yaloz[/b] and UI Lead[b] Raoul Zander[/b] to present the revamped [b]new player experience[/b], [b]UI improvements[/b], and two powerful new [b]Crystal Weapons[/b]. From wide-eyed newcomers to battle-hardened brawlers ready to shake up the meta, this update has something for everyone. Let’s take a look:

[previewyoutube=pMnUK0rWdbo?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]New Player Experience[/h3]
A core focus of Abyssal Depths is supporting Albion’s long-term growth by improving the [b]experience for new players[/b] just entering the game.

A new [b]First Steps[/b] category has been added to the [b]Albion Journal[/b]:
[list]	[*]This system offers structured [b]post-tutorial paths[/b] for PvE, PvP, and gathering[/*]	[*]Each path gradually introduces core gameplay mechanics, with [b]hints[/b] and [b]visual guidance[/b][/*]	[*][b]The full Journal remains hidden until a path is completed, at which point players unlock:[/b]	[list]		[*]A [b]guide[/b] on how to use the Journal[/*]		[*]A set of first-step [b]milestones[/b] to encourage further exploration[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/47c6b59c5aeb8b5166c2844adb078eff4f8ba208.png][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/64312adb6c7f768bd306db752362b5f8a85f6d53.png[/img][/url]

Additional changes aim to expose players to more content earlier:
[list]	[*]Tier 3 [b]Tracking [/b]mobs have been added to Blue and Yellow Zones[/*]	[*]A [b]Showroom Island[/b] lets players preview island features without purchasing one[/*]	[*]Item Power requirements have been lowered for the [b]Arena[/b] and [b]Hunter Corrupted Dungeons[/b][/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/14f789246d4228d990ce11c469c7c9b66fe2211e.png][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4c806339d286b8c863c4538eb1ca2fd8d4393af2.png[/img][/url]

The [b]tutorial[/b] itself has been revised to:
[list]	[*]Reduce the focus on gathering and crafting[/*]	[*]Improve pacing by showing less text and information[/*][/list]These onboarding changes are supported by broader changes like improvements to early combat gear and UI refinements.

[h3]UI Improvements[/h3]
Several broad changes are aimed at improving usability and accessibility:
[list]	[*]A complete [b]recategorization[/b] of all items in the game:	[list]		[*]Designed to simplify browsing in the [b]Marketplace[/b] and other interfaces[/*]		[*]Lets players quickly find and compare specific items via improved [b]category dropdowns[/b][/*]	[/list][/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/49c1a5d855f5f7fcca78b76387bb3b5a1dd77034.png][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9af3851c1a07015d0fb02326a7d2b9a25e4150fd.png[/img][/url]
[list]	[*]A new [b]Combined HUD Tracker[/b]:	[list]		[*]Merges previously separate trackers into [b]one consistent, unified layout[/b][/*]		[*]Integrates better with the [b]HUD Editor[/b][/*]		[*]Includes a global[b] toggle shortcut[/b] for desktop users[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4a3726ae47b43b1a25b7e8368ca261ff7494fe5d.png][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c928d8aac40ff3942f1e833b1e89ef8a4c558ab4.png[/img][/url]
[list]	[*]Additional UI improvements:	[list]		[*]The Appearance UI now shows where [b]vanity items [/b]come from[/*]		[*]The [b]Artifact Foundry [/b]supports bulk crafting[/*]		[*]New [b]Tooltips[/b] have been added to buildings and NPCs to help players find relevant tasks[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][h3]Learning Point Rework[/h3]
Abyssal Depths brings a rework of the [b]Learning Point [/b]system.
[list]	[*]The 20% threshold for Learning Points has been removed[/*]	[*]Instead, they are gradually consumed, multiplying Fame gains by five on active nodes[/*]	[*]The Auto-Learn toggle has been replaced with a [b]Quick Learn [/b]toggle[/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5ccad397e6110f04c1ed1a084862c61f24a0d6ca.png][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/67200e5e70b43df40d5321ecfd792d47d236ce94.png[/img][/url]
[list]	[*]Players can now clearly see:	[list]		[*]Which nodes are Quick Learn enabled[/*]		[*]An overview of all[b] boosted nodes[/b] by category[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]When the update goes live:	[list]		[*]Any skill node with 20% or more progress will be [b]automatically completed[/b] at no LP cost[/*]		[*]Players may wish to progress to 20% on their nodes before the update launches[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][h3]New Crystal Weapons[/h3]
This update also introduces the final additions to the Crystal Weapon lineup:
[list]	[*][b]Truebolt Hammer[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Hyperstatic[/b] opens cracks of magical energy[/*]		[*][b]Shields[/b] nearby allies[/*]		[*]Applies [b]static[/b] stacks to enemies		[list]			[*]Hitting enemies affected by static triggers a powerful [b]stun[/b][/*]		[/list][/*]	[/list][/*][/list][video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/68516c2ac94c6_720.mp4[/video][list]	[*][b]Stillgaze Staff[/b]	[list]		[*]Transforms the user into a [b]Crystal Cobra[/b][/*]		[*]Grants [b]two active abilities[/b] and [b]two passives[/b][/*]		[*]Features [b]Serpent’s Gaze[/b], a channeled spell that petrifies unmounted enemies		[list]			[*][b]Petrified[/b] enemies are stunned and cannot be cleansed, but they gain damage resistance and are immune to forced movement[/*]		[/list][/*]	[/list][/*][/list][video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/68516b5f8ad88_720.mp4[/video]

With Abyssal Depths just around the corner, we’re very close to seeing these features in action. Meanwhile, if you haven’t already seen them, check out our [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-abyssal-depths][b]introduction to the update[/b][/url] and our deep dive into the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-the-depths][b]Depths[/b][/url]. We can’t wait to see how you take on this new content when the update releases, and we’ll see you [b]June 30[/b]!

notes.title: Dive into Albion’s Abyssal Depths on June 30
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dd85ff0eb581558ba8234ef556cfeb20f191b20a.png[/img]

The [b]Abyssal Depths[/b] are calling… On [b]June 30[/b], Albion’s next major content update arrives, offering new paths into Albion’s deepest reaches. [b]The Depths[/b] provide a thrilling new PvP experience for new and veteran players alike. The [b]Antiquarian’s Den[/b] acts as a route into an array of hell-themed content, with new rewards for those who fully explore this. A reworked [b]new player experience[/b] presents structured guidance to Albion’s gameplay. And a new [b]Albion Journal[/b] category and [b]Crystal Weapons[/b] offer coveted rewards to experienced players. With all this and more, dare you look into Albion’s Abyssal Depths?

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/07a9e6649cbde83b27be0b402dfd31fa99801ad0.png[/img]

[h3]Enter the Depths[/h3]
[b]The Depths[/b] are an all-new type of instanced PvP, located in Albion’s ancient underground aqueducts. Players are trapped inside a collapsing dungeon for a limited time, and must battle fierce mobs – and each other – to earn loot and buffs. Once the exits open, players can decide whether to make their escape or venture deeper for greater rewards. And if killed in combat, fallen fighters can be revived by their allies with their equipped gear intact, allowing them to return to the fray with a vengeance. The Depths provide players with an ideal gateway into Albion’s competitive PvP, offering meaningful, adrenaline-fueled combat without the danger of gear loss.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/43faf3d8c0594d5b1ede71644fe78ab92b63df15.png[/img]

[h3]Diabolical Dens[/h3]
The Depths can be accessed from the [b]Antiquarian’s Den[/b], a new subterranean staging ground for all of Albion’s most infernal content. Each city on the Royal Continent contains an Antiquarian’s Den entrance, from which players can dive into the Depths, [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and [b]Hellgates[/b]. These lairs serve as a place to gear up and meet others who wish to test themselves in these areas, making matchmaking faster and fairer. And within these dens you can also meet the [b]Antiquarian[/b] itself – a sinister, mysterious merchant offering hellish rewards to those who’ve proven themselves in Albion’s underworld, including new spider mounts for you to raise and ride into combat.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/66fae08cf55c0b415bb1a991aaef0a662f4e6d32.png[/img]

[h3]Further Improvements[/h3]
Abyssal Depths reworks Albion’s [b]new player experience[/b], providing a smoother and more structured entry to the game while introducing players to the breadth of content they can enjoy. A dedicated [b]Albion Journal[/b] category offers concrete goals for the initial stages of the game, with rewards for every milestone reached, and there’s also a new [b]Character Progression[/b] category based on Destiny Board progress. The final two [b]Crystal Weapons[/b], for the Shapeshifter Staff and Hammer, are coming for successful Guild Season players. And there are further [b]quality-of-life improvements [/b]across the board, such as a new combined tracker in the HUD and a reworked Marketplace categorization system.

For more info, watch our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r_q20UZ-fKQ][b]introductory Dev Talk[/b][/url] and our deep dive into the [b]Depths[/b], and check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/abyssal-depths][b]official update page[/b][/url] here:

[b][url=https://albiononline.com/update/abyssal-depths]LEARN MORE[/url][/b]

notes.title: Dev Talk: The Depths and Antiquarian’s Dens
notes.content:
Albion’s next major content update, [b]Abyssal Depths[/b], launches [b]June 30[/b], bringing a renewed focus on instanced PvP, along with updates to the new player experience and further quality-of-life improvements. Following our [b]introduction to the update[/b], it’s time to dive into the fire with an, ahem, [i]in-depth [/i]look at a brand-new type of dungeon, along with a new staging ground for all of Albion’s most hellish content. Join [b]Game Director Moritz Bokelmann [/b]and [b]Co-Creative Director Michael Schwahn [/b]to get a taste of what’s on the way.

[previewyoutube=yiw6yOAFfY8?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]The Depths[/h3]
[b]The Depths [/b]are a brand-new type of instanced PvP dungeon.
[list]	[*]Aimed at groups of [b]2-3 players[/b], though daring solo players can join[/*]	[*]Once inside, all players are [b]trapped [/b]for a limited, but undisclosed, period[/*]	[*]There are [b]three different levels [/b]within, with greater dangers and greater rewards as you go deeper[/*]	[*]After a time, [b]exits open[/b]	[list]		[*]At this point you can decide whether to [b]leave [/b]with your loot, or [b]venture further [/b]in[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c60f192d997b0a1c3770ff71d72718aa1a0c5f5b.jpeg[/img]

What’s within the Depths?
[list]	[*]Inside, you’ll encounter [b]mobs[/b], [b]loot[/b], and [b]other groups of players[/b][/*]	[*]Early areas focus on clearing rooms of [b]mobs[/b]	[list]		[*]When a room is cleared, you are rewarded with [b]loot [/b]or [b]buffs [/b]that persist throughout the dungeon[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Along the way, you can collect different types of [b]Souls[/b]	[list]		[*][b]Hostile Souls [/b]from fallen enemies[/*]		[*][b]Neutral Souls [/b]from mobs or players who forfeited the dungeon[/*]		[*][b]Friendly Souls [/b]from your fallen allies[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Souls can be transported to [b]Altars [/b]within the Depths	[list]		[*]Hostile and Neutral Souls can be taken to the [b]Altar of Greed [/b]for loot[/*]		[*]Friendly Souls can be taken to the [b]Altar of Awakening [/b]to revive your allies[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]The third and final level contains a [b]Treasure Vault[/b]:	[list]		[*]To access this, players must collect [b]keys[/b] throughout the level[/*]		[*]Delivering these to the [b]Treasure Vault[/b] will unlock its riches[/*]		[*][b]Other groups[/b] will also be fighting for this reward[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ef9c023ef1ebb631570116da6559e9cfcecdce24.jpeg[/img]

The Depths introduce a new ruleset: [b]Orange PvP[/b].
[list]	[*]Orange PvP is a [b]bridge[/b] between knockdown and full-loot PvP[/*]	[*]On death, players	[list]		[*][b]Retain[/b] their equipped gear[/*]		[*][b]Lose[/b] their inventory items[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Orange PvP areas have an [b]Item Power soft-cap[/b][/*][/list]The Depths offer players a balance between accessibility and risk. Players can test their PvP skills and strategies in a competitive and rewarding environment, without the tough consequences of full-loot combat.

[h3]The Antiquarian’s Den[/h3]
The [b]Antiquarian’s Den[/b] is a new hub for Albion’s hell-themed content.
[list]	[*]This can be accessed directly from [b]any Royal City and Caerleon[/b][/*]	[*]It offers access to [b]Hellgates[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and the [b]Depths[/b][/*]	[*]Players can [b]gather and find teams [/b]in these Dens[/*]	[*]It contains a local [b]bank [/b]connected to each city[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c75e9a4fc7f5256c84d0f52b7538fd90c4a8463d.jpeg[/img]

Within this Den, you’ll find a new NPC: [b]the Antiquarian[/b]. The Antiquarian offers hell-themed rewards, such as:
[list]	[*]An [b]Avatar[/b] and [b]Avatar Ring[/b][/*]	[*][b]Demon Cape Crests[/b][/*]	[*]Two spider mount babies, the Tier 5 [b]Hellspinner[/b] and Tier 8 [b]Soulspinner[/b]	[list]		[*]These can be raised on your island, and the Soulspinner has a [b]unique new spell[/b][/*]	[/list][/*][/list][b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0ee3c95c6e1bdc472fae162942db7e5f20991159.jpeg[/img]

[/b]

Purchasing these rewards requires sufficient [b]Antiquarian Standing[/b].
[list]	[*]This is a new [b]PvP progression system[/b][/*]	[*]Antiquarian Standing can be increased by:	[list]		[*]Completing [b]Hellgates[/b][/*]		[*]Completing [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b][/*]		[*]Offering enemies’ [b]Souls [/b]at Altars within the Depths[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3c66e09679d77b56f5d31775e83361ea05ebea91.jpeg[/img]

Antiquarian Standing rewards long-term engagement with this content, and offers instanced PvP players a new way to engage with Albion’s economy.

[h3]Hellgate and Corrupted Dungeon Changes[/h3]
The Abyssal Depths update also addresses some issues with [b]Hellgates[/b] and [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b].
[list]	[*]Direct entrance from Antiquarian’s Dens make them far more [b]accessible[/b][/*]	[*]This access hub increases the [b]matchmaking pool[/b], creating fairer matchups[/*]	[*]Matchmaking has also been made [b]quicker and more consistent[/b][/*]	[*]Baseline [b]loot[/b] has been increased across the board[/*]	[*][b]Infamy [/b]no longer scales loot[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0180410bb19ac4fe567ef591999cf87db3368791.jpeg[/img]

We can’t wait to bring you all this in the Abyssal Depths update, and to see how you deal with the challenges, build your strategies, and make this content your own. Stay tuned for our final Dev Talk before the update releases, where we’ll go over the changes coming to the new player experience, along with some of the other features coming on June 30. See you soon!

notes.title: Get the Summer Fawn this Referral Season

Where sunlight filters through fresh green leaves and the ancient world breathes with new life, the [b]Summer Fawn[/b] steps timidly from the tree line. Soft-footed, radiant, and full of promise, this skin transforms your[b] Giant Stag[/b] into a delicate young deer, available to all your characters on the same server. Sure, it may not strike fear like a direwolf or command respect like a battle-worn stallion, but isn’t cuteness its own kind of power?

notes.title: The Morgana Challenge Brings Back the Darkness
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7cb5cebaf2ab918f9b578012d1e47c3718e1cf13.png[/img]

The [b]Morgana Challenge[/b] begins, as cultists loyal to the exiled sorceress gather in secret to restore her lost power. Embrace the darkness and earn a reward pulled straight from the depths of nightmare: the [b]Morgana Raven[/b]. Draped in shadow, this unholy mount glides with spectral speed and unleashes a cry that scatters the weak in fear. Earn [b]Challenge Points[/b], claim your mount, and let the darkness be your weapon!

[h3]Embrace the Darkness[/h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/52730b26d43c7acb500a97266e27664755578c46.png[/img]
[b]MORGANA RAVEN:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the popular [b]Morgana Raven[/b], a fearsome, fast-moving flying mount with an area-of-effect Fear spell. (Note: the Morgana Raven requires the same terrain pathing as all other mounts, and cannot fly over gaps or obstacles).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/175ed5e819977913f6ace2cd32c91c580891d193.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Morgana Challenge Avatar Ring[/b], a menacing, fiery frame that will give your avatar an aura of dread. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar ring for one character.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d8d2b4012ed682b05e9e12428f4bd0ba820113b2.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Morgana Challenge chests[/b]. These chests contain valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes and Silver bags, along with unique Morgana-themed furniture items.

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/680f8cc040401_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 6
notes.content:
[quote][i]This light patch brings a handful of balance tweaks, background optimizations, and minor fixes.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Arcane Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Evensong and Locus have fallen out of favor as Great Arcane has grown increasingly valued. Their cooldowns have been adjusted to promote variance in the arcane support slot.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Dark Sphere (Evensong)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 42s → 38s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The Void (Malevolent Locus)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 68s → 62s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Time Freeze (Great Arcane Staff)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 45s → 50s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Frost Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]As most Frost players have shifted toward Frozen Surge and sustain builds, some damage has been added back to Ice Shard to better reward cast speed-focused setups.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ice Shard (all Frost Staffs)	[list]		[*]Damage vs players: 125 → 130[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Spears[/b]

[quote][i]Cripple’s damage has been increased, as it was too conservative for a low-range, single-target ability that requires users to hold it for the right moment.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Cripple (all Spears)	[list]		[*]Damage: 106.03 → 120[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b]

[quote][i]Hamstring’s first cast has felt underwhelming for players, so its base slow duration has been increased, the time window to cast Heroic Leap extended, and the cooldown when not multicasting reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Hamstring (all Swords)	[list]		[*]1st cast cooldown: 10s → 8s[/*]		[*]Time window duration: 3s → 4s[/*]		[*]Slow duration: 3s → 4s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]War Gloves[/b]

[quote][i]Create Opening’s restrictive range has limited its effective output, so its baseline damage and resistance reduction have been increased to improve its overall value.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Create Opening (all War Gloves)	[list]		[*]Damage: 72 → 80[/*]		[*]Pierce: 0.1 → 0.12[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Potions[/b]

[quote][i]Hellfire Potion has been a powerful addition for builds with heavy CC but limited damage. Its damage against players has been too high, especially when paired with Smuggler’s Cape in IP-capped content, so it has been reduced. To keep the potion attractive, its healing reduction has been increased.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Hellfire Potion	[list]		[*]Damage vs players (700 IP): 42.4 → 36[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (800 IP): 64.5 → 54.8[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (900 IP): 82.5 → 70.1[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (1000 IP): 98.2 → 83.5[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (1100 IP): 112 → 95.2[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (1200 IP): 126 → 107[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (1300 IP): 138 → 117[/*]		[*]Damage vs players (1400 IP): 149 → 126[/*]		[*]Healing received reduction: 35% → 50%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Mounts[/b]

[quote][i]Take Cover! and Charge! have been reworked to improve performance and address behavior issues.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Take Cover!, Charge! (Command Mammoth)	[list]		[*]Buffs are now applied via an aura, and are removed when leaving this area[/*]		[*]Buffs are no longer purgeable[/*]				[*]High Command now correctly increases their effects for the full duration[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where the first tab of the Guild Details UI could appear empty[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the 'Copied to clipboard' message would stay visible after closing the Guild Members UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the ‘For Sale’ tooltip would stick to the cursor after closing the minimap[/*][/list]
[b]Other Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue preventing Warden Mastery Pack skins from being tradable on the Marketplace in Albion Europe[/*][/list]

notes.title: Season 27 Begins This Weekend!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a3ec20788ced4366da9404959d95cfa6045bddf5.png[/img]

A new [b]Guild Season[/b] starts this weekend, and after the backstabs, steamrolls, and razor-thin finishes that defined [b]Season 26[/b], the stage is set for another wild ride.

Guilds across Albion are once again rallying their forces for a season-long war that will test their strategy, strength, and resolve in a battle for lasting glory. Tune in to [url=http://twitch.tv/albiononline][b]twitch.tv/albiononline[/b][/url] to witness history in the making as the [b]AlbionTV[/b] crew brings you live coverage of the opening [b]Invasion Day[/b], complete with commentary and analysis:
[list]	[*][b]Albion Asia[/b]: April 19, 14:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Europe[/b]: April 19, 18:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Americas[/b]: April 20, 01:00 UTC[/*][/list][h3]What to Expect This Season?[/h3]
The [b]Might requirements[/b] for Treasures, Crystal Creatures, Smugglers, and Gathering categories have all been reduced. For the first three categories, Season Point payouts were also adjusted to maintain balance in total output. Gathering, however, retains its full reward potential – giving smaller or economy-focused guilds greater opportunity to work up their way up the rankings.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9bb7a2a94bc19325dc9213cf6fbbd8aa0c3f73ac.jpeg[/img]

For more info, check out our [url=https://albiononline.com/news/season-27-coming][b]Season 27 preview[/b][/url], and for the full schedule see this [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/209673-Season-27-Schedules/][b]forum post[/b][/url].

[h3]Ready to Join the Fight?[/h3]
[b]Guild Seasons[/b] are open to players of all types – PvP veterans, gatherers, strategists, and support players alike. From leading the charge to contributing from the backline, every action matters. Use the [url=https://albiononline.com/guides/article/guild-finder+106][b]Guild Finder[/b][/url] to connect with allies, and check out our [url=https://albiononline.com/guides/article/guild-seasons+100][b]Guild Season Guide[/b][/url] to learn how to make your contribution count.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c672f66e7c4154cdd4a6cb303f02e2b8f02e3701.png[/img]

notes.title: The Rites of Spring Returns: Now with Even More Chocolate!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/233129f5d5bd9da457a9a24bda8d35b215a94d27.jpeg[/img]

Spring has sprung in Albion, and the chocolate-fueled eggstravaganza begins soon! For two full weeks, the[b] Rites of Spring[/b] returns in a cocoa-rich celebration. From Fame boosts to combat-ready bunnies, get ready for an event full of loot, fluff, and far too many types of eggs.

After each server’s next maintenance, the chocolate rush begins:
[list]	[*][b]Albion Asia[/b]: April 14 at 23:00 UTC – April 28 at 23:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Americas & Europe[/b]: April 15 at 10:00 UTC – April 29 at 10:00 UTC[/*][/list][h3]Snack for Fame[/h3]
This year, Albion’s bunnies have outdone themselves, scattering even more types of treats across the land. Find new [b]Chocolate Eggs[/b] and crack them open to get a [b]15% Fame boost[/b] for 30 minutes. Just don’t try sitting on these – everyone knows bunnies don’t hatch from eggs…

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/fe26d93a31afb6ab98a2c7bc624d07c74c73f864.jpeg[/img]

[h3]The Cottontail Mafia Returns[/h3]
Oh, who are we kidding? Of course bunnies hatch from eggs! Keep an eye out for the rare [b]Cottontail Eggs[/b] during your egg-hunting adventures. These can be raised into Tier 8 bunny mounts with serious hop: the [b]Spring Cottontail[/b], a soft, snowy puffball of speed and bounce, and the rarer, darker [b]Caerleon Cottontail[/b], whose leap ends with a fearsome bite that roots enemies and sends them running. Don’t let the fluff fool you… these mounts bite back!

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/624f050bc1743_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]Hunt for Spring Loot[/h3]
Wondering where to find all those eggs? [b]Spring Treasure Chests[/b] will be popping up across the open world, packed with Chocolate Eggs and, if fortune favors you, a Cottontail Egg or two.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/85a6cd1548e1db89cb5c8d1b1622dff8a56f6c93.jpeg[/img]

Meanwhile, [b]Colored Eggs[/b] have also returned. These vibrant finds may [i]also[/i] contain Chocolate Eggs and, on very rare occasions, a Cottontail Egg. But that’s not all: you might also uncover [b]Chocolate bars[/b] to boost your Energy, and, most importantly, [b]Surprise Eggs[/b]. Bring those to the Vanity Merchant and trade them for seasonal delights like the [b]Bunny Stalker[/b] wardrobe, the [b]Snow Bunny Hat[/b] that spawns cuddly companions, or the coveted [b]Eggsecutioner[/b] – an overengineered contraption that lobs eggs and spawns critters on impact.

Phew! At this point, we’ve got more eggs than sense, and more chocolate than any one adventurer should safely eat.

It’s chaotic, it’s egg-cellent, and it all begins very soon. Hop to it!

notes.title: A New Batch of Crystal Weapons is Here!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1b3925a40474f859512772a751b0dc4814ece472.png[/img]

With [b]Guild Season 26[/b] concluded and rewards distributed, a new set of [b]Crystal Weapons[/b] has been unlocked for crafting. Those who have earned the necessary Artifacts from [b]Conqueror’s Chests[/b] can now forge and wield the latest additions to this powerful and prestigious category, each offering unique battlefield potential and high-end tactical versatility.

Let’s take a closer look at what this trio of weapons brings to Albion’s battlegrounds:

[h3]Flamewalker Staff (Fire Staff)[/h3]
Spell: [b]Spontaneous Combustion[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67f3be6257861_720.mp4[/video]

This is fire magic with the heat cranked all the way up. [b]Spontaneous Combustion[/b] transforms you into a living fireball, letting you crash through enemy lines while immune to new spells, damage, and crowd control. Enemies you pass will be set ablaze, and if you land on an opposing player, the spell's cooldown partially resets, making it ideal for follow-ups or escapes. Perfect for bursting single targets, it also has potential in team fights, offering fire users a bold tool for breaking through frontline defenses.

[h3]Forgebark Staff (Nature Staff)[/h3]
Spell: [b]Dual Nature[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67f3be8395447_720.mp4[/video]

Who says healers can't lead the charge? [b]Dual Nature[/b] is a two-pronged spell, giving Nature Staff users the power to either anchor their team with Fortify – shielding and healing teammates while enhancing their own healing output – or flip the script with Ensnare to root enemies and boost your allies’ damage. The ability encourages fast decision-making and makes it possible to switch from support to disruption in the blink of an eye. A bold pick for healers who want to step up and shake up the frontline.

[h3]Arclight Blasters (Crossbow)[/h3]
Spell: [b]Flickershots[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67f3be514d589_720.mp4[/video]

[b]Flickershots[/b] brings the boom, the bounce, and the bolt spam. This ability sends you dashing a short distance while unleashing a barrage of energy bolts in a wide radius, damaging enemies and granting resistances mid-move. You can recast it up to three times, but each use increases its cooldown – so pick your moments carefully. Whether you’re peppering the enemy backline or executing a quick in-and-out, this is a spell that rewards calculated aggression.


This latest trio of Crystal Weapons brings fresh firepower to Albion’s elite battlefields. Designed for high-level PvP, each one offers a new way to outmaneuver, outplay, and outlast your opponents.

For those already looking ahead: the next batch of Crystal Weapons is set to arrive with Albion’s next major update. Until then, it’s time to take to the battlefield with fire, magic, and unrelenting force.

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 5
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch focuses on Guild Season content, introducing the next batch of Crystal Weapons and several balance changes to shake up the ZvZ meta ahead of the new season.[/i][/quote]
[h3]New Crystal Weapons[/h3]

This patch introduces three brand-new Crystal Weapons, craftable from Artifacts awarded in Conqueror’s Chests at the end of Season 26. Each Crystal Weapon has its own unique, powerful spell:[list]	[*][b]Flamewalker Staff[/b] (Fire Staff): [b]Spontaneous Combustion [/b]transforms you into a raging fireball, flying towards your enemies and dealing damage to those in your path[/*]	[*][b]Forgebark Staff [/b](Nature Staff): [b]Dual Nature[/b] allows you to switch between fortifying your allies and ensnaring your enemies[/*]	[*][b]Arclight Blasters[/b] (Crossbow): [b]Flickershots [/b]unleashes a barrage of energy bolts as you spin through the air, dealing damage and increasing your resistances[/*][/list]
[h3]Season 27 Changes[/h3]

The following categories in the Conqueror's Challenge have had their Might requirements per level reduced, while their Season Point output for each level has also been reduced to maintain overall Season Point payouts:

[b]Treasures[/b][list]	[*]Might needed per Level: 13,000 → 10,400	[list]		[*]Season Points per Level: 20 → 16[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Crystal Creatures[/b][list]	[*]Might needed per Level: 6,000 → 4,000	[list]		[*]Season Points per Level: 30 → 20[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Smugglers[/b][list]	[*]Might needed per Level: 34,000 → 27,200	[list]		[*]Season Points per Level: 20 → 16[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]Gathering has also had its Might requirement per level reduced, to make it easier for smaller guilds to earn Season Points from this activity:

[b]Gathering[/b][list]	[*]Might needed per Level: 3,500 → 2,700[/*][/list]
[h3]Other Changes[/h3][list]	[*]Smuggler Crates are now visible on the minimap to everyone in the same region[/*]	[*]Players can now send only one message every two seconds in the following chat channels:	[list]		[*]Say[/*]		[*]Whisper[/*]		[*]Help[/*]		[*]Faction[/*]		[*]Faction Local[/*]		[*]All language channels[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The following automated chat message has been changed:	[list]		[*]“Player x has committed suicide.” → “Player x has died.”[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Text entered in the Marketplace UI search box now carries over when switching between the Buy and Buy Order tabs[/*]	[*]The Kills and Deaths tabs in the Player Stats UI now remember the previous dropdown selection on opening[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Axes[/b]
[quote][i]Despite multiple nerfs, Infernal Scythe has continued to dominate as the ZvZ damage dealer of choice, crowding out alternatives. The damage of the second swing has been increased but converted into a DoT to disincentivize zergs from running five per party.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Bloody Reap (Infernal Scythe)	[list]		[*]2nd swing now deals damage in 3 ticks over 2 seconds (doesn’t stack)[/*]		[*]Damage per tick below 40%: 85 (total damage 220 → 255)[/*]		[*]Damage per tick above 40%: 47 (total damage 120 → 141)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Raging Blades has been a powerful component of axes’ domination in ZvZs, so its area has been reduced to limit its effectiveness in the largest fights.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Raging Blades (all Axes)	[list]		[*]Radius: 6m → 5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Crossbows[/b]
[quote][i]Energy Shaper has remained a niche pick in ZvZs. Its total channel duration has been reduced, while the damage per tick has been increased to make accurate beams deadlier in a shorter time.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Divine Engine (Energy Shaper)	[list]		[*]Channel duration: 3.3s → 2.6s (Total ticks 11 → 9)[/*]		[*]Damage per tick (vs players): 96 → 117[/*]		[*]Damage per tick (vs mobs): 57 → 70[/*]		[*]Initial tick: 0.2s → 0.1s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Daggers[/b]
[quote][i]Because Demonfang has been a menace in ZvZ, it has received multiple nerfs to damage and resilience penetration over previous patches. Some of that damage has now been restored.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Blood Ritual (Demonfang)	[list]		[*]Damage per cast: 106 → 112[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Due to the significant setup required for Ring of Death, its penalty for misexecution has been softened, giving Twin Slayer players more opportunities to land the one-shot.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ring of Death (Twin Slayers)	[list]		[*]1st cast cooldown: 25s → 15s[/*]		[*]Energy cost: 12 → 10[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Fire Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Raging Flare’s damage has been condensed and increased to provide Fire users with a quicker, more impactful long-range damage option.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Raging Flare (all Fire Staffs)	[list]		[*]Cast time: 0.6s → 0.4s[/*]		[*]Impact damage: 186 → 205[/*]		[*]DoT ticks: 6 → 3 (1s interval unchanged)[/*]		[*]DoT damage per tick: 7.2 → 21.4[/*]		[*]Total DoT damage: 43.2 → 64.2[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Frost Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Frost’s spell stack requirement has been reduced, as it felt too high on builds using less spammable abilities like Frozen Surge and Frost Nova. This will help Frost players keep enemies locked down more consistently.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Frost (all Frost Staffs)	[list]		[*]Stack requirement: 5 → 4[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Icicle Staff has remained a niche defensive tank option in ZvZs, but its dramatic hit delay has made it feel outdated in modern Albion, so this has been reduced to improve responsiveness.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Frozen Hell (Icicle Staff)	[list]		[*]Hit delay: 0.7s → 0.3s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Permafrost has been a strong ZvZ option, but its crowd control when stacked as an 8-man bomb squad has left too little room for reaction. With such a consistently valuable long-range stun, its damage has been reduced to compensate.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ice Crystal (Permafrost Prism)	[list]		[*]Damage: 184.69 → 173[/*]		[*]Stun duration now ignores diminishing returns (but does not apply it)[/*]		[*]Stun duration no longer refreshes by consecutive Ice Crystal stuns[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Hammers[/b]
[quote][i]Grovekeeper has fallen out of favor as both an engage and peel tank option. The bonus resistances for hitting targets have not felt impactful to Grovekeeper players, so they have been removed in favor of an instant knock-up, making engages more deadly, even against enemy cleanses.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ground Pound (Grovekeeper)	[list]		[*]Removed: Increased resistances per targets hit[/*]		[*]Added: Knocks up all targets for a duration based on the amount of enemies hit		[list]			[*]1, 2, or 3 enemies hit: 0.4s knock up[/*]			[*]4, 5 or 6 enemies hit: 0.8s knock up[/*]			[*]7 or more enemies hit: 1.2s knock up[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Holy Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]To help Exalted Staff feel more responsive and succeed in its intended role of clearing hostile ground areas, its long cast time has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Sanctify (Exalted Staff)	[list]		[*]Cast time: 1s → 0.6s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Maces[/b]
[quote][i]Dreadstorm Monarch has struggled to find a strong foothold in the meta. As a result, the value of Eye of the Storm’s uncleansable resistance reduction has been increased, to help it compete with alternative pierce options.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Eye of the Storm (Dreadstorm Monarch)	[list]		[*]Resistance reduction: 0.15 → 0.18[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Vendetta’s pull hit delay has felt overly generous to opponents, so it has been shortened to help Camlann compete with other clump tank options.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Vendetta (Camlann Mace)	[list]		[*]Hit delay: 1.5s → 1.2s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Nature Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Protection of Nature has been a strong defensive tool with a very high uptime. Its high damage reduction, paired with the bonus healing received, has resulted in targets having too much survivability too often in smaller-scale group fights, so its resistance has been reduced somewhat.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Protection of Nature (all Nature Staffs)	[list]		[*]Resistance: 0.24 → 0.2[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Quarterstaffs[/b]
[quote][i]To help Fatal Blades counter fast ZvZ engages, its damage reduction now stacks higher and faster, but with reduced duration.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Fatal Blade (Black Monk Stave)	[list]		[*]Damage reduction (vs. players): 22% → 30%[/*]		[*]Duration: 6s → 5s[/*]		[*]Initial tick: 0.25s → 0.1s[/*]		[*]Projectile speed: 30 m/s → 35 m/s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Soul Shaker has fallen out of favor as a viable defensive tank option in ZvZs. To help players better protect their team’s flanks, its root duration has been increased to match its area duration.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Soul Shaker (Grailseeker)	[list]		[*]Area duration: 4s → 3.5s[/*]		[*]Root duration: 3s → 3.5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Soulscythe has remained a niche shotcaller option in ZvZs, so its standtime has been reduced to make it feel more responsive and return control to its users more quickly.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Tornado (Soulscythe)	[list]		[*]Standtime: 0.7s → 0.4s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Spears[/b]
[quote][i]While Cripple has been a good tool to counter swords, adjustments have been made to help it feel powerful in more situations, more often.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Cripple (all Spears)	[list]		[*]Damage type: magical → physical[/*]		[*]Added: Auto-attack speed is reduced by 25% for 4s[/*]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 18s[/*]		[*]Move speed buff duration: 5s → 4s[/*]		[*]No longer gives bonus damage when purging a sprint[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b]
[quote][i]The previous buff to Blade Cyclone has been reverted, as it became the default option and outperformed all other options, particularly for Carving and Infinity Blade players.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Blade Cyclone (all Swords)	[list]		[*]1 charge damage: 70 → 60[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]War Gloves[/b]
[quote][i]To help Ursine Maulers find more success, the damage reduction from a previous nerf, originally paired with a significant resilience penetration decrease, has been reverted.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Hundred Striking Fists (Ursine Maulers)	[list]		[*]Damage per tick: 32.4 → 36 (vs players)[/*]		[*]Delayed damage: 27 → 30 (per stack)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Some of Infernal Boulder’s instant damage has been moved into its DoT component, to both reward skilled players for hitting all three boulders and to limit its effectiveness when stacked in ZvZs.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Infernal Boulder (Hellfire Hands)	[list]		[*]1st boulder damage: 199.5 → 177[/*]		[*]2nd boulder damage: 133 → 126[/*]		[*]3rd boulder damage: 66.5 → 76[/*]		[*]DoT tick damage: 14 → 18[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Armors[/b]
[quote][i]To make Protection of the Fiends more risky, its negative resistance penalty has been increased, making it more important to combo with allies or cancel the channel early.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Protection of the Fiends (Demon Armor)	[list]		[*]Caster resistance reduction: 0.34 → 0.37[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Taunt has been simplified to apply the same effects regardless of the selected target, while increasing its value as a short-cooldown damage option for Plate Armor users.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Taunt (all Plate Armors)	[list]		[*]No longer distinguishes between target types[/*]		[*]Bonus Damage vs All: 10% → 20%[/*]		[*]Defense vs Players: -10% → -20%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Capes[/b]
[quote][i]The Fort Sterling Cape has had its cooldown significantly reduced at higher tiers to justify its price increase and enable players to rely on it as a consistent cleanse option.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Untouchable (Fort Sterling Cape)	[list]		[*]Base cooldown: 139 → 168[/*]		[*]Cooldown reduction per 100 IP: 3s → 8s (118s → 112s at 700 IP, 91s → 40s at 1600 IP)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Potions[/b]
[quote][i]Invisibility Potion’s damage reduction has not been significant enough or lasted long enough to give opponents a fair chance to react to fully undetectable engages. Damage reduction has now been changed to reduce all damage dealt by players, making it harder to bypass the penalty with stacked damage buffs. The effect also lingers for 2 seconds after exiting stealth, rather than starting from the moment of use, giving players a chance to fight back if revealed early.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Invisibility Potion	[list]		[*]Ability damage reduction → Damage vs All reduction (-50% value is unchanged)[/*]		[*]Duration: Fixed time on cast → While Invisible, and remaining for 2s once revealed[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Other[/b][list]	[*]Judgment (Lightcaller) visuals have been updated to be more readable in large-scale fights[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Spell Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Spinning Blades (Dual Swords): Fixed issue where immunity to Crowd Control persisted after impact[/*]	[*]Holy Beam (Holy Staffs): Fixed issue where stacks persisted after casting was interrupted[/*]	[*]Razor Cut (Bear Paws): Fixed issue where the same enemy could be hit multiple times[/*]	[*]Time Freeze (Great Arcane Staffs): Fixed issue where frozen enemies could still receive healing from lifesteal effects[/*][/list]
[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where the Arena queue timer would not reappear if a player canceled the match invitation[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where combat logs in the Death Recap would be overwritten by new actions performed on the player when switching tabs in the UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the ‘Take All’ button on the Marketplace would reset filters without resetting the filter text	[list]		[*]The text is now reset along with the filters[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][MOBILE] Fixed issue where main dynamic action button on the virtual controller could appear to remain in motion after use[/*]	[*][CONTROLLER] Fixed issue where ‘Select Next Party Member’ keybinding option was missing from the Settings menu[/*][/list]
[b]Other Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed Faction Warfare “connection bug”; it is now always possible to capture Outposts in a region if at least one adjacent frontline or backline region is owned by your Faction[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where it was possible for players to buy their own items at the Marketplace[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Rock Giant’s Aspect would not pursue players or use melee attacks[/*][/list]

		[*]2nd swing now deals damage in 3 ticks over 2 seconds (doesn’t stack)
		[*]Damage per tick below 40%: 85 (total damage 220 → 255)
		[*]Damage per tick above 40%: 47 (total damage 120 → 141)
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Raging Blades has been a powerful component of axes’ domination in ZvZs, so its area has been reduced to limit its effectiveness in the largest fights.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Raging Blades (all Axes)
	[list]
		[*]Radius: 6m → 5m
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Crossbows[/b]
[quote][i]Energy Shaper has remained a niche pick in ZvZs. Its total channel duration has been reduced, while the damage per tick has been increased to make accurate beams deadlier in a shorter time.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Divine Engine (Energy Shaper)
	[list]
		[*]Channel duration: 3.3s → 2.6s (Total ticks 11 → 9)
		[*]Damage per tick (vs players): 96 → 117
		[*]Damage per tick (vs mobs): 57 → 70
		[*]Initial tick: 0.2s → 0.1s
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Daggers[/b]
[quote][i]Because Demonfang has been a menace in ZvZ, it has received multiple nerfs to damage and resilience penetration over previous patches. Some of that damage has now been restored.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Blood Ritual (Demonfang)
	[list]
		[*]Damage per cast: 106 → 112
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Due to the significant setup required for Ring of Death, its penalty for misexecution has been softened, giving Twin Slayer players more opportunities to land the one-shot.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Ring of Death (Twin Slayers)
	[list]
		[*]1st cast cooldown: 25s → 15s
		[*]Energy cost: 12 → 10
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Fire Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Raging Flare’s damage has been condensed and increased to provide Fire users with a quicker, more impactful long-range damage option.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Raging Flare (all Fire Staffs)
	[list]
		[*]Cast time: 0.6s → 0.4s
		[*]Impact damage: 186 → 205
		[*]DoT ticks: 6 → 3 (1s interval unchanged)
		[*]DoT damage per tick: 7.2 → 21.4
		[*]Total DoT damage: 43.2 → 64.2
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Frost Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Frost’s spell stack requirement has been reduced, as it felt too high on builds using less spammable abilities like Frozen Surge and Frost Nova. This will help Frost players keep enemies locked down more consistently.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Frost (all Frost Staffs)
	[list]
		[*]Stack requirement: 5 → 4
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Icicle Staff has remained a niche defensive tank option in ZvZs, but its dramatic hit delay has made it feel outdated in modern Albion, so this has been reduced to improve responsiveness.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Frozen Hell (Icicle Staff)
	[list]
		[*]Hit delay: 0.7s → 0.3s
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Permafrost has been a strong ZvZ option, but its crowd control when stacked as an 8-man bomb squad has left too little room for reaction. With such a consistently valuable long-range stun, its damage has been reduced to compensate.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Ice Crystal (Permafrost Prism)
	[list]
		[*]Damage: 184.69 → 173
		[*]Stun duration now ignores diminishing returns (but does not apply it)
		[*]Stun duration no longer refreshes by consecutive Ice Crystal stuns
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Hammers[/b]
[quote][i]Grovekeeper has fallen out of favor as both an engage and peel tank option. The bonus resistances for hitting targets have not felt impactful to Grovekeeper players, so they have been removed in favor of an instant knock-up, making engages more deadly, even against enemy cleanses.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Ground Pound (Grovekeeper)
	[list]
		[*]Removed: Increased resistances per targets hit
		[*]Added: Knocks up all targets for a duration based on the amount of enemies hit
		[list]
			[*]1, 2, or 3 enemies hit: 0.4s knock up
			[*]4, 5 or 6 enemies hit: 0.8s knock up
			[*]7 or more enemies hit: 1.2s knock up
		[/list]
		[*] 
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Holy Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]To help Exalted Staff feel more responsive and succeed in its intended role of clearing hostile ground areas, its long cast time has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Sanctify (Exalted Staff)
	[list]
		[*]Cast time: 1s → 0.6s
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Maces[/b]
[quote][i]Dreadstorm Monarch has struggled to find a strong foothold in the meta. As a result, the value of Eye of the Storm’s uncleansable resistance reduction has been increased, to help it compete with alternative pierce options.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Eye of the Storm (Dreadstorm Monarch)
	[list]
		[*]Resistance reduction: 0.15 → 0.18
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Vendetta’s pull hit delay has felt overly generous to opponents, so it has been shortened to help Camlann compete with other clump tank options.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Vendetta (Camlann Mace)
	[list]
		[*]Hit delay: 1.5s → 1.2s
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Nature Staffs[/b]
[quote][i]Protection of Nature has been a strong defensive tool with a very high uptime. Its high damage reduction, paired with the bonus healing received, has resulted in targets having too much survivability too often in smaller-scale group fights, so its resistance has been reduced somewhat.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Protection of Nature (all Nature Staffs)
	[list]
		[*]Resistance: 0.24 → 0.2
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Quarterstaffs[/b]
[quote][i]To help Fatal Blades counter fast ZvZ engages, its damage reduction now stacks higher and faster, but with reduced duration.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Fatal Blade (Black Monk Stave)
	[list]
		[*]Damage reduction (vs. players): 22% → 30%
		[*]Duration: 6s → 5s
		[*]Initial tick: 0.25s → 0.1s
		[*]Projectile speed: 30 m/s → 35 m/s
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Soul Shaker has fallen out of favor as a viable defensive tank option in ZvZs. To help players better protect their team’s flanks, its root duration has been increased to match its area duration.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Soul Shaker (Grailseeker)
	[list]
		[*]Area duration: 4s → 3.5s
		[*]Root duration: 3s → 3.5s
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Soulscythe has remained a niche shotcaller option in ZvZs, so its standtime has been reduced to make it feel more responsive and return control to its users more quickly.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Tornado (Soulscythe)
	[list]
		[*]Standtime: 0.7s → 0.4s
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Spears[/b]
[quote][i]While Cripple has been a good tool to counter swords, adjustments have been made to help it feel powerful in more situations, more often.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Cripple (all Spears)
	[list]
		[*]Damage type: magical → physical
		[*]Added: Auto-attack speed is reduced by 25% for 4s
		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 18s
		[*]Move speed buff duration: 5s → 4s
		[*]No longer gives bonus damage when purging a sprint
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Swords[/b]
[quote][i]The previous buff to Blade Cyclone has been reverted, as it became the default option and outperformed all other options, particularly for Carving and Infinity Blade players.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Blade Cyclone (all Swords)
	[list]
		[*]1 charge damage: 70 → 60
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]War Gloves[/b]
[quote][i]To help Ursine Maulers find more success, the damage reduction from a previous nerf, originally paired with a significant resilience penetration decrease, has been reverted.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Hundred Striking Fists (Ursine Maulers)
	[list]
		[*]Damage per tick: 32.4 → 36 (vs players)
		[*]Delayed damage: 27 → 30 (per stack)
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Some of Infernal Boulder’s instant damage has been moved into its DoT component, to both reward skilled players for hitting all three boulders and to limit its effectiveness when stacked in ZvZs.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Infernal Boulder (Hellfire Hands)
	[list]
		[*]1st boulder damage: 199.5 → 177
		[*]2nd boulder damage: 133 → 126
		[*]3rd boulder damage: 66.5 → 76
		[*]DoT tick damage: 14 → 18
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Armors[/b]
[quote][i]To make Protection of the Fiends more risky, its negative resistance penalty has been increased, making it more important to combo with allies or cancel the channel early.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Protection of the Fiends (Demon Armor)
	[list]
		[*]Caster resistance reduction: 0.34 → 0.37
	[/list]
	[*]

[quote][i]Taunt has been simplified to apply the same effects regardless of the selected target, while increasing its value as a short-cooldown damage option for Plate Armor users.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Taunt (all Plate Armors)
	[list]
		[*]No longer distinguishes between target types
		[*]Bonus Damage vs All: 10% → 20%
		[*]Defense vs Players: -10% → -20%
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Capes[/b]
[quote][i]The Fort Sterling Cape has had its cooldown significantly reduced at higher tiers to justify its price increase and enable players to rely on it as a consistent cleanse option.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Untouchable (Fort Sterling Cape)
	[list]
		[*]Base cooldown: 139 → 168
		[*]Cooldown reduction per 100 IP: 3s → 8s (118s → 112s at 700 IP, 91s → 40s at 1600 IP)
	[/list]
	[*]

[b]Potions[/b]
[quote][i]Invisibility Potion’s damage reduction has not been significant enough or lasted long enough to give opponents a fair chance to react to fully undetectable engages. Damage reduction has now been changed to reduce all damage dealt by players, making it harder to bypass the penalty with stacked damage buffs. The effect also lingers for 2 seconds after exiting stealth, rather than starting from the moment of use, giving players a chance to fight back if revealed early.[/i][/quote][list]
	[*]Invisibility Potion
	[list]
		[*]Ability damage reduction → Damage vs All reduction (-50% value is unchanged)
		[*]Duration: Fixed time on cast → While Invisible, and remaining for 2s once revealed
	[/list]
	[*]

notes.title: Track Your Prey in the Hunter Challenge!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/51b0902b256574216a78cbabebb9ecc6d70f3238.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Hunter Challenge[/b] calls all master predators to the wilds for the ultimate test! Prove your skill, and you’ll be rewarded with the [b]Black Panther[/b], a formidable beast that boasts a powerful burst of speed, propelling its rider across vast distances in a heartbeat – [i]silent[/i], [i]swift[/i], and [i]relentless[/i]. Earn [b]Challenge Points[/b], claim your prize, and show the world you’re the apex predator!

[h3]Hunt Down Fantastic Items[/h3]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/65c7ebd0bcfd8882b852c1c9ac87eaa7c6954b21.png[/img]
[b]BLACK PANTHER:[/b] This month's Challenge sees the return of the mighty [b]Black Panther[/b], a sleek feline mount with a fearsome appearance. It boasts a powerful [b]speed boost[/b] spell that can propel its rider across large distances – helping both hunters and hunted alike.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/66c0235463c49befe79f1a8d85cc5c2f4f67d56c.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Reach your goals to unlock the [b]Hunter Challenge avatar ring[/b] to give your favorite avatar a hunting-themed border. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded for one [b]Adventurer's Token[/b] at the Vanity Merchant.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/343bde109e559187dfdfa642750988366c00824b.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Hunter Challenge chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver bags, and rare resources, this month's chests contain various [b]hunting-themed statues and furniture items[/b].

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67d9809849357_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!
