notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 4
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch improves the Conqueror's Challenge reward system with better tracking and reward claiming for past seasons. It also includes combat balance changes, bug fixes, and gameplay improvements.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Changes[/h3]

[b]Conqueror’s Challenge Changes[/b]

A new Conqueror’s Challenge History Tab has been added, allowing players to track their past seasons and claim rewards more easily.[list]	[*]Players can now view their stats and rewards from previous seasons by selecting them from a dropdown menu[/*][/list]Within this new tab, rewards can be claimed through an improved UI:[list]	[*]Conqueror’s Chest rewards now appear as a list of claimable items instead of a single chest	[list]		[*]Players can claim items individually or use ‘Claim All’ to collect as much as their inventory space allows[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Knight’s Vows and Avatars are sent directly to the inventory when claimed[/*][/list]
[b]Other Changes[/b][list]	[*]Personal and Guild tabs within a Guild Bank are now visually distinguished[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Frost Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]To increase the consistency of Arctic Volley, each icicle has been adjusted to slow all targets hit, making it easier to land multiple volleys.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Arctic Volley (Arctic Staff)	[list]		[*]Slow per hit: 10% for 1s (stacks up to 6 times)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Holy Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]As Holy Staff has been a dominant option in the 2v2 meta, the energy cost of Desperate Prayer has been increased to make energy denial a possible counter.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Desperate Prayer (Holy Staff)	[list]		[*]Energy cost: 12 → 15[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Nature Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Since Druidic Staff has fallen out of the meta following previous nerfs, the additional cooldown for recasting Spiritual Seed has now been removed to increase its healing output in group play.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Spiritual Seed (Druidic Staff)	[list]		[*]Recast cooldown: 25s → 20s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shapeshifter Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Bloodmoon continues to be a problem for larger groups to deal with. To give enemies a better chance at bursting a Werewolf down, their max health while transformed has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Werewolf Transformation (Bloodmoon Staff)	[list]		[*]Transformation health: 1100 → 1000[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b]

[quote][i]Infinity Blade’s popularity has increased since Limit Breaker stopped consuming its damage buff. To reduce its brawling power somewhat, its long buff duration has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Limitbreaker (Infinity Blade)	[list]		[*]Damage buff duration: 7s → 5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Helmets[/b]

[quote][i]Smokebomb has been adjusted to no longer silence party members, as this behavior was difficult to control and led to frustrating gameplay experiences.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Smokebomb (Hellion Hood)	[list]		[*]No longer silences group members[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shoes[/b]

[quote][i]The stun duration for Crush Charge – a highly telegraphed ability – has been increased to make it more rewarding, especially since it takes the place of a traditional mobility option.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Crush Charge (Duskweaver Boots)	[list]		[*]Stun: 2.35s → 2.5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Capes[/b]

[quote][i]Capes that primarily scale their cooldowns with Item Power have not provided enough value to warrant their increasing cost per tier. With significantly shorter cooldowns at higher tiers, these capes can now become a more reliable build component.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Berserk (Keeper Cape)	[list]		[*]Base cooldown: 112.5 → 150[/*]		[*]Cooldown reduction: 2.5s → 7.5s (95s → 98s at 700 IP, 73s → 30s at 1600 IP)[/*]		[*]Buff duration: 6s → 5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Devious Trap (Heretic Cape)	[list]		[*]Base cooldown: 112.5 → 150[/*]		[*]Cooldown reduction: 2.5s → 7s (95s → 101s at 700 IP, 73s → 38s at 1600 IP)[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Mark of the Raven (Morgana Cape)	[list]		[*]Cooldown reduction: 3.1s → 6s (98s → 78s at 700 IP, 70s → 24s at 1600 IP)[/*]		[*]Buff duration: 8s → 5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Miscellaneous[/b][list]	[*]Hellgates	[list]		[*]Rising Lava stacks now persist after being knocked down while inside the lava[/*]		[*]Rising Lava stacks now break shields and cause immunity against shield effects[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Spell Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Enfeeble Blades (Lifecurse Staff)	[list]		[*]Fixed issue where enemies would continue having their buffs purged shortly after leaving the target area[/*]		[*]Fixed issue where enemies could become invisible within the target area[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Holy Beam (Holy Staffs), Hover (Sandals of Purity), and Levitate (Cultist Robes) could have their channeled effects purged[/*][/list]
[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where removing an item from either the Main Hand or Off-Hand slot in the Loadouts menu would clear both slots[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Tracking Toolkits could be placed in the weapon slot when creating a Loadout[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the Overcharge confirmation pop-up could appear twice when using a hotkey[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Crystal Weapon combat and crafting specializations on the Destiny Board displayed incorrect bonus values[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the item icon in the furniture UI was selectable but not clickable with a controller	[list]		[*]The icon is now clickable across all inputs to open the furniture item's details UI[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Other Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where the following mobs would deal significantly higher damage than intended:	[list]		[*]Earthkeeper Shaman[/*]		[*]Avalonian High Priestess[/*]		[*]Sir Bedivere[/*]		[*]Castle Mortar[/*]		[*]Champion of Fort Sterling[/*]		[*]Bandit Ringleader[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where items that cannot drop as loot could be listed for sale on the Black Market[/*]	[*]Various additional graphical, animation, terrain, audio, UI, and localization fixes[/*][/list]

As [b]Season 26[/b] enters its final stretch, the next battle for supremacy is already in sight! The [b]shorter season format[/b] has kept the action fast and relentless, and [b]Season 27[/b] promises another intense two-month race to the top.

notes.title: 7 Dumb Ways to Lose Your Account
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b616c2dc171b42c1d436b9db5cdcf932b6f0af3a.jpeg[/img]

You’ve spent countless hours surviving ganks, hoarding loot, and maybe even winning a fight or two. But what if you wanted to throw it all away?

Lucky for you, there are plenty of dumb ways to do just that! Some are instant, some take effort, but they all end the same way – with you staring at the login screen, wondering what went wrong. We know you’d [i]never[/i] fall for these… but let’s take a look at[b] what not to do[/b], just for fun.

[h3]1. Download Mystery Software (Enjoy the Free Malware!)[/h3]
You just wanted a harmless little mod, maybe some fun sound effects, or a purely academic armor removal mod for "historical accuracy". But oops! That “totally safe” download came with surprise perks like a free keylogger that sends your login info straight to a scammer, and a bonus backdoor for hackers to snoop around your PC. Want to stay safe? [b]Stick to trusted sources[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/deb3cdb804dd0323f443e3e8e5c106b86a537633.png[/img]

[h3]2. Take the Phishing Bait Like a Champ[/h3]
"300m Silver giveaway in 15 mins! Just log in [i]here [/i]with your Albion account!" – sounds great, right? Except that you’ve just given your credentials to [i]xxDarkScammer420xx[/i], who’s now flipping your hard-earned loot for pennies. Pro tip: Use [b]unique passwords[/b], and[b] only use your Albion account to log into the game client or albiononline.com[/b]. Not that hard.

[h3]3. Trust That “Totally Legit” Currency Seller[/h3]
You found a site offering Silver or items at suspiciously good prices? That’s because it’s a suspiciously fantastic way to spend [i]real money[/i] on getting your account banned. And guess what? That deal comes from stolen accounts and credit cards, so when you buy, you're not just fueling the phishing market – you’re swimming in digital dirty money. That’s like 9000+ points of [i]bad karma[/i]. Here’s an idea for getting currency: [b]play the game[/b],[b] trade with other players[/b], or, you know,[b] use the official shop[/b] – the one that doesn’t come with a lifetime ban.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/862248537c4b61e2d0e03d8dbf3f36fc05a44e6c.png[/img]

[h3]4. Let a Bot Do the Work for You[/h3]
A little automation can’t hurt, right? So you find an easy way to "help" yourself – be it a bot or a simple macro you program by hand. Except Albion isn’t one of those idle games where you level up without ever learning how to play. Here, actions matter, and we’ll notice if your character’s been chopping trees in the same spot for two weeks like an overachieving ghost. And when that happens, we’ll assume your account has left the need for a player behind. So unless you want your progress to vanish faster than a rat stealing a kill, maybe – just maybe – [b]click your own buttons?[/b]
[h3]5. Find Creative Ways to Cheat[/h3]
We get it, you want all the glory and none of the hassle of actually having to be good at it. Maybe you tweak a few files, maybe you install that fancy radar tool. What could possibly go wrong? Oh, just the minor inconvenience of your "advantage" lasting a glorious five seconds before the ban hammer swings and your account gets [i]yeeted[/i] into the void harder than a bunny in the middle of a ZvZ. If you really want to win, [b]refine your strategy[/b], [b]practice more[/b], or – here’s a wild idea –[b] [i]git gud[/i][/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/42878aad276547afb683c267213bff8c15f52fce.png[/img]

[h3]6. Use Your Alt Account for Sneaky Scouting[/h3]
Wow, look at you! No need to download shady software – you’ve devised your own "brilliant" strategy. Running two accounts at once? Surely that’s just efficient gaming, right? Except now, instead of having an advantage, you get to stare at not one, but [i]two[/i] "BANNED!" messages on your login screen. So before you go recruiting yourself as your own personal spy, just [b]stick to teammates[/b],[b] legit scouting tactics[/b], and keeping at least one account you can log into.

[h3]7. Exploit Bugs Like There’s No Tomorrow[/h3]
You’re minding your own business when – [i]bam![/i] – you stumble upon a glitch that spits out infinite loot. Jackpot! Or so you tell yourself, rubbing your hands together like a cartoon villain. Except… we have logs. We [i]always[/i] have logs. So now the real decision: do you [b]report it like the unsung hero of bug reporting that you are[/b], basking in the glory of keeping the game fair for everyone, or do you go down in history as the person who got banned for trying to hoard virtual carrots?

In conclusion, maybe just don’t? [b]Be smart, stay safe, and play fair![/b]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a9c9a7cce225234482e0a0104ab0dcf03d193159.png[/img]

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 3
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch brings important refinements and bug fixes but primarily focuses on combat balance changes.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Changes[/h3]

[b]Destiny Board Changes[/b][list]	[*]The Reaver line bonus has been reworked to prevent unintended interactions with spells and other effects	[list]		[*]Bonus defense/damage vs mobs should now work as intended for higher-tier enemies[/*]		[*]Armor and magic resistance reduction effects are now more effective against higher-tier enemies[/*]		[*]Aside from these interactions, there should be no noticeable difference when fighting mobs[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Corrupted and Solo Randomized Dungeon Changes[/b]

[quote][i]With the introduction of the Gold Market Stabilization system, Common Chests that typically dropped a single Bag of Silver could sometimes be empty. To prevent this without altering the stabilization system, we have moved Silver from Common Chests to higher-value chests, and replaced them with Tomes of Insight to ensure a guaranteed reward.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Common Chests now drop Beginner’s Tomes of Insight instead of Bags of Silver[/*]	[*]Uncommon, Rare, and Legendary Chests now contain more Bags of Silver          [/*][/list]
[b]UI Changes[/b][list]	[*]To standardize Cast Time and Cooldown Rate modification values, they now always display a positive value to indicate longer durations and a negative value to indicate reductions	[list]		[*]The item stat 'Cast Time Reduction' has been renamed to 'Cast Time' to align with this system[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Reduced chat frequency for /HCE, /LFG, /TR, and /REC by increasing message cooldown from 30 seconds to 2 minutes[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Arcane Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Evensong has offered powerful offensive utility but is almost always used with plate armor. Its base damage has been increased to help players who want to lean more into being a DPS threat.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Dark Sphere (Evensong)	[list]		[*]Damage: 100 → 112[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Axes[/b]

[quote][i]Axe players in ZvZs have been overperforming, frequently hitting more than 10 enemies. To address this, the damage and complexity of Raging Blades have been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Raging Blades (all Axes)	[list]		[*]Removed: Targets within 2 meters take no damage[/*]		[*]Damage per tick: 26 → 22[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Hammers[/b]

[quote][i]Giant Steps has been far from its previously overwhelming state. A portion of its slowing aura has been restored to reinforce Forge Hammers as a tanky disruptor.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Giant Steps (Forge Hammers)	[list]		[*]Slow: 20% → 35%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Holy Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Great Holy Staff has been underperforming, so part of its resistance increase has been restored.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Holy Explosion (Great Holy Staff)	[list]		[*]Resistance increase: 0.12 → 0.16[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]To give Lifetouch Staff a unique role, Holy Touch’s target is now immune to Crowd Control for the channel's duration (unless self-targeting). In addition, its range has been increased to improve its reliability in modern Albion.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Holy Touch (Lifetouch Staff)	[list]		[*]Added: Target is immune to all crowd-control (unless self-targeting)[/*]		[*]Range: 6m → 9m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Spears[/b]

[quote][i]Fling has struggled to find success. To improve its effectiveness, its stand time and cooldown have been reduced, making it easier to confirm an Impaler hit.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Fling (Glaive)	[list]		[*]Standtime: 0.85s → 0.6s[/*]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 18s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b]

[quote][i]Swords already have strong chase potential due to their passive movement speed bonuses. To balance this, Heroic Strike’s above-average range has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Heroic Strike (all Swords)	[list]		[*]Range: 4m → 3.5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]War Gloves[/b]

[quote][i]Fleet Footwork has provided War Gloves users with a solid mobility option while also serving as an exceptional DPS tool. Its damage output has been reduced to bring it more in line with alternatives.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Fleet Footwork (all War Gloves)	[list]		[*]Auto-attack damage buff: 150% → 125%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Armors[/b]

[quote][i]Ambush has remained a top-tier damage boost while also offering great defensive capabilities. Its maximum damage bonus has been reduced to allow other aggressive chest armors to be more competitive.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ambush (Assassin Jacket)	[list]		[*]Damage buff per stack: 4% → 5%[/*]		[*]Max buff stacks: 10 → 6 (max damage bonus 40% → 30%)[/*]		[*]Stack rate: 0.5s → 1s (time to max stacks: unchanged)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shoes[/b]

[quote][i]A few underused shoe abilities with restrictive conditions and mobility trade-offs have been improved. [/i][/quote][quote][i]Giant’s cooldown and uptime have been adjusted to make Guardian Boots a more available defensive option.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Giant (Guardian Boots)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 60s → 40s[/*]		[*]Duration: 8s → 6s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Mark of Sacrifice, Shield Charge, and Swift Cut have been standardized to a 15m range with below-average cooldowns, as their target requirements have been too limiting.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Mark of Sacrifice (Hellion Shoes)	[list]		[*]Range: 12m → 15m[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Shield Charge (Knight Boots)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 18s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Swift Cut (Assassin Shoes)	[list]		[*]Range: 11m → 15m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Spell Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Holy Beam (Holy Staffs) no longer adds a spell effect icon to the target’s buff bar[/*]	[*]Hamstring (Swords): Fixed issue where the tooltip displayed an incorrect cooldown[/*]	[*]Ambush (Assassin Jacket): The damage buff can now be purged and no longer persists if the caster does not deal damage within the first 7 seconds[/*][/list]
[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where icons on the Region Map could duplicate over time[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where some tooltips would remain visible and follow the cursor[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Medium Treasure Chests were not visible on the map for players in a neighboring region[/*][/list]
[b]Other Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where Elite Cursed Harvester did not count towards the Albion Journal mission ‘Defeat any Reaper or Harvester’[/*]	[*]Various additional graphical, animation, terrain, audio, UI, and localization fixes[/*][/list]

notes.title: Embrace the Wild in the Keeper Challenge!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9fade3d422c0bb7bdfc7f574d635d1be092368ac.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Keeper Challenge[/b] has begun, and deep in Albion’s wilds, the mighty [b]Grizzly Bear[/b] awakens from its long winter slumber. A symbol of raw strength and primal wisdom, this formidable beast stands unshaken in battle, its mere presence enough to make foes falter. Honor the Keepers' bond with nature, earn [b]Challenge Points[/b], and claim this guardian of the forest before it retreats into hibernation once more!

[h3]Timeless Treasures are Yours to Claim[/h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1ccea52c14db951c087f75c496b24b9167bff943.png[/img]
[b]GRIZZLY BEAR:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the popular [b]Grizzly Bear[/b], a huge, intimidating mount with an arsenal of powerful spells. In addition to its Intimidating Aura toggle spell, it also gains a temporary [b]speed boost[/b] when attacked, giving its rider an edge when enemies are in pursuit.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0982b57fc7c3a7bae9ab2319c7a4167acd5242d9.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Reach your goals to unlock the [b]Keeper Challenge avatar ring[/b], which gives your chosen avatar the stone-and-leather look of Albion's true guardians. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded for one [b]Adventurer's Token[/b] at the Vanity Merchant.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f3133179480d81f62910c49a583f47e255fbad23.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Keeper Challenge chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver bags, and rare resources, this month's chests contain various [b]Keeper-themed furniture and capes[/b].

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67b3252382013_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Development Update Feb 2025
notes.content:
The [b]Rogue Frontier[/b] update launched in early February, and it’s made Albion’s open world busier than ever, with players diving into Smuggler’s Dens and planting their Kill Trophies all over the world. In this new Dev Talk, Head of Production [b]Moritz Bokelmann[/b] looks at the impact of that update and offers a taste of what we’re cooking up for you next.

[previewyoutube=9YDq8y3U5xs?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Rogue Frontier[/h3]
The Rogue Frontier update has so far been a success, and activity levels are looking good.
[list]	[*]The [b]Bank Overview[/b], [b]Personal Island Chests[/b], and [b]Kill Trophies[/b] have all been very popular[/*]	[*][b]Smuggler’s Dens[/b] and [b]Smuggler’s Activities[/b] have made the Outlands more lively than ever[/*]	[*]Solo players and all sizes of groups are thriving in the [b]open world[/b][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/16fbe461a7ef4ff8e855aeecea195fdec138cca9.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Albion’s Next Update[/h3]
Work is underway on the next major game update, which will focus on instanced PvP and the new player experience.

[b]Instanced PvP Content[/b]
[list]	[*]The next update will address community concerns with [b]Corrupted Dungeons [/b]and [b]Hellgates[/b]	[list]		[*]Additionally, these will be made directly [b]accessible from major cities[/b][/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]A [b]new PvP dungeon[/b] aimed at 2-3 player groups will be introduced	[list]		[*]This is inspired by Knightfall Abbey, but with fewer exits, deeper levels, and greater consequences[/*]		[*]Players can weigh up whether to escape with their loot, or dive deeper for more rewards[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1d06279be159d411d7848b5b951b95f9472d13a5.jpeg][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6bd1715d7c1c8c105dd88f24a2fc721e43fe6ed8.jpeg[/img][/url]

[b]Early Game Improvements[/b]
[list]	[*]The next update also aims to help [b]new players[/b] once they’ve finished the tutorial[/*]	[*]A new, dedicated [b]Albion Journal[/b] category will offer structured milestones	[list]		[*]These start simple, and gradually encourage self-sufficiency[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]There will be additional improvements aimed to help [b]early-to-mid level players[/b][/*][/list]The new update will also, of course, bring additional quality-of-life and gameplay improvements, and a new batch of Crystal Weapons.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0f0e4fb9f65b9d4990681ce890db0db85cce1d99.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Looking Further Ahead[/h3]
Beyond the next update, we want to continue improving [b]Royal Continent[/b] gameplay for early-to-mid level players. One particular area of focus will be [b]Faction Warfare[/b]. Faction Warfare is an important and popular feature, but several issues need to be addressed, for instance:
[list]	[*]High repair costs[/*]	[*]Difficulty finding consistent action[/*]	[*]Lack of variety in objectives[/*][/list]We’re currently working on addressing these problems, as well as finding ways to make Faction Warfare activities more rewarding and engaging for everyone.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1c88917cf3eea7781919b0efb3fcc990133f102f.jpeg[/img]

We’ll also have had a few [b]Guild Seasons [/b]with the new, shorter format by then, and we’ll want to take another look at them – in particular to make them more attractive to mid-range guilds, while offering new goals for high-level guilds. We’re eager to hear your suggestions for improvements here and for other parts of the game, so if you have any ideas, let us know by [b]commenting on the video above[/b]!

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 2
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch adds further polish to the Rogue Frontier update, along with several combat balance changes and additional fixes.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Season Winner Statues Added[/h3]

The statues to honor the winners of Season 25 are now viewable in each servers’ Conqueror’s Hall. Congratulations to the triumphant guilds – PIVAS, Upper Class, and Take Care!

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]	[*]Portal Towns can now be set as Home	[list]		[*]Players now receive a warning when leaving a Portal Town for the Outlands if the Homesick debuff will be triggered[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The cooldown on Hideout Headquarters Boosters has been reduced from 90 days to 60 days, reflecting the new, shorter Guild Season duration	[list]		[*]Guilds which have already used their Booster this season will find its current cooldown also reduced by 30 days after this patch[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Smuggler Coins no longer leave trash when destroyed[/*]	[*]Trash once again has a 100% destruction rate when killed or ejected from the Roads of Avalon (as was the case before the release of Rogue Frontier)[/*]	[*]Added new Albion Journal missions for Kill Trophies in the Social & Guild category, under the Player Interactions subcategory[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Arcane Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Astral Staff had been too powerful in group fights, so Starfall’s damage output has been reduced to bring it more in line with other AoE pressure weapons.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Starfall (Astral Staff)	[list]		[*]Damage per tick: 66 → 63[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Axes[/b]

[quote][i]Razor Cut’s lifesteal effect has been significantly buffed to increase its impact.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Razor Cut (Bear Paws)	[list]		[*]Lifesteal: 10% → 20%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Bows[/b]

[quote][i]Bows had fallen out of the meta following previous nerfs, so a portion of their power has been restored.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Enchanted Quiver (Bow)	[list]		[*]Attack damage increase: 220% → 230%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Daggers[/b]

[quote][i]Twin Slayers have been performing well, but since it never feels good to be unable to recall your daggers due to a lack of energy, the entire energy cost is now paid up front.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Ring of Death (Twin Slayers)	[list]		[*]Cast energy cost: 6 → 12[/*]		[*]Recast energy cost: 6 → 0[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Fire Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Infernal Staff has struggled to find its place in the meta. As a result, its fear duration has been increased to allow more set-up time on the primary target, and require enemies to pay more attention to its fiery trail.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Combustion (Infernal Staff)	[list]		[*]Fear duration: 0.75s → 1.25s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shapeshifter Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Fireflash Orb’s damage bonus has been increased to further reward Hellfire Imp players for hitting targets from greater distances.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Fireflash Orb (Hellspawn Staff)	[list]		[*]Bonus damage per tick: 30 → 33[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b]

[quote][i]Clarent Blade had been affected by multiple tangential nerfs, so in order to revitalize it, the value of its secondary effect has been increased across all stack counts.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Crescent Slash (Clarent Blade)	[list]		[*]1 stack slow duration: 2s → 2.25s[/*]		[*]2 stack silence duration: 2s → 2.25s[/*]		[*]3 stack damage: 155 → 160[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Soulless Stream’s long casting time has struggled in modern Albion. It has now been reduced slightly, but not so much that it loses its identity.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Soulless Stream (Galatine Pair)	[list]		[*]Cast time: 1.1s → 0.9s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]War Gloves[/b]

[quote][i]Earth Crusher’s knock-up duration has been extended to further highlight its utility. [/i][/quote][list]	[*]Earth Crusher (Ravenstrike Cestus)	[list]		[*]Knock-up duration: 1s → 1.2s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]In addition to some hitbox and hit detection improvements, Shockwave's damage has been significantly increased to better accommodate mid-range fighting builds.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Shockwave (all Gloves)	[list]		[*]Damage: 106 → 122[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Helmets[/b]

[quote][i]While Firebreath is a popular solo PvE item, its damage has been increased to improve its success in PvP encounters.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Firebreath (Mage Cowl)	[list]		[*]Damage per tick: 33 → 36[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]All Gathering Caps now have the Emergency Shield spell to help gatherers remove lingering DoTs before consuming an Invisibility Potion or mounting up.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]All Gathering Caps	[list]		[*]Additional ability: Emergency Shield (same as the Guardian Helmet ability)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shoes[/b]

[quote][i]While the adoption of Demon Boots following its previous buffs has been satisfying, they now offer too much mobility at higher health percentages. Therefore, their buff duration and move speed bonus per stack have been reduced slightly.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Vengeful Sprint (Demon Boots)	[list]		[*]Move speed bonus per stack: 25% → 22%[/*]		[*]Duration: 6s → 5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Mounts[/b]

[quote][i]Toxic Reaction has been removed, as it had the potential to put the mount's rider into combat unintentionally, hindering their ability to flee.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Toxic Reaction (Pest Lizard) has been removed[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Spell Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Dodge (all T4+ Shoes): Fixed issue where immunity could be purged[/*]	[*]Interrupt (Swords): Fixed issue where the buff icon did not match the spell icon[/*]	[*]Toxic Cloud (Pest Lizard), Energy Cloud (Tower Chariot), Boulder Crash (Earthrune Staff), Sky’s Fury (Skystrider Bow), and Infernal Boulder (Hellfire Hands) now have more accurate spell indication areas[/*]	[*]Fixed several spell tooltips with more accurate descriptions[/*][/list]
[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where sorting options in the Guild Rights Management UI behaved incorrectly[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where filtering the Bank Overview by all tiers would filter out all tiers, rather than including them[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where several categories in the Rankings UI were not displaying in the correct order[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where some T3 weapons had their abilities displayed in the wrong order on the Item Details UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Hellion Hood spells were displayed in the wrong order on the Item Details UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where hovering over an item’s Average Price or Market History at the Marketplace would not display the exact amount[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where different travel costs could be displayed for the same journey, depending on the UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the region map would not display City Plot details if opened while changing regions[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the Arena Match invitation pop-up could be closed with the ESC key without canceling the match, preventing entry[/*]	[*][CONTROLLER] Fixed issue where Marketplace category filters could not be changed[/*][/list]
[b]Albion Journal Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where missions to free Captured Smugglers would not grant progress to party members[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where missions to defeat Ghouls and Brawlers did not count all types[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where defeating Archers within Avalonian Dungeons counted towards the wrong Albion Journal mission[/*][/list]
[b]Other Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where items recovered to a city bank could not be accessed from a corresponding island bank[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the Smuggler’s Den and Hideout Fame buffs could stack[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where having an Awakened Item in equipment or inventory would trigger spell cooldowns when changing regions[/*]	[*]Various additional graphical, animation, terrain, audio, UI, and localization fixes[/*][/list]

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Patch 1
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch follows up on previous combat balance changes, enhances some less prominent weapons and abilities, and introduces additional changes and fixes.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Changes[/h3]

[b]Item Destruction[/b][list]	[*]Items can no longer be destroyed if a player is ejected from the Roads of Avalon[/*]	[*]Many item types that previously did not create a trash item upon destruction (e.g. consumable items) began to do so with the Rogue Frontier update	[list]		[*]This has been reverted, and those items once again do not generate trash[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]In addition, we would like to clarify the changed rate of item destruction in the Rogue Frontier update	[list]		[*]Equipable items had their destruction rate increased from 30% to 33%[/*]		[*]Non-equipable items had their destruction rate decreased from 36% to 33%[/*]		[*]These rates have not changed at all in this patch[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Other Changes[/b][list]	[*]Energy destruction from Territory Raiding has been increased from 10% to 20%[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Axes[/b]

[quote][i]Relentless Assault’s damage has been increased, to help Crystal Reaper find its place in the meta.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Relentless Assault (Crystal Reaper)	[list]		[*]Damage: 90 → 105[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Bows[/b]

[quote][i]Skystrider Bow’s Sky Bolts now deal more damage and hit more easily, especially against close-range targets.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Sky's Fury (Skystrider Bow)	[list]		[*]Dash range: 7m → 10m[/*]		[*]Buff duration: 3.5s → 3.75s[/*]		[*]Damage per bolt: 130 → 140[/*]		[*]Bolt hit delay: 0.6s → 0.4s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]As Undead Arrows is a toggled ability with a significant downside while active, its cooldown has been reduced to make it less punishing to toggle off.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Undead Arrows (Whispering Bow)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 12s → 10s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Frost Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Hoarfrost has received a significant buff to increase its baseline effectiveness.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Avalanche (Hoarfrost Staff)	[list]		[*]Snowball damage: 60 → 120[/*]		[*]Snowball Knockback distance: 5m → 10m (knockback duration unchanged)[/*]		[*]Increased slow trail width: 4m → 5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shapeshifter Staffs[/b]

[quote][i]Pulse Shock is intended to support melee-oriented transformations, but not so strong as to be the default damaging Q. Therefore, its damage has been reduced.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Pulse Shock (all Shapeshifter Staffs)	[list]		[*]Damage: 109 → 97[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list][quote][i]Following the recent range increase to Sinister Swipes, Prowling Staff has gained a lot of stickiness, and no longer requires such a strong baseline movement speed increase.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Shadow Panther Transform (Prowling Staff)	[list]		[*]Transformation movement speed: 6.5 → 5.5[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]War Gloves[/b]

[quote][i]Purifying Combination's cooldown has been increased to remove some of Fists of Avalon’s power as a non-commital mobility option.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Purifying Combination (Fists of Avalon)	[list]		[*]Dive Kick cooldown: 20s → 25s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Helmets[/b]

[quote][i]Circle of Inspiration’s maximum targets have been increased to make Druid Cowl more suitable for large groups.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Circle of Inspiration (Druid Cowl)	[list]		[*]Max targets: 5 → 10[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Spell Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Evasive Jump (Royal Shoes): Fixed issue where immunities could incorrectly be purged[/*]	[*]Infernal Boulder (Hellfire Hands): Fixed issue where a line of sight was required[/*]	[*]Sky Bolt (Skystrider Bow): Fixed issue where a line of sight was required[/*][/list]
[b]UI Fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where islands would sometimes not be selectable in the Travel Planner UI[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where linking Kill Trophies in chat would not display correctly[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where it was not possible to reach Elite Levels on the Destiny Board using the Learn button[/*]	[*][MOBILE] Fixed issue where chat channel buttons would not work[/*]	[*][MOBILE] Fixed issue where long-pressing in various UIs would fail to bring up tooltips[/*][/list]

notes.title: Season 26 Starts Saturday
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7f55ae8006b1f0c456141500c734abfd0bf10d85.jpeg[/img]

The [url=https://albiononline.com/news/rogue-frontier-live][b]Rogue Frontier[/b][/url] update is live, and players are diving into Smuggler’s Dens, trading their wares on the Smuggler’s Network, and planting Kill Trophies in the open world. And things are about to step up another gear in Albion, as [b]Season 26 [/b]kicks off this [b]Saturday, February 8[/b]!

[h3]Season Changes[/h3]
This season is the first to use the new, shorter Guild Season format. The length of a season has been reduced to [b]59 days[/b], and there will be three Invasion Days – at the beginning, middle, and end of the season. This promises to make seasons even more intense and action-packed, with opportunities for guilds of all sizes to rise up the rankings.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7bd8faa3744066dc1d1933703a34302989ba05c1.jpeg[/img]

The Might requirements for the various Guild Challenges have been reduced in accordance with the shortened season, and the Season Points for PvE, Gathering, and Corrupted Dungeons have been increased significantly. For a full rundown of these changes, see the ‘Season Changes’ section in the [url=https://albiononline.com/changelog/rogue-frontier-update][b]Rogue Frontier patchnotes[/b][/url].

[h3]Watch the Season Start Live[/h3]
As always, we’ll be bringing you the action from the opening weekend of the season live on [b]AlbionTV ([/b][url=http://twitch.tv/AlbionOnline][b]twitch.tv/AlbionOnline[/b][/url][b])[/b]. Tune in at the following times to watch the action on all three servers:
[list]	[*][b]Albion Asia[/b]: February 8, 14:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Europe[/b]: February 8, 18:00 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Americas[/b]: February 9, 01:00 UTC[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce8b5e9ab7439b9ba58a0be0f6be676744087ce.jpeg[/img]

We’re excited to see Albion’s guilds rushing forth to claim territories and work their way up the season rankings in this new format, so see you then!

For the full season schedule, check [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/207076][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

tags.balance_change: The Might requirements for the various Guild Challenges have been reduced in accordance with the shortened season, and the Season Points for PvE, Gathering, and Corrupted Dungeons have been increased significantly.

notes.title: Rogue Frontier is Live!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a47c46c8bc3fb15cc8355ab6f4926ad87236a462.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Rogue Frontier[/b] is open! Albion’s shady new update introduces the [b]Smugglers[/b], a new Outlands-based faction with much to offer daring adventurers, along with [b]Kill Trophies[/b], new [b]Crystal Weapons[/b], a [b]Bank Overview[/b], and more.

Get a taste of what’s available in our brand-new trailer:

[previewyoutube=1JVBcYooqcU?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Roguish Opportunities[/h3]
This update introduces [b]Smuggler’s Dens[/b] to the Outlands – underground lairs which solo and small-scale players can make their bases of operations. Within these you’ll be able to access the [b]Smuggler’s Network[/b], a new market system for the Outlands which opens up intriguing trade opportunities. The Smugglers bring new [b]activities [/b]with them as well, as you can help them transport their contraband wares or free apprehended rogues to earn their approval. Get on their good side, and you’ll be able to purchase brand-new themed items, like the [b]Smuggler Cape [/b]and exclusive vanity skins.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0836623682fb0e071c52c55b974806ddd6ccd011.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Prestigious Prizes[/h3]
[b]Kill Trophies[/b] are new furniture items that act as a souvenir of your most legendary PvP victories. These mementos come in three different designs, depending on where the kill took place, and allow you to show off your combat prowess to enemies and friends alike. New [b]Crystal Weapons[/b] are now available, too, bringing awesome new abilities to Albion’s battlefields. And a new [b]Albion Journal[/b] Category – Creatures – challenges you to kill all of Albion’s myriad mobs, with intimidating rewards like the Emerald Basilisk available to the most determined hunters.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d8886a1e02c7a578e2a21d91e9eab47be8e5ea1f.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Further Improvements[/h3]
The [b]Bank Overview[/b] is here, allowing you to view where all of your items are stored, from wherever you are in Albion. New varieties of [b]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b] have been added, providing even more lucrative opportunities to intrepid gatherers. And there’s a broad array of combat balance changes and further quality-of-life improvements too, keeping things fresh and fun for all players.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c83898838809ea114e0d37da3685289bc785ee48.jpeg[/img]

[h3]Double Twitch Drops[/h3]
To celebrate the release of Rogue Frontier, we’re offering [b]double Twitch Drops[/b] until [b]February 16 at 9:30 UTC[/b] on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url] and all other streams in the Albion Online category! Here’s how you can get them:
[list]	[*]Make sure you are logged into the Albion Online account where you want your drops delivered[/*]	[*]Connect your Twitch account with your Albion Online account [url=https://www.albiononline.com/twitch][b]here[/b][/url][/*]	[*]Watch any streams in the [url=https://www.twitch.tv/directory/category/albion-online][b]Albion Online category[/b][/url] on Twitch[/*][/list]For more on what lies on the Rogue Frontier, check out our latest Dev Talks [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-smugglers][b]here[/b][/url] and [url=https://albiononline.com/news/dev-talk-trophies-more][b]here[/b][/url], read the full patchnotes [url=https://albiononline.com/changelog/rogue-frontier-update][b]here[/b][/url], and check out the [b]official update page [/b]here:
 

[b][url=https://albiononline.com/update/rogue-frontier]LEARN MORE[/url][/b]

notes.title: Changelog: Rogue Frontier Update
notes.content:
[quote][i]This update expands the Outlands with the introduction of Smuggler’s Dens, the Smuggler’s Network, and the Smuggler Faction, providing new tools and activities for solo and small group players. It also adds a Bank Overview, new Crystal Weapons, Kill Trophies, and brings adjustments to Guild Seasons and the economy.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Smuggler’s Dens[/h3]

Smuggler’s Dens are new safe zones within the Outlands, offering certain city amenities and allowing solo and small-scale players to base themselves in the Outlands.[list]	[*]There are 35 Smuggler’s Dens in total[/*]	[*]These contain a Repair Station, Artifact Foundry, Travel Planner, Bank, the new Smuggler Faction trader, and a Smuggler’s Marketplace (see ‘Smuggler’s Network’ below)[/*]	[*]Outlands Banks have been removed	[list]		[*]Instead, Banks in the Outlands can be found within Smuggler’s Dens[/*]		[*]Items stored within Outlands Banks have been moved to a Smuggler’s Den nearby, with bank tabs opened for these items[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Each Smuggler’s Den has two entrances, both located within the same Outlands region	[list]		[*]These entrances are displayed on the minimap[/*]		[*]Outlaws and players in combat cannot enter a Smuggler’s Den[/*]		[*]Players can enter and exit while mounted, and can mount up within[/*]		[*]Entering a Smuggler’s Den resets active S.A.F.E. Portal and Journey Back bindings[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Smuggler’s Dens can be set as a player’s home	[list]		[*]Travel to a Smuggler’s Den is possible if set as home, and only without luggage[/*]		[*]When a Smuggler’s Den is set as home, players receive a 2.5% buff to Combat and Gathering Fame in the Outlands[/*]		[*]Having a Smuggler’s Den set as home significantly intensifies the effect of Disarray to disincentivize guilds from using them as a base for large-scale battles (see ‘Additional Changes and Improvements’ below for details)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Smugglers’ Network[/h3]

The Smuggler’s Network is a new, Outlands-based Marketplace network, which operates independently of the Royal Continent Marketplaces. The Marketplaces in this network are connected, allowing players to buy from distant points in the Smuggler’s Network, albeit with distance fees applied. It gives players the ability to offload loot, and the choice to regear within the Outlands for a fee or do so from the Royal Continent at lower fees.[list]	[*]Smuggler’s Markets can be found within Smuggler’s Dens and Outlands Rests	[list]		[*]Unlike Marketplaces on the Royal Continent, these are all connected, essentially functioning as a single Marketplace with multiple access points[/*]		[*]Active Buy and Sell Orders and unclaimed items on Outlands Rests Marketplaces will be moved to the new Smuggler’s Network[/*]		[*]Buy and Sell Orders can be canceled from any location within the network, but editing orders or claiming items can only be done where the order was created[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Distance Fees are applied when completing orders remotely	[list]		[*]These fees are determined by:		[list]			[*]The distance between where in the Outlands an item was sold and where it was purchased[/*]			[*]The item price[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]The greater the distance, the higher the fee[/*]		[*]The fee is always paid by the player completing the transaction[/*]		[*]Not subject to a Premium discount[/*]		[*]The distance is displayed in a new column in the Marketplace UI[/*]		[*]A ‘Max Distance’ filter can be applied[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Displayed prices include fees by default	[list]		[*]This can be toggled to display prices without fees, to make it possible to compare original listing prices and view their locations    [/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Items must meet a minimum price threshold to be listed on this Marketplace[/*][/list]
[h3]Smuggler’s Activities[/h3]

This update introduces a new, Outlands-based faction: the Smugglers. There are three new activities which players can perform in the Outlands to earn Standing with this faction, along with Might and Favor.

[b]Smuggler Crates[/b][list]	[*]Smuggler Crates spawn in the open world	[list]		[*]They can be found within a broken Smuggler Wagon[/*]		[*]Multiple Crates can spawn at one of these Wagons[/*]		[*]Depending on the amount of crates in a Wagon, their broadcast range varies		[list]			[*]1 crate:			[list]				[*]Visible in close proximity[/*]				[*]Unlocked immediately[/*]			[/list]			[/*]			[*]5 crates:			[list]				[*]Visible on the Region Map[/*]				[*]Locked for 1 minute[/*]			[/list]			[/*]			[*]10 crates:			[list]				[*]Visible on the Region Map[/*]				[*]Locked for 3 minutes[/*]			[/list]			[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Crates have four rarity levels, indicated by a colored glow		[list]			[*]Green: Common[/*]			[*]Blue: Uncommon[/*]			[*]Purple: Rare[/*]			[*]Golden: Legendary[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Dismounted players can pick up and carry these Crates	[list]		[*]A player can only carry one Crate at a time[/*]		[*]The highest rarity level is automatically the first to be picked up[/*]		[*]Players carrying Smuggler Crates are not displayed on the Region Map[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Once picked up, multiple drop-off locations, called Smuggler Stashes, appear on the Region Map[/*]	[*]Successfully transporting a Crate to one of these Stashes rewards the player with Might, Favor, and Smuggler Standing[/*]	[*]Crates can be dropped, though they cannot be returned to the Wagon[/*]	[*]Dropped Crates disappear after 30 minutes[/*][/list]
[b]Captured Smugglers[/b][list]	[*]Captured Smugglers can be found in the open world, surrounded by Royal Guards[/*]	[*]Players can free a Captured Smuggler after defeating the guards	[list]		[*]After a short channel, the Smuggler is freed and the player rewarded with Smuggler Standing, Might and Favor[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Smuggler’s Coins[/b][list]	[*]Smuggler’s Coins can be found as additional loot in Camp Caches, Coffers, and Hidden Treasures in the Outlands[/*]	[*]These can be delivered to Maggy Slade in Smuggler’s Dens (see ‘Smuggler’s Rewards’ below) to increase your Smuggler Standing and earn a small amount of Favor[/*][/list]
[h3]Smuggler’s Rewards[/h3]

Smuggler’s Dens play host to a shadowy new NPC: Maggy Slade. Brand new Smuggler items can be purchased from her with Favor.

[b]Smuggler Cape[/b][list]	[*]A craftable Cape with a unique passive spell – Hidden Vial	[list]		[*]This spell activates upon using a potion, reducing the potion slot cooldown by 90 seconds[/*]		[*]After activation, the spell enters a long cooldown[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Crafting a Smuggler Cape requires:	[list]		[*]A Smuggler Crest (purchasable from Maggy Slade)[/*]		[*]A Caerleon Heart[/*]		[*]A base cape of Tier 4 to Tier 8[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Smuggler Vanity Items[/b][list]	[*]New, non-tradable vanity items can be purchased from Maggy Slade:	[list]		[*]Full Smuggler wardrobe set		[list]			[*]Smuggler’s Hat[/*]			[*]Smuggler’s Coat[/*]			[*]Smuggler’s Boots[/*]			[*]Smuggler’s Cloak[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Smuggler Avatar[/*]		[*]Smuggler Avatar Frame[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Bank Overview[/h3]

This is a much-requested new UI which allows players to see an overview of items they have stored in all banks across the game, including the new banks in Smuggler’s Dens. Players with the ‘Manage Guild Chests’ guild right can also view items stored in their guild’s shared bank tabs from the Bank Overview.[list]	[*]The Bank Overview can be opened from:	[list]		[*]The Player Menu (clicking or tapping your character avatar in the top-left of the screen)[/*]		[*]The hotkey ‘K’[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]There is now also a ‘Search in Bank Overview’ option in the Item Details UI	[list]		[*]This allows you to see where you currently have items of that type stored[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Upon opening, players can see an overview of the number of items they have in each bank and their estimated market value	[list]		[*]Clicking an item shows its details[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The contents of the selected bank tab are displayed in the right-hand side of the UI[/*]	[*]Shared Bank contents are not updated in real time	[list]		[*]The time since the information was last updated is displayed in the top right[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]A dropdown menu allows players to switch between bank tabs	[list]		[*]Recovered items from a destroyed Hideout have their own entry in this menu[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]From this UI, items can be searched and filtered across all banks simultaneously	[list]		[*]Items cannot be moved, stacked, or sorted – this is a view-only UI[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]This feature also allows players to view and recover items from Guild Islands to which they have lost access	[list]		[*]Recovered items are moved to a new tab in the nearest city or Smuggler’s Den bank from where they have been recovered[/*]		[*]As long as a Recovered Items tab exists in a bank, more of these tabs cannot be created at the same bank until it is cleared[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Kill Trophies[/h3]

Kill Trophies are new, themed furniture items that serve as mementos of PvP combat victories. They allow you to admire a monument to your own triumph, and brag to your friends and foes about your combat prowess.[list]	[*]There is a chance for one of these to drop whenever you kill a player in full-loot PvP combat	[list]		[*]They come in three different sizes[/*]		[*]The more valuable the victim, the greater the chance that a trophy will drop, and that it will be a larger trophy[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Knockdowns and self-kills do not grant Kill Trophies[/*]	[*]There are three variants of Kill Trophies, called Mementos, depending on where the kill occurred	[list]		[*]Open World Mementos drop in the Outlands and the Roads of Avalon[/*]		[*]Hell Mementos drop in Corrupted Dungeons and Hellgates[/*]		[*]Mists Mementos drop in the Mists and Knightfall Abbey[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Mementos can be placed in the open world or on islands[/*]	[*]They display the kill details, including the victim’s name[/*]	[*]They are tradable, but cannot be sold at the Marketplace[/*][/list]
[h3]Dynamic Resource Hotspot Additions[/h3]

This update builds on the introduction of Dynamic Resource Hotspots in the Horizons update with three new variations, giving dedicated gatherers lucrative new objectives to pursue.

[b]Medium Resource Hotspots[/b][list]	[*]These are larger Resource Hotspots than the ones that currently exist[/*]	[*]They can appear in open-world regions from Tier 5 to Tier 8, and are active for an entire day[/*]	[*]They contain one resource type, and can also contain Resource Guardians (eg. Old White)	[list]		[*]Resource Guardians can spawn in any region where their matching resource can be found, regardless of the Hotspot's resource type[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]In the open world, Resource Guardians now spawn exclusively in these areas[/*][/list]
[b]Resource Mists[/b][list]	[*]Resource Mists can be accessed by finding a Verdant Will o’ Wisp in a Dynamic Resource Hotspot[/*]	[*]A Verdant Will o’  Wisp can be pursued until it opens a portal	[list]		[*]These portals lead to smaller, resource-rich Mists[/*]		[*]The primary resource found within a Resource Mist is the same as that of the Resource Hotspot from which it was accessed[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]These can range from Tier 6 to Tier 8, and exist in different rarities[/*]	[*]There are Small Resource Mists for individual players, and Medium Resource Mists where you can encounter other players[/*]	[*]Resource Mists close after a short time, with Medium Resource Mists lasting longer than Small ones[/*][/list]
[b]Small Resource Mob Hotspots[/b][list]	[*]Small Resource Mob Hotspots spawn Resource Mobs of their biome’s primary type[/*][/list]
[h3]New Albion Journal Category[/h3]

This update introduces the eighth Albion Journal category: Creatures.[list]	[*]This challenges players to hunt every type of creature that can be found in the world of Albion[/*]	[*]New, unique rewards, based around the theme of a beast hunter, are available as you progress through the category[/*][/list]In addition, a new subcategory – Smugglers – has been added to the Exploration category.

[h3]New Crystal Weapons[/h3]

With this update, three new Crystal Weapons are available to successful guilds, each with its own unique spell:[list]	[*][b]Rotcaller Staff (Cursed Staff): [/b]Plaguebringer summons a cursed spectre that spews a deadly mist[/*]	[*][b]Skystrider Bow (Bow): [/b]Sky’s Fury allows you to jump into the air and fire powerful bolts down onto your opponents[/*]	[*][b]Forcepulse Bracers (War Gloves): [/b]Unstoppable Rush infuses your attacks with magical damage as you dash towards your enemies[/*][/list]
[h3]Gold Market Stabilization[/h3]

With this update, we are introducing a self-regulating economic system to the game that will help stabilize the price of Gold and Premium when purchased with Silver. This system automatically makes minor adjustments on each server as needed, to gradually stabilize prices without the need for large-scale economic intervention.

As a result, players may notice changes in the amount of Silver received for some activities – such as killing mobs –, and in the Silver cost for certain actions. These changes will be quite subtle, however, and will slow down over the long term, thus avoiding any economic shocks.

[h3]Season Changes[/h3]

Beginning with Season 26, Guild Seasons will be shortened to 59 days, in order to create a more dynamic and engaging experience:[list]	[*]Territories will reset three times during a season:	[list]		[*]Opening Day[/*]		[*]Mid-Season Invasion Day[/*]		[*]Final Weekend[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Double point scoring will begin on the mid-season Invasion Day, and cover half the season[/*]	[*]Off-season length will alternate between the standard 12 days and a shorter 5-day break[/*][/list]Several balance adjustments accompany the shorter season:[list]	[*]Territories now generate 50% more Fortification Points each day[/*]	[*]Conqueror's Challenge Chest values have been adjusted in proportion to the season length[/*]	[*]The 90-day Fame buff reward (Knight's Vow) has been replaced with a shorter 60-day Fame buff[/*]	[*]A new Guild Challenge has been added for Smuggler Activities[/*]	[*]Basic Guild Challenge	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 50%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Crystal Creatures	[list]		[*]Might, Favor, and Loot rewards have been doubled[/*]		[*]Crystal Creature respawn rate reduced by 50%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Territory Energy Crystals	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 44%[/*]		[*]Season Points reduced by 20% to balance the impact of double scoring now applying to a larger portion of the season[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Hideout Power Cores	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 30%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Treasure Chests	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 35%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Castles	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 33%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]PvE	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 33%[/*]		[*]Season Points increased by 100%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Gathering	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 30%[/*]		[*]Season Points increased by 300%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Corrupted Dungeons	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 25%[/*]		[*]Season Points increased by 25%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]2v2 Hellgates	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 30%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]5v5 Hellgates	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 33%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]10v10 Hellgates	[list]		[*]Requirements reduced by 33%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Arena	[list]		[*]Promotion values have been adjusted to enable faster rank progression:		[list]			[*]Rank Iron 1: 250 → 150[/*]			[*]Rank Iron 2: 500 → 300[/*]			[*]Rank Iron 3: 750 → 450[/*]			[*]Rank Iron 4: 1000 → 600[/*]			[*]Rank Bronze 1: 1250 → 750[/*]			[*]Rank Bronze 2: 1500 → 900[/*]			[*]Rank Bronze 3: 1750 → 1050[/*]			[*]Rank Bronze 4: 2000 → 1200[/*]			[*]Rank Silver 1: 2250 → 1350[/*]			[*]Rank Silver 2: 2500 → 1500[/*]			[*]Rank Silver 3: 2750 → 1650[/*]			[*]Rank Silver 4: 3000 → 1800[/*]			[*]Rank Gold 1: 3250 → 1950[/*]			[*]Rank Gold 2: 3500 → 2100[/*]			[*]Rank Gold 3: 3750 → 2250[/*]			[*]Rank Gold 4: 4000 → 2400[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Demotion values have been adjusted to 50 points below the promotion threshold for the previous rank (previously 100 points)		[list]			[*]For example, you will drop from Bronze 1 to Iron 4 (promotion threshold: 600 points) if your points fall below 550[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Headquarters Hideout requirements have not changed for Season 26 due to the overall Season Point output remaining largely unchanged[/*][/list]
[h3]Additional Changes and Improvements[/h3]

[b]Home and Disarray Changes[/b][list]	[*]Players entering the Outlands from a Portal Town no longer lose their home if it is set to a location there (Outlands Hideout, Rests, or Smuggler’s Den)[/*]	[*]Instead, they now receive a new debuff, ‘Homesick’[/*]	[*]When in groups of 21 or more players, Homesick significantly increases the effect of Disarray:	[list]		[*]Normal Disarray Level 1 reduces Damage & CC by 1%[/*]		[*]Increased Disarray Level 1 reduces Damage & CC by 21%[/*]		[*]Normal Disarray Level 2 reduces Damage & CC by 2%[/*]		[*]Increased Disarray Level 2 reduces Damage & CC by 22%, etc.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]This debuff also applies when players have set home in a Smuggler’s Den[/*][/list]
[b]Dynamic Encampment Changes[/b][list]	[*]Since the Mob Fame Penalty was removed from Dynamic Encampments with Horizons Patch 1, the total amount of Fame from Group Dynamic Encampments has overperformed relative to other features[/*]	[*]To bring Group Dynamic Encampments more in line with other features, the amount of non-tradable Tome Fame found in the Green (Common) Caches of open-world Encampments has been reduced[/*]	[*]While open-world Solo Dynamic Encampments are also affected by this Fame reduction to a lesser extent, they were also found to be underperforming from a loot perspective, so they have received an increase of 10% to their loot[/*]	[*]Both types of Encampments can now also drop Smuggler's Coins from their Green (Common) Cache variants[/*]	[*]Neither of these changes affect the Mists, and mobs still yield their full Fame value[/*][/list]
[b]Mists Changes[/b][list]	[*]Unstable Roads found within the Mists now have an increased chance to spawn:	[list]		[*]Unenchanted Mists: 10% → 25%[/*]		[*]Enchanted Mists: 50% → 100%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Unstable Roads found within Nonlethal Mists are now more likely to connect to the Royal Continent, while Unstable Roads within Lethal Mists are more likely to connect to the Outlands[/*]	[*]Wisps now ignore mounted players[/*][/list]

tags.feature: This update expands the Outlands with the introduction of Smuggler’s Dens, the Smuggler’s Network, and the Smuggler Faction, providing new tools and activities for solo and small group players. It also adds a Bank Overview, new Crystal Weapons, Kill Trophies, and brings adjustments to Guild Seasons and the economy.
Smuggler’s Dens are new safe zones within the Outlands, offering certain city amenities and allowing solo and small-scale players to base themselves in the Outlands.

The Smuggler’s Network is a new, Outlands-based Marketplace network, which operates independently of the Royal Continent Marketplaces. The Marketplaces in this network are connected, allowing players to buy from distant points in the Smuggler’s Network, albeit with distance fees applied. It gives players the ability to offload loot, and the choice to regear within the Outlands for a fee or do so from the Royal Continent at lower fees.

This update introduces a new, Outlands-based faction: the Smugglers. There are three new activities which players can perform in the Outlands to earn Standing with this faction, along with Might and Favor.
Smuggler Crates spawn in the open world
Captured Smugglers can be found in the open world, surrounded by Royal Guards
Smuggler’s Coins can be found as additional loot in Camp Caches, Coffers, and Hidden Treasures in the Outlands
Smuggler’s Dens play host to a shadowy new NPC: Maggy Slade. Brand new Smuggler items can be purchased from her with Favor.
A craftable Cape with a unique passive spell – Hidden Vial
New, non-tradable vanity items can be purchased from Maggy Slade:

This is a much-requested new UI which allows players to see an overview of items they have stored in all banks across the game, including the new banks in Smuggler’s Dens. Players with the ‘Manage Guild Chests’ guild right can also view items stored in their guild’s shared bank tabs from the Bank Overview.

Kill Trophies are new, themed furniture items that serve as mementos of PvP combat victories. They allow you to admire a monument to your own triumph, and brag to your friends and foes about your combat prowess.
There is a chance for one of these to drop whenever you kill a player in full-loot PvP combat
This update builds on the introduction of Dynamic Resource Hotspots in the Horizons update with three new variations, giving dedicated gatherers lucrative new objectives to pursue.
Medium Resource Hotspots are larger Resource Hotspots than the ones that currently exist
Resource Mists can be accessed by finding a Verdant Will o’ Wisp in a Dynamic Resource Hotspot
Small Resource Mob Hotspots spawn Resource Mobs of their biome’s primary type
This update introduces the eighth Albion Journal category: Creatures.
In addition, a new subcategory – Smugglers – has been added to the Exploration category.
With this update, three new Crystal Weapons are available to successful guilds, each with its own unique spell:

With this update, we are introducing a self-regulating economic system to the game that will help stabilize the price of Gold and Premium when purchased with Silver. This system automatically makes minor adjustments on each server as needed, to gradually stabilize prices without the need for large-scale economic intervention.
Beginning with Season 26, Guild Seasons will be shortened to 59 days, in order to create a more dynamic and engaging experience:
Several balance adjustments accompany the shorter season:
Players entering the Outlands from a Portal Town no longer lose their home if it is set to a location there (Outlands Hideout, Rests, or Smuggler’s Den)
Since the Mob Fame Penalty was removed from Dynamic Encampments with Horizons Patch 1, the total amount of Fame from Group Dynamic Encampments has overperformed relative to other features
Unstable Roads found within the Mists now have an increased chance to spawn:
Unstable Roads found within Nonlethal Mists are now more likely to connect to the Royal Continent, while Unstable Roads within Lethal Mists are more likely to connect to the Outlands
Knockdowns and Arena deaths are now included in the Player Stats UI (in the Deaths and Kills tabs)
UI windows now scale according to the aspect ratio of the display
Added an ‘S’ to the bottom of the minimap to indicate South
Marketplace UI now keeps filter settings separated per tab, except for Loadouts
Attacker’s equipment information is now included in the Death Recap
Death Recap entry in the Player Menu is now always visible, appearing in a disabled state when unavailable
The login screen now scales with the Window Scaling setting in the Interface menu
Added a server selection UI to match the existing mobile version
Icons for the buttons opening the game menu and party UIs in the combined tracker have been updated
A click-through option is now available for some HUD elements: minimap (desktop only), spell buttons, and player frames
Controller support added to the Manage Layouts UI
Minimap opacity now affects only the background texture, leaving labels and icons unchanged
The amount of Boss Lair chests has been changed back down to 1 (from 3), but their loot multiplier has been increased back up to 3 (from 1)
Hideout bonus buffs now apply from Power Level 1, and the bonus Fame levels are as follows:
The trash rate of equipable items has been increased slightly, while the trash rate of non-equipment items has been reduced slightly
City Banks can now be accessed from Personal Islands connected to that city
Kill messages in chat are now highlighted to show the killer and victim’s relation to you
Crystal Arena Avatar Ring items are now salvageable, allowing players to repurpose duplicate items:
Tier 4, 6, and 8 versions of Resource Mobs have been added to their respective biomes

tags.balance_change: Chain Missile’s bounce damage has received a boost to help solo Arcane Staff players clear packs of enemies in PvE.
Chain Missile (all Arcane Staffs)
Bounce damage: 25 → 40

Bear Paws have been very successful as a ganking weapon, especially in catching opponents, but their fighting abilities have been somewhat lacking. To make them less one-dimensional, their fighting strength has been improved, but their catch potential toned down.
Razor Cut (Bear Paws)
Added 10% life steal buff for 4s on cast start
Removed Damage over Time effect

Jump can no longer be interrupted
Jump Range: 10m → 8m
Jump Speed: 22 → 18
Rending Strike’s damage has fallen behind Rending Rage, even on single targets. For this reason, Rending Strike’s damage has been increased.
Rending Strike (all Axes)
Damage: 54 → 59
Cursed Tar (all Cursed Staffs)
Improved area hit detection on initial tick
Maximum area duration: 4s → 4.2s

Inner Shadow’s effect on Leather Armor offered too much sustain in PvE situations. Therefore, its sustain has been reduced against mobs, and increased against players. Its total area damage in PvP has been increased, while its duration has been reduced.
Shadowcaller (Inner Shadow, Leather)
Maximum duration: 3.2s → 2s
Maximum ticks: 5 → 4
Damage per tick (vs players): 24 → 33
Damage per tick (vs mobs): 24 → 16.5

Due to Deathgivers consuming Q Stacks before dealing damage, having two stacks dealt more damage than having max stacks. To fix this, it now consumes stacks after dealing damage. Since this increases the damage output of an already very strong item, its base damage has been reduced to compensate.
Ghost Strike (Deathgivers)
Now deals damage before Sunder Armor’s pierce is removed

Due to its long range and cone angle, Throwing Blades could often hit unintended targets. For this reason, its range has been reduced and damage increased. In addition, its buff no longer requires a unique target, making it more reliable.
Throwing Blades (all Daggers)
Reduced Range: 18m → 12m
Damage: 45 → 60
Damage type: Magical → Physical
Blade radius: 1m → 1.2m
Standtime: 0.4 → 0.2
The one-handed Hammer is the introductory Hammer for players who prefer tank playstyles, so Earth Shatter now has a taunt against mobs to help new tanks and their allies in group PvE.
Earth Shatter (Hammers)
Now makes you the highest priority target for all mobs hit
Powerful Swing’s bonus damage against crowd-controlled targets was too unreliable, so it has been simplified and this conditional strength added to its baseline damage instead.
Powerful Swing (Hammers)
Damage: 113 → 169
Removed: 56 bonus damage to CC’d targets
Fallen Staff has been underused recently. To make it more attractive and to give it a more unique role, it now removes damage-over-time effects.
Salvation (Fallen Staff)
Now cleanses damage-over-time effects
Defensive Slam has received a significant cooldown reduction. While its damage has also been reduced, these changes give it greater damage-over-time potential, making it a more viable option.
Defensive Slam (all Maces)
Damage: 77.81 → 60
Cooldown: 3s → 2s
Threatening Smash’s cooldown has been significantly reduced to make it more viable in a brawling playstyle. This slightly reduces Caerleon Cape’s burst damage.
Threatening Smash (all Maces)
Cooldown: 6s → 4s
Damage: 146 → 135

Thorn Growth is one of the strongest Q-slot damage abilities against multiple enemies in PvE, on a weapon line that also offers very high sustain. Its area damage has therefore been reduced against mobs, while its damage output and usability has been increased in PvP.
Thorn Growth (all Nature Staffs)
Damage vs mobs: 30 → 24
Damage vs players: 25 → 30

Forceful Swing had been able to shut down builds that rely on auto-attacks, but otherwise unreliable. Its duration has therefore been reduced, but the power of its debuff increased significantly to allow Quarterstaff tank players to better protect their allies.
Forceful Swing (all Quarterstaffs)
Damage reduction: 20% → 50%
Duration 8s → 5s
Mystic Rocks no longer removes healing-over-time effects as a separate mechanic. Instead, it now properly negates all healing received by the caster, which includes healing-over-time.
Mystic Rocks (Staff of Balance)
No longer removes healing-over-time effects on the caster
Instead, healing-over-time effects will simply not heal the caster while the effect is active
Adapting Matter’s energy cost has been reduced to make it more similar to the other Shapeshifter Q abilities.
Adapting Matter (all Shapeshifter Staffs)
Energy cost: 16 → 10
Tether Shift’s shield duration has been extended to give its users a longer protection window.
Tether Shift (all Shapeshifter Staffs)
Shield Duration: 1.5s → 2s
Blade Cyclone’s Heroic Stack removal creates a significant cost, so its damage output has been increased to justify this.
Blade Cyclone (all Swords)
1 stack damage: 60 → 70

Swords have high mobility, and Limitbreaker adds another unconditional move speed buff that can be used to engage and disengage. This made its overall mobility somewhat too effective in the Mists, so that buff has been reduced.
Limitbreaker (Infinity Blade)
Move speed buff while channeling: 40% → 30%
Heroic Cleave has had its hit delay reduced to improve its feel and hit more reliably.
Heroic Cleave (all Swords)
Hit delay: 0.3s → 0.2s
To ensure Poison Potions are not too powerful as ganking tools in combination with the new Smuggler Cape, their damage against mounted players has been halved.
Poison Potions
Damage against mounted players reduced by 50%
Spectral Bat, Spectral Direboar, Divine Owl, and Saddled Terrorbird spells no longer interrupt their gallops

Increased Diminishing Returns have helped solo players against multiple enemies, but in large-scale battles where cleanses are widely available, this change nerfed crowd control-focused tank builds more than intended. To make these tanks more viable in large-scale fights, cleanses now significantly reduce Diminishing Returns, resulting in longer crowd control durations, especially in fights with multiple cleanses available.

notes.title: Swoosh into the Carnival Challenge!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b102e4b02ca5668c450bb7006840c81c534492c3.jpeg[/img]

The[b] Carnival Challenge[/b] has arrived, and amidst the joyful chaos, the swift and cunning [b]Terrorbird[/b] streaks through the festivities. Built for the chase, this relentless predator thrives on the thrill of pursuit, its invisibility and speed making it a master of ambush and retreat. Venture into the open world, earn [b]Challenge Points[/b], and bring this untamed hunter to your side before the curtain falls!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/8icVSJN.png[/img]
[b]SADDLED TERRORBIRD:[/b] This month’s Challenge brings back the charming, lightning-fast [b]Saddled Terrorbird[/b], a speedy mount that will carry you quickly across the lands of Albion. With an above-average base move speed and an additional [b]invincibility/speed burst spell[/b], it’s the perfect ride for those who need to cover some ground quickly and safely.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/DknmhgQ.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Along with the Saddled Terrorbird, you’ll unlock the [b]Carnival Challenge Avatar Ring[/b] when you reach this month’s Challenge Point goal. Give your avatar a colorful, festive look all year round! This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded for one [b]Adventurer’s Token[/b] at the Vanity Merchant.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/82d77b86fd6884367e5c504dcebf892dd3ca04cc.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS: [/b]Unlock weekly Carnival Challenge chests to get valuable rewards like Adventurer’s Tomes, resources, and silver bags, along with a chance at carnival-themed [b]Wardrobe Skins[/b]. You can also get three furniture items: the [b]Carnival Firework, Carnival Arch, [/b]and[b] Carnival Costume Cart.[/b]

 
[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer’s Challenge
[/h3]The [b]Adventurer’s Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you’ll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer’s Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

tags.feature: This month’s Challenge brings back the charming, lightning-fast Saddled Terrorbird, a speedy mount that will carry you quickly across the lands of Albion. With an above-average base move speed and an additional invincibility/speed burst spell, it’s the perfect ride for those who need to cover some ground quickly and safely.

Along with the Saddled Terrorbird, you’ll unlock the Carnival Challenge Avatar Ring when you reach this month’s Challenge Point goal. Give your avatar a colorful, festive look all year round! This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded for one Adventurer’s Token at the Vanity Merchant.

Unlock weekly Carnival Challenge chests to get valuable rewards like Adventurer’s Tomes, resources, and silver bags, along with a chance at carnival-themed Wardrobe Skins. You can also get three furniture items: the Carnival Firework, Carnival Arch, and Carnival Costume Cart.
