notes.title: Dev Talk: Kill Trophies, Weapons, Journal & More
notes.content:
[url=https://albiononline.com/update/rogue-frontier][b]Rogue Frontier[/b][/url], Albion Online’s next major update, arrives [b]February 3[/b]. Having looked at many of its features in our previous [b]Dev Talk[/b], today we explore Kill Trophies, new Crystal Weapons, a new Albion Journal category, new Dynamic Resource Hotspots, and a new economic stabilization mechanism. Game Director [b]Robin Henkys [/b]and Head of Production [b]Moritz Bokelmann [/b]took a moment to bring you the details.

[previewyoutube=jpgw4Z-zSyk?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube] [h3]Kill Trophies[/h3]
[b]Kill Trophies [/b]are new furniture items that immortalize your PvP victories.
[list]	[*]When you kill another player, a Kill Trophy may [b]drop[/b][/*]	[*]They display [b]stats[/b] about about the encounter, such as:	[list]		[*]Who you killed[/*]		[*]Their equipment[/*]		[*]When and where the kill occurred[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Each Trophy’s look is determined by where the kill happened	[list]		[*][b]Open world[/b]: a triumphant standard[/*]		[*][b]Hellgates and Corrupted Dungeons[/b]: a demonic monument[/*]		[*][b]The Mists[/b]: a knightly statue[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Kill Trophies are [b]tradable[/b][/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/05c061a9544cae3183f642ee47bc269bf40607e4.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New Crystal Weapons[/h3]
Three brand-new [b]Crystal Weapons [/b]become available when Rogue Frontier launches.
[list]	[*][b]Rotcaller Staff [/b](Cursed Staff): Summon a cursed spectre which spews deadly a mist[/*]	[*][b]Skystrider Bow [/b](Bow): Jump into the air and fire up to three shots onto your enemies below[/*]	[*][b]Forcepulse Bracers [/b](War Gloves): Dash towards a target, infusing your auto-attacks and Q and W abilities with additional magical damage[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d0f83426504ab8af396748392a7dec2e0c54e924.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New Journal Category[/h3]
Rogue Frontier introduces a new Albion Journal category: [b]Creatures[/b].
[list]	[*]A [b]bestiary [/b]containing most of Albion’s enemies[/*]	[*]Shows their [b]appearance [/b]and describes [b]where to find them[/b][/*]	[*]Offers unique rewards, such as	[list]		[*][b]Hunting-themed [/b]wardrobe skins[/*]		[*]The [b]Emerald Basilisk [/b]Swamp Dragon mount skin[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/43b3bbec4d3d271bb5856bda1111a32061a00f13.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/h3]
Three new types of [b]Dynamic Resource Hotspot[/b] are coming.
[list]	[*][b]Medium Resource Hotspots[/b]	[list]		[*]Larger gathering zones with a single resource type[/*]		[*]Found in Tier 5 to Tier 8 regions[/*]		[*]Open-world Resource Guardians are now exclusively found in these[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Resource Mists[/b]	[list]		[*]Accessed via a new type of Wisp[/*]		[*]Temporary regions rich in one resource type[/*]		[*]Coming in two variants		[list]			[*]Small Resource Mists are for solo players[/*]			[*]Medium Resource Mists allow multiplayer encounters[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/fb4f85a9c1d3e01bca4c10b602d6a95335bdeb4f.jpeg[/img]

Additionally, small Dynamic Resource Templates can now spawn [b]Resource Mobs[/b].
[h3]Season Changes[/h3]
Changes are coming to the [b]Guild Season[/b] structure from Season 26.
[list]	[*]Guild Seasons will now last roughly [b]two months[/b], rather than three[/*]	[*]A content update will be released [b]every other season[/b]	[list]		[*]This extends the production cycle, for more impactful updates[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Seasonal challenge [b]requirements and rewards[/b] have been updated for this new schedule[/*][/list]
For more on the Season 26 changes, click [url=https://albiononline.com/news/season-26-changes][b]here[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9aad2d4ba9c78f3933ec7ae5beef1448c985a2f3.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Gold Market Stabilization[/h3]
A new [b]self-balancing economic mechanism[/b] will soon be introduced to help stabilize the prices of Gold and Premium when purchased with Silver, ensuring a healthy economy over the long run.
[list]	[*]This makes [b]daily adjustments[/b] to the prices of certain ingame services, and the amount of Silver generated ingame[/*]	[*]The rate of change will be [b]slow[/b], and decrease further over time[/*]	[*]Prices will [b]gradually stabilize[/b] at a reasonable level for each server[/*]	[*]Slow, gradual adjustments prevent economic shocks and overreaction to temporary trends[/*][/list]
We can’t wait to see all of Rogue Frontier’s new features in action when the update launches on February 3, and we hope to see you ingame then!

notes.title: Big Changes are Coming with Season 26!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/cce8b5e9ab7439b9ba58a0be0f6be676744087ce.jpeg[/img]

With the [url=https://albiononline.com/update/rogue-frontier][b]Rogue Frontier[/b][/url] update arriving February 3, the Outlands are poised to be more vibrant than ever. This sets the stage for a faster-paced Guild Season, where every guild member, from fierce warriors to diligent gatherers, has a critical role in the pursuit of glory. Let's dive into some of the changes coming with Season 26.

[h3]Guild Season Changes[/h3]
Beginning with Season 26, seasons will be reduced to [b]59 days[/b], with a faster-paced, more intense dynamic. Major content updates will now arrive every four months instead of three, allowing for two full seasons within the same update cycle.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8cc626cbb8ec775c91887cf84d4e43687666bd54.png[/img]

Territories will reset [b]three times[/b] during a season: at the start, in the middle, and on the final weekend. The mid-season Invasion Day introduces the [b]double point-scoring [/b]period, meaning this high-stakes phase now covers half the season (previously it was a third). This heightens the need for sharp strategic planning, with greater opportunity for guilds to dramatically change the course of a season. Off-seasons will alternate between twelve and five days.

[h3]Balance Adjustments[/h3]
Several balance adjustments accompany the shorter season:
[list]	[*][b]Might requirements[/b] for Guild Challenges are being reduced[/*]	[*]Territories will generate [b]50% more Fortification Points[/b] each day[/*]	[*]Season Points are being rebalanced:	[list]		[*]Significant boosts to [b]PvE[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and [b]gathering[/b], encouraging open-world exploration and enhancing the value of non-PvP contributions[/*]		[*][b]Energy Crystals[/b] will offer 20% less Season Points, to account for the double scoring phase now covering half the season[/*]		[*]The overall [b]Season Point[/b] output should remain much the same, so Headquarters Hideout requirements are unchanged[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Might, Favor and Loot from [b]Crystal Creatures[/b] is being doubled, but they will respawn 50% less frequently​[/*]	[*][b]Crystal Arena[/b] promotion and demotion values are being adjusted for faster rank progression[/*]	[*][b]Conqueror's Challenge Chest [/b]values are being scaled in proportion to the reduced season length[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8f3026da394dba42efdf4c4e7e89f7a28f8c8cc0.jpeg[/img]

Full details can be found in this [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/207076-Season-26-Schedules/][b]Forum post[/b][/url], and the upcoming patchnotes accompanying the launch of Rogue Frontier.

[h3]Smuggler Activities and Challenges[/h3]
The Rogue Frontier update introduces the [b]Smuggler Faction[/b] to the Outlands, giving solo players and smaller guilds new opportunities to earn Might and Favor by freeing captured smugglers and recovering crates from ambushed wagons.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/275895a4059e4c2e3fdf0b547f82ecb3ae2a934f.jpeg[/img]

These activities contribute to a new [b]Guild Challenge[/b] category, offering fresh opportunities for guild members to support their teams.

[h3]Get Ready for the Action[/h3]
Guild Seasons lie at the heart of Albion's competitive scene, where guilds vie for territories, Season Points, and top rankings. Participating allows you to contribute to your guild’s success through diverse activities – even if PvP isn’t your focus, there are plenty of ways to help secure rewards and climb the ranks. Ready to get started? Use the [url=https://albiononline.com/guides/article/Guild-Finder+106][b]Guild Finder[/b][/url] to connect with a guild and embark on your journey to guild glory.

These changes promise a faster, action-packed season, keeping the competition intense and every moment engaging. Good luck, and may your efforts lead your guild to glory. See you on the battlefield!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Introducing Rogue Frontier
notes.content:
In this [b]Dev Talk[/b], Game Director [b]Robin Henkys[/b] and Co-Creative Director [b]Michael Schwahn [/b]introduce [b]Rogue Frontier[/b], Albion Online’s next major update, coming this February. This update builds on the [b]Outlands[/b] focus from Horizons by introducing new solo and small-scale features, and brings the highly requested [b]Bank Overview[/b]. Let’s dive into the highlights:

[previewyoutube=dUz6k8x-hwE?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Find your New Home in the Outlands[/h3]
[b]Smuggler’s Dens[/b] are safe hubs for you to set as home and fast travel
[list]	[*]Ideal for solo and small-scale adventurers looking to set up base in the Outlands[/*]	[*]Outlands Banks will be phased out in favor of these new zones[/*]	[*]Fast travel with gear is not possible[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/526ba5835388a3ba9195cc4ddf62cfe1932be0ef.jpeg[/img]

[list]	[*]Connects all Dens and Outlands Rests markets[/*]	[*]Trading fees are based on distance between markets[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/53761989f4c7d19625fe495bebc0413d961cc3c4.jpeg[/img]

[h3]The Smuggler Faction[/h3]
Engage with [b]Smuggler Faction Activities[/b] designed for small groups and solo players:
[list]	[*][b]Secure crates[/b] from ambushed wagons and deliver them to Hidden Smuggler Stashes	[list]		[*]Crates can be carried one at a time and disappear quickly[/*]		[*]Multiple stash locations prevent drop-off camping[/*]		[*]Designed for swift small-group tactics, limiting the dominance of large guilds[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*]Free [b]captured Smugglers[/b] from Royal Guards[/*]	[*]Collect [b]Smuggler Coins[/b] from Hidden Treasures and Coffers[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1c79ae751b0779d733bc12985dddaadd77e22b33.jpeg[/img]

Complete these activities and boost your [b]Smuggler Faction Standing[/b] for exclusive rewards:
[list]	[*]The [b]Smuggler Vanity Set[/b] lets you proudly display your allegiance[/*]	[*]The [b]Smuggler Cape[/b] features the Hidden Vial ability, which reduces potion cooldowns by 90 seconds[/*][/list][h3]Bank Improvements[/h3][list]	[*]View and search personal and guild bank tabs [b]remotely[/b] from the [b]Bank Overview[/b][/*]	[*]Access corresponding city banks directly [b]from personal islands[/b][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c8f0592b89a6131707edfe9661515befe9e2031c.jpeg[/img]

Don’t miss the [b]next Dev Talk[/b] video to learn about even more features coming with[b] Rogue Frontier[/b], including new Crystal Weapons, Resource Wisps, Kill Trophies, and a new Journal category. See you then!

notes.title: Explore Albion’s Rogue Frontier
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a47c46c8bc3fb15cc8355ab6f4926ad87236a462.jpeg[/img]

On [b]February 3[/b], the[b] Rogue Frontier[/b] update brings Albion Online into a daring new era. At its heart lurk the [b]Smugglers[/b], a new faction that has risen in the chaos of the Outlands. Their covert dens offer sanctuary and opportunity, while their market network weaves a clandestine web of trade. This update calls adventurers to seize fortune in the shadows – will you dare to answer?

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a3fc2205378d63522878ede1c9a00bcda7e64e10.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Secrets of the Smugglers[/h3]
Beneath the Outlands lie [b]Smuggler’s Dens[/b] – hidden refuges providing city amenities, fresh activities, and access to the [b]Smuggler Markets[/b]. These dens offer solo and small-scale adventurers a means to set up base, while the [b]Smuggler’s Network[/b] acts as a shadowy Outlands marketplace that rewards resourcefulness and cunning. [b]Smuggler Faction Activities[/b] offer a new layer of intrigue: rescue captured smugglers, deliver rare Smuggler Crates, and hunt for Smuggler’s Coins to build your standing with the faction. Meanwhile, the enigmatic trader Maggy Slade offers [b]exclusive rewards[/b], including the Smuggler’s Cape and a brand-new vanity set. Chaos breeds opportunity for those bold enough to grasp it.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/be1b21dba661590148fc51b868c101eac4d0b60a.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Trophies of Triumph[/h3]
Immortalize your PvP victories with all-new [b]Kill Trophies[/b]. Showing off the details of your triumph, these can be displayed for your allies to admire and to make your rivals tremble. Meanwhile, three [b]new Crystal Weapons[/b] – the Rotcaller Staff, Skystrider Bow, and Forcepulse Bracers – bring devastating new abilities to the battlefield. The artifacts needed to craft them are rewarded from the current Guild Season, meaning adventurers can wield these powerful armaments as soon as Rogue Frontier launches.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/741c4e0e0ef3162074db305854796cffeb05a901.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Beyond the Shadows[/h3]
With the new opportunities opened up by the Smugglers, staying organized has never been more critical. A new [b]Bank Overview[/b] streamlines inventory management across personal and guild storage, allowing players to track their possessions from anywhere in one convenient UI. A new Albion Journal category, [b]Creatures[/b], introduces a bestiary challenge, encouraging players to hunt the realm’s wildlife and earn unique vanity items, signifying mastery over Albion’s most fearsome beasts. And [b]new varieties of Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b] create fresh opportunities for Albion’s intrepid gatherers.

With all this and more, [b]Rogue Frontier[/b] adds thrilling new depths to Albion. Step boldly into this shadowy world on [b]February 3[/b] and stake your claim to its riches. For more details, visit the official update page [url=https://albiononline.com/update/rogue-frontier][b]here[/b][/url].

tags.feature: - On [b]February 3[/b], the[b] Rogue Frontier[/b] update brings Albion Online into a daring new era. At its heart lurk the [b]Smugglers[/b], a new faction that has risen in the chaos of the Outlands. Their covert dens offer sanctuary and opportunity, while their market network weaves a clandestine web of trade. This update calls adventurers to seize fortune in the shadows – will you dare to answer?

Beneath the Outlands lie [b]Smuggler’s Dens[/b] – hidden refuges providing city amenities, fresh activities, and access to the [b]Smuggler Markets[/b]. These dens offer solo and small-scale adventurers a means to set up base, while the [b]Smuggler’s Network[/b] acts as a shadowy Outlands marketplace that rewards resourcefulness and cunning. [b]Smuggler Faction Activities[/b] offer a new layer of intrigue: rescue captured smugglers, deliver rare Smuggler Crates, and hunt for Smuggler’s Coins to build your standing with the faction. Meanwhile, the enigmatic trader Maggy Slade offers [b]exclusive rewards[/b], including the Smuggler’s Cape and a brand-new vanity set. Chaos breeds opportunity for those bold enough to grasp it.

Immortalize your PvP victories with all-new [b]Kill Trophies[/b]. Showing off the details of your triumph, these can be displayed for your allies to admire and to make your rivals tremble. Meanwhile, three [b]new Crystal Weapons[/b] – the Rotcaller Staff, Skystrider Bow, and Forcepulse Bracers – bring devastating new abilities to the battlefield. The artifacts needed to craft them are rewarded from the current Guild Season, meaning adventurers can wield these powerful armaments as soon as Rogue Frontier launches.

With the new opportunities opened up by the Smugglers, staying organized has never been more critical. A new [b]Bank Overview[/b] streamlines inventory management across personal and guild storage, allowing players to track their possessions from anywhere in one convenient UI. A new Albion Journal category, [b]Creatures[/b], introduces a bestiary challenge, encouraging players to hunt the realm’s wildlife and earn unique vanity items, signifying mastery over Albion’s most fearsome beasts. And [b]new varieties of Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b] create fresh opportunities for Albion’s intrepid gatherers.

With all this and more, [b]Rogue Frontier[/b] adds thrilling new depths to Albion. Step boldly into this shadowy world on [b]February 3[/b] and stake your claim to its riches. For more details, visit the official update page [url=https://albiononline.com/update/rogue-frontier][b]here[/b][/url].

notes.title: Stride Through Albion’s Winter with the Frost Moose!
notes.content:

[list]	[*][b]Step 1[/b]: Share your referral link with a friend, which you can find [url=https://albiononline.com/profile/referral/overview][b]here[/b][/url] when logged into the website with your game account.[/*]	[*][b]Step 2[/b]: Your friend signs up to Albion Online.[/*]	[*][b]Step 3[/b]: Your friend purchases at least 30 days of Premium status, unlocking your rewards.[/*][/list]This Referral Season ends on [b]January 31[/b] at[b] 23꞉59꞉59 UTC[/b]! notes.title: Leap into the Frost Challenge!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e51fb2f8ee38acfdea10abf16dc950f667f24aac.png[/img]

The [b]Frost Challenge[/b] has stormed into Albion, plunging the land into a deep winter slumber. But it's time to stop counting sheep in your sleep and claim the [b]Frost Ram[/b] instead! Take the reins and let its horns ram enemies aside as it leaps undaunted through icy perils. Brave the frosty wilderness to earn Challenge Points, and charge into baaa-ttle with this woolly champion before winter thaws!

[h3]Frost-Themed Rewards for Intrepid Adventurers[/h3]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f910e0d55dd57fbe2ef6ca625aa1b1b8a9f9e8cc.png[/img]
[b]FROST RAM:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the popular [b]Frost Ram[/b], a sturdy mount with an impressive leap spell. With its relatively fast move speed and ability to carry plenty of weight, it's the perfect companion for gathering missions.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b81af17ba41ed8b868c2bdf8322f9e6af4b7be86.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Along with the Frost Ram, you can unlock the [b]Frost Challenge Avatar Ring[/b] to give your avatar an ice-cold aura all year long. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or it can be traded for one [b]Adventurer's Token[/b] at the Vanity Merchant.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ee96535737e93e2de301f3612d876986429ec635.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month, unlock Frost Challenge chests to get valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes and Silver bags, along with furniture items like the [b]Snowman[/b] and [b]Snowball Pile[/b], classic [b]ice sculptures[/b], the epic [b]Frost Igloo[/b], and a rare chance for the [b]Rich Noble[/b] vanity skins.

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67596717a19e4_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

notes.title: 2024: Albion’s Year in Review
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/2b2fab512e6017622b74416806cf6b9881090df0.png[/img]

As 2024 winds down, Albion Online stands stronger than ever. From the launch of [b]Albion Europe[/b] to an impressive number of game-changing updates, this year has expanded the boundaries of what's possible in Albion. With a new development cycle delivering focused changes every three months, [b]four major updates[/b] have changed the landscape of the game. Let’s relive the biggest moments of 2024!

[h3]Re-envisioning Guild Warfare[/h3]
2024 began with [url=https://albiononline.com/news/crystal-raiders-live][b]Crystal Raiders[/b][/url], shaking up Guild Seasons and introducing new layers of strategy to warfare in the Outlands.This update introduced [b]Territory Raiding[/b], giving smaller groups fresh tactical opportunities, and revamped the [b]Conqueror’s Challenge[/b], offering more pathways to season rewards for both guilds and solo players.

[previewyoutube=th9a8Mu6FWM?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[b]Crystal Weapons[/b] made their debut, adding explosive power and new combat strategies. Nine of these weapons have launched so far, and with more on the way, they will continue to bring further possibilities to the battlefield.

[h3]Laying the Groundwork[/h3]
Building on the vision for guild warfare introduced with Crystal Raiders, the [url=https://albiononline.com/news/foundations-is-live][b]Foundations[/b][/url] update took things a step further. With [b]Fortifications[/b] allowing guilds to bolster their territory defenses, and [b]Siege Banners[/b] providing attackers with new ways to counter them, this update added new tactical dimensions to guild battles.

[previewyoutube=vTj-NaMx4gs?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
The update also introduced [b]Territory Activity Chests[/b], from which guilds can earn valuable rewards through their activities. However, rivals can raid them to steal the spoils, adding another layer of depth to territory conflict. Overall, Foundations set the stage for even more strategic and engaging guild warfare for seasons to come.

[h3]A Global Expansion[/h3]
In April, Albion Online launched [url=https://albiononline.com/news/albion-europe-live][b]Albion Europe[/b][/url], a server tailored to players in the Europe and MENA regions. This offered players a fresh start, and brought improved connection speeds and optimized event timings, along with language support for Turkish and Arabic.

[previewyoutube=xPyw4nZlGNA?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
The [url=https://albiononline.com/news/record-player-numbers][b]results[/b][/url] were staggering: daily active users surpassed [b]350,000 by May 1[/b], breaking the previous record by over 50,000! With more than 150,000 daily players on Albion Europe alone, this was one of the game’s most momentous expansions.

[h3]Writing Your Legend[/h3]
Following the launch of Albion Europe, [url=https://albiononline.com/news/paths-to-glory-live][b]Paths to Glory[/b][/url] introduced the [b]Albion Journal[/b], a personal log for chronicling player adventures. Divided into [b]categories[/b] focused on distinct areas of the game, it provides guidance for new adventurers and challenges veterans with fresh objectives to master. Missions grant [b]themed rewards[/b] for each category, including exclusive mount skins and vanity items with dazzling effects to show off your achievements.

[previewyoutube=1EvSkwrsGXk?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
Dedicated adventurers are already flaunting these rewards, and new categories will continue to appear in future updates, ensuring challenges remain plentiful for a long time to come.

[h3]Transforming the Open World[/h3]
The year closed with [url=https://albiononline.com/news/horizons-live][b]Horizons[/b][/url], which brought tougher PvE challenges and reward scaling to reignite the excitement of battle, and quality-of-life enhancements like the [b]HUD Editor [/b]gave players greater control over their gameplay experience.

[previewyoutube=_zw91Vj29nc?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
But at the heart of this transformative update was the revitalization of Albion's open world. [b]Dynamic Encampments[/b], [b]Boss Lairs[/b], and [b]Crystal Creatures[/b] brought new opportunities, while [b]S.A.F.E. Portals[/b] were added to offer solo players quick access to the deeper reaches of the Outlands. With this, Horizons set the stage for yet more developments coming to the Outlands with our next update...

[h3]Looking Ahead to 2025[/h3]
Phew! That was a busy year! And as we look back at the year that’s passed, we're re-evaluating our [b]development cycle[/b]. Beginning with Season 26, [b]Guild Seasons[/b] will move to a two-month format, with [b]major updates arriving every four months[/b].

[previewyoutube=NYly30z8Duk?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
The [b]next update[/b] will build on what Horizons started, bringing new objectives and shady trading opportunities to the Outlands, as well as a new Journal category, and much more. Stay tuned for more on that very soon!

In the meantime, let's give a shout out to our incredible community; your passion and dedication have propelled Albion to new heights. Here's to the next chapter!

notes.title: Find Uncle Frost to Claim Holiday Treasures
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3ee9c90fad019090e36179bad72ffdb7c0719b05.png[/img]

‘Tis the time for snowballs in people’s faces and fireworks in the skies. The Yuletide season is here, and Albion is once again under the cold thumb of the one and only [b]Uncle Frost[/b]. Down in the dungeons, the bearded giant is spreading chaos – and loot!

[h3]Find Uncle Frost and Reap the Rewards![/h3]
Uncle Frost has set up camp again in a selection of[b] T4-T8 Solo and Group Randomized Dungeons[/b]. Keep an eye out for a holiday-themed boss room – when you see it, Uncle Frost will be waiting to greet you with his usual icy disposition.

Defeat him and you could walk away with festive treasures like [b]Uncle Frost’s hat[/b], [b]decorated pine trees[/b], [b]snowballs[/b], or even the ultra-rare [b]Yule Stag mount skin[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dd3ad1c011e4013ce34a7b891fd472eeac2af504.png[/img]

The mischief runs for [b]the following times[/b] on each server:
[list]	[*][b]Albion Asia[/b]: December 19 at 23 UTC - January 5 at 23 UTC[/*]	[*][b]Albion Americas[/b] and [b]Albion Europe[/b]: December 20 at 10 UTC - January 6 at 10 UTC[/*][/list]But the fun doesn’t stop there! Simply log in during the event to receive [b]seasonal gifts [/b]via ingame mail:
[list]	[*]5 fireworks in green, red, and yellow[/*]	[*]50 snowballs to settle scores the holiday way[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7637238d533cfddb74aade728704aaab304fd77e.png[/img]

Grab your gear, brave the snow-filled dungeons, and show Uncle Frost who’s boss! Happy Yuletide, adventurers!

notes.title: Dev Talk: 2024 In Review
notes.content:
Another year is almost over, and it’s been a busy one for Albion Online, with four content updates bringing numerous new features and improvements to the game. With so much having happened, Game Director [b]Robin Henkys[/b], Co-Creative Director [b]Michael Schwahn[/b], and Head of Production [b]Moritz Bokelmann[/b] took a moment to recap the game’s development over the past twelve months and look ahead to what’s in store for 2025.

[previewyoutube=NYly30z8Duk?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h3]Crystal Raiders[/h3]
2024 kicked off with the [b]Crystal Raiders[/b] update:

[b]Paths to Glory[/b] introduced a new achievement system: the [b]Albion Journal[/b]:
[list]	[*]This serves two main functions:	[list]		[*]Guides [b]new players[/b] through features, and encourages [b]older players[/b] to try new activities[/*]		[*]Provides tangible goals for each feature of the game[/*]	[/list][/*]	[*][b]Unique vanity items[/b] reward progress	[list]		[*]These are [b]non-tradable[/b], so act as a genuine mark of achievement[/*]	[/list][/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/fb14b20e5a9e82f42ca198a9542055397fb91892.jpeg[/img]

This update also overhauled the Roads of Avalon:
[list]	[*]Activities and rewards were [b]rebalanced[/b][/*]	[*]New activities were added, like [b]Tracking[/b][/*]	[*]As a result, activity in the Roads has increased significantly[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/182a5e794ec3c608213471cc14c27124aa0434e8.jpeg[/img]

Portals[/b] transport solo players to random locations in the Outlands[/*][/list][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7be72f2174df1694eb441b1c1a1724a3273f2002.jpeg[/img]

notes.title: Spread the Joy and Claim Your Yuletide Yak
notes.content:
Refer a friend this winter season, the [b]Yuletide Yak [/b]is all the reason! With a jingle bell hat and gifts in its sack, this jolly steed will have your back. Unlock this mount with festive fervor, for all your characters on that server!

notes.title: The Yuletide Challenge Brings Holiday Magic!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/887c6acfa5693e983b7f066b5da3544661037ab4.jpeg[/img]

It’s time to celebrate the holidays with the arrival of the [b]Yuletide Challenge[/b]! Tireless and true, the [b]Snow Husky [/b]will dash through icy winds and snowdrifts for you. With its fluffy fur keeping you warm on long winter nights, this good boy is the perfect companion for a season of triumphs and festive cheer. Let the Yuletide spirit guide your journey as you earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] this month to unlock this and other festive rewards!

[h3]Yuletide Greetings[/h3]
[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9ddc23c30b8fa56077944e0f5f3a72c8eeda3e83.png[/img]

SNOW HUSKY:[/b] You've got another chance to claim the charming [b]Snow Husky[/b], a handsome canine companion that will carry you through Albion's harshest terrain. Along with its strong base move speed, its Hunting Instinct spell gives a short but powerful speed burst.
 

[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/aa747399b53699a7bd2eed5c6be3d296d1e4439c.png[/img]

AVATAR RING:[/b] Along with the Snow Husky, adventurers who reach this month's total point goal will unlock the [b]Yuletide Challenge Ring[/b], which gives your avatar a cheery holiday look any time of year. And remember: unclaimed Adventurer's Challenge Rings can always be traded in for Adventurer's Tokens at the Vanity Merchant!
 

[b][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0f7030ae6ea3d3c0e75a7faa62b51498bb55d887.png[/img]

SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] Unlock Yuletide Challenge chests to get a mix of holiday-themed prizes, along with goodies like Silver, Tomes of Insight, treasures and resources. Each chest has a chance to give classic Yuletide decorations like [b]Presents [/b]and [b]Decorated Trees[/b] as well as the [b]Yuletide Candle, Wreath, Lantern,[/b] and[b] Candy Boot[/b]!

 
[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/6749980a8fbd1_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

notes.title: Changelog: Horizons Patch 2
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch makes some adjustments to features introduced with the Horizons update, along with combat balancing and some other important changes and fixes.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Season 24 Winner Statues Unveiled[/h3]

The statues to honor the winners of Season 24 are now viewable in each server’s Conqueror’s Hall. Congratulations to the triumphant guilds!

[h3]New Boss Lairs[/h3]

The Boss Lairs introduced with the Horizons update have been revamped, with new layouts and visuals that better communicate their status as a faction boss hideout.[list]	[*]There is now a new Boss Lair for each faction (Undead, Heretic, Morgana)[/*]	[*]The +200% loot bonus for Boss Lairs has been removed, but now there are 3 chests instead of 1[/*]	[*]Each Boss Lair now contains only the boss, and no other mobs[/*]	[*]Their entrances in the open world have been modified slightly[/*][/list]
[h3]Territory Raiding Changes[/h3][list]	[*]Once a banner has been dropped and channeled, the time until it is destroyed has been reduced from 5 minutes to 3 minutes[/*]	[*]Raid Banners can no longer be used to raid a territory if an older Raid Banner is already active there, or if two banners are spawned simultaneously	[list]		[*]In order to raid a territory with your own banner, older Raid Banners must first be destroyed[/*]		[*]Raid Banners that need to be destroyed first are visually distinguished on the minimap[/*]		[*]If two Raid Banners are raised within 30 seconds of each other, one must be destroyed before the other can be used to raid[/*]		[*]Raid Banners that are raised later on in the battle cannot be used to prevent raiding[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Mob Combat Changes[/h3][list]	[*]Spells and combat behavior have been updated for a number of mobs[/*]	[*]Out-of-combat status in PvE now begins when the mob is killed, rather than when its corpse disappears[/*][/list]
[h3]Other Changes[/h3][list]	[*]As a followup to our Solo Dynamic Encampment loot increases in Patch 1, Group Dynamic Encampments now award less Fame and Objective progress to players if they are solo or in very small groups	[list]		[*]Our intent with this, along with the changes in Patch 1, is to create rewarding gameplay loops both for solo players in Solo Encampments, and for group players in Group Encampments[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Mini roaming mob camps in the open world no longer spawn around World Bosses[/*]	[*]Equipping food or potions now puts all spells on a 10 second cooldown[/*]	[*]Enchantment Level 4 Treasure Resources are now more likely to unlock at Prime Time, rather than spawning at Prime Time and unlocking later[/*]	[*]Certain items are now less expensive to Journey Back or use a S.A.F.E. Portal with	[list]		[*]This mostly affects Randomized Dungeon Maps and Player Island furniture[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]The radius of the Crystal Beetle’s ‘Magical Discharge’ spell has been significantly increased[/*]	[*]Hostile player count in safe regions now only counts players explicitly flagged as hostile, not unflagged players in open PvP areas[/*]	[*]Guild Codexes (guilds’ internal descriptions) can now be edited by any member with the ‘Change Guild Logo’ permission[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Axes[/b][list]	[*]Relentless Assault (Crystal Reaper)	[list]		[*]Leaving the area does not end the spell[/*]		[*]Hitting enemies while outside of the area does not reduce weapon ability cooldowns[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Holy Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Sanctify (Exalted Staff)	[list]		[*]Cast Range: 8m → 10m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Nature Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Soul Link (Ironroot Staff)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 12s[/*]		[*]Energy cost: 18% → 11%[/*]		[*]Duration: 7s → 5s[/*]		[*]Ally/ally effect:		[list]			[*]Healing shared: 100% → 50%[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Ally/enemy effect:		[list]			[*]Enemy healing redirected to ally: 30% → 50%[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Casting both parts on the same target now resets its cooldown[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Circle of Life (Nature Staff)	[list]		[*]Max targets: 5 → 10[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Quarterstaffs[/b][list]	[*]Soul Shaker (Grailseeker)	[list]		[*]Area duration: 3.5s → 4s[/*]		[*]Multicast time window: 3s → 5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shapeshifter Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Werewolf Transformation (Bloodmoon Staff)	[list]		[*]Bloody Roar lifesteal: 6% -] 8% (while below 40% health)		[list]			[*]Lifesteal is now only triggered by Werewolf form abilities[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Distortion (all Shapeshifter Staffs)	[list]		[*]Damage per tick: 54 → 48[/*]		[*]No longer reflectable[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Sinister Swipes (Prowling Staff)	[list]		[*]Range: 4m → 5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Spirit Bear Transformation (Primal Staff)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 5s → 10s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Tether Shift (all Shapeshifter Staffs)	[list]		[*]Dash now applies a shield to yourself which absorbs 200 damage for 1.5s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Helmets[/b][list]	[*]Ice Block (Cleric Cowl)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 60s → 90s[/*]		[*]Removed 50% healing debuff while frozen[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shoes[/b][list]	[*]Dodge (all Shoes)	[list]		[*]Added immunity to transformation[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Capes[/b][list]	[*]Devious Trap (Heretic Cape)	[list]		[*]Trap hit delay: 0.8s → 0.4s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Energy Reserve (Lymhurst Cape)	[list]		[*]Energy restoration: 80% → 70%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Battle Mounts[/b][list]	[*]Healing Sapling (Ancient Ent)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 4s → 3s[/*]		[*]Radius: 2.5m → 4m[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Ent's Blessing (Ancient Ent)	[list]		[*]Can no longer be interrupted[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]

[b]Albion Journal fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where the mission ‘Raise all different types of animals’ could not be completed because it required an obsolete animal[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the mission ‘Knock down another player in a Yellow Zone’ could be completed by knocking down oneself with self-damaging spells[/*][/list]
[b]Spell fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where Avalanche (Hoarfrost Staff) could knock-up targets with forced movement immunity[/*][/list]

[b]UI fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where player count display would sometimes fail to update immediately after changing regions[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where player nametags would sometimes fail to display in safe regions[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where gathering tooltips would not scale correctly with window size[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where chat window size would reset after saving HUD changes[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the Bandit Assault countdown would remain on the World Map after changing servers[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where, after an Arena battle, the Player Stats UI would open under the Arena Stats UI when clicking a player’s avatar[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where some UI elements would not function correctly after entering a Randomized Dungeon[/*]	[*]Various fixes and improvements made to the Travel Planner UI[/*][/list]
[b]Other fixes[/b][list]	[*]Fixed issue where some mobs in the Hardcore Expedition ‘Fistful of Silver’ had higher resistances than intended[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where Mists Encampments could sometimes contain mobs that did not count towards completing the quest[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where some Resource Guardians would grant too little Fame[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where rerolling an item’s quality would sometimes incorrectly state that the player’s inventory is full[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where saved frame rate settings would not be applied immediately after starting the game[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where the Forgotten General mob would perform a slide after its auto-attacks[/*]	[*]Fixed issue where guild logos on the ground of Guild Islands would appear mirrored[/*]	[*][MOBILE] Fixed issue where emotes could not be used with custom hotkeys[/*][/list]

notes.title: Changelog: Horizons Patch 1
notes.content:
[quote][i]This patch focuses on making adjustments to new features introduced with the Horizons update, along with important fixes to a few gameplay issues.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Changes[/h3]

[b]Alternate Mount-up[/b][list]	[*]Running back to a mount when using the Mount ability in the half-mounted radius is now available as a toggle option	[list]		[*]This new option can be found in the ‘General’ section of the settings menu[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Crystal Creatures Changes[/b][list]	[*]Crystal Cobra: Some abilities have had their damage and potency reduced[/*]	[*]Crystal Beetle: The Lightning Strike ability has had its duration and frequency reduced[/*][/list]
[b]Journal Changes[/b][list]	[*]The Journal mission ‘Your voice sounds familiar…’ has been renamed ‘Talk to yourself…’ and its reward has been adjusted:	[list]		[*]200 Ghost Victory Emote Charges → Master’s Tome of Insight[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Dynamic Encampment Adjustments[/b][list]	[*]Based on feedback, mobs in Encampments no longer have a Fame penalty, resulting in a significant increase in Fame gained per mob    	[list]		[*]Fame required to complete the objective has been increased proportionally to match the new values[/*]		[*]To mitigate the risk of creating extremely powerful Fame farms, Fame can no longer be gained from mobs after the objective has been completed or if the player is outside the Encampment area[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Tomes of Insight have been removed from Uncommon, Rare, and Legendary Caches to partially offset the increase in Fame[/*]	[*]Common Caches continue to reward the majority of their Tomes of Insight, but at a slightly reduced value	[list]		[*]Common Caches have been renamed to ‘Common Tome Caches’ to highlight their primary reward[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]As a result of Fame increases, Might conversions have increased accordingly	[list]		[*]To partially offset this, the Might rewarded for completing the objective has been reduced[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]These changes result in an overall buff to the Fame gained from Encampments[/*]	[*]The changes above also apply to Mists Camps[/*]	[*]Solo Caches in Open World Dynamic Encampments have had their loot values (excluding Tomes of Insight) substantially increased[/*][/list]

tags.feature: Running back to a mount when using the Mount ability in the half-mounted radius is now available as a toggle option

tags.balance_change: Crystal Cobra: Some abilities have had their damage and potency reduced
Crystal Beetle: The Lightning Strike ability has had its duration and frequency reduced
200 Ghost Victory Emote Charges → Master’s Tome of Insight
Based on feedback, mobs in Encampments no longer have a Fame penalty, resulting in a significant increase in Fame gained per mob
Fame required to complete the objective has been increased proportionally to match the new values
To mitigate the risk of creating extremely powerful Fame farms, Fame can no longer be gained from mobs after the objective has been completed or if the player is outside the Encampment area
Tomes of Insight have been removed from Uncommon, Rare, and Legendary Caches to partially offset the increase in Fame
Common Caches continue to reward the majority of their Tomes of Insight, but at a slightly reduced value
As a result of Fame increases, Might conversions have increased accordingly

notes.title: The Grim Challenge Creeps Back
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/ec1560b9441b828936377c59c79adf7e38cc0ecf.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Grim Challenge[/b] has risen, and with it a dark presence flickers its tongue, searching for its next victim – the poisonous [b]Pest Lizard[/b] is slithering from its tomb, leaving a trail of venom in its wake! By earning [b]Challenge Points[/b] through open-world activities, you can claim this toxic mount and other sinister rewards. Rise to the challenge and claim them before they crawl back into their crypt!

[h3]Pestilential Prizes For Intrepid Adventurers[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/37098394fc221f53b22942d5c2018a17b86b1dca.png[/img]

[b]PEST LIZARD: [/b]This month's Challenge offers another chance to claim the popular [b]Pest Lizard[/b]. This sleek, slithery mount comes with a [b]Toxic Cloud[/b] ability that causes enemies who touch it to become temporarily disoriented, and can be used to disrupt enemy players in numerous situations.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/fd248429c8bb16fadb892cc6075439f63762bd27.png[/img]

[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Grim Challenge Avatar Ring[/b], featuring a spooky skull-topped iron frame. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Adventurer's Token.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b4e8429d41f50d3444dd5beab0bf7fc0a7f824ca.png[/img]

[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly point totals to unlock [b]Grim Challenge Chests[/b]. Along with valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver, resources, and other loot, you'll also have a chance to unlock four furniture items: the [b]Empty Coffin, Grim Gravestone, Grim Lantern, [/b]and[b] Weeping Woman Statue.[/b]

[video autoplay="yes" loop="yes" muted="yes"]https://assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/video_/media/67211fc695427_720.mp4[/video]

[h3]How to participate in the Adventurer's Challenge[/h3]
The [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] is a monthly event where you can earn [b]exclusive rewards[/b] such as mounts, Tomes of Insight, bags of Silver, and more. By [b]gathering, fishing, farming, [/b]and[b] defeating monsters, [/b]you'll earn [b]Challenge Points[/b] that fill daily, weekly, and monthly progress bars. To track your progress, open the Adventurer's Challenge UI by clicking on the [b]Activities menu[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/bbe632b8c242dd9526c11b8d54741acce88fee5a.png[/img]

While only [b]Premium[/b] players can unlock the [b]Monthly Rewards [/b](Avatar Ring, Mount) and [b]Weekly Rewards[/b] (Challenge Chests), anyone can claim the [b]Daily Rewards[/b], which include 10 Learning Points and a Tier 4 Tome of Insight. Non-Premium players also make progress on all reward tracks, so when you’re ready to unlock Premium, your earned rewards will be waiting for you!

notes.title: Horizons is Live!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/6d6512b0d8a42cfd90374f633a7e10ab01235d0a.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Horizons[/b] are open! Today sees Albion’s latest update arrive, bringing with it improved [b]open-world gameplay[/b], some huge new [b]UI features[/b], new [b]Albion Journal[/b] categories, and much more. And, as always, there’s a fresh [b]trailer [/b]to boot. Check it out here:

[previewyoutube=_zw91Vj29nc?rel=0;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]Unexpected Encounters[/h3]
Horizons brings some brand-new features to Albion’s open world. [b]Dynamic Encampments[/b] are mob camps which appear in random locations for a limited time, offering loot, Might, and Favor to those who can complete them. And other shifting, unexpected objectives are appearing too: [b]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b] which offer a wealth of resources for a short time, [b]Coffers[/b] which offer rewards to those who find them, and [b]Lair Maps[/b] which provide access to a hidden Boss Lair. With these unpredictable objectives springing up, exploring the open world has new layers of depth, interest, and chance.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e8ed1561f5175f13a1d7743773f2b4b4071f4530.png[/img]

[h3]S.A.F.E. Travels[/h3]
Albion’s inventors have been hard at work, and by reverse-engineering Avalonian technology have developed the new [b]S.A.F.E Portal[/b]. This transports solo players from Portal Towns into unpredictable Outlands locations, offering a means to venture into Albion’s deepest regions. At the same time, the Outlands now increase in [b]difficulty and rewards[/b] the higher the region quality, encouraging exploration of their less-trodden areas. New Crystal Creatures – the [b]Crystal Beetle[/b] and [b]Crystal Cobra[/b] – roam the Outlands, providing frightening new objectives for groups. And the Royal Continent now has [b]Tier 5 Blue Zones[/b] and [b]Tier 6 Yellow Zones[/b], proving more valuable content before players enter the deadlier regions.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7e917bacb2a516d36dd0b411eb237bf6aa771b4d.png[/img]

[h3]Freedom at your Fingertips[/h3]
The [b]HUD Editor[/b] provides players with unprecedented control over their display, with the ability to adjust the size, scale and opacity of different elements, and move them around freely. These custom layouts can be saved and shared, and [b]Quick Settings Presets[/b] allow them to be assigned to a hotkey and switched for different gameplay scenarios. [b]Inventories[/b] now have adjustable icon sizes, a collapsible equipment display, and new sorting options, allowing far greater flexibility. And [b]Banks and Chests[/b] have improved UIs, too, with optimizations like the ability to repair items from within Banks.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e958fbf88f0370577185446eab6f99024d303ec0.png[/img]

With all this and more – like two brand-new [b]Albion Journal[/b] categories – there’s so much to explore across the Horizons. For the full patchnotes, click [url=https://albiononline.com/changelog/horizons-update][b]here[/b][/url].

And if you want to see what’s new as soon as the update launches, our AOCP Ambassadors are exploring the new content on Twitch today! For more information, click [url=https://albiononline.com/news/horizons-launch-streams][b]here[/b][/url].

notes.title: Changelog: Horizons Update
notes.content:
[quote][i]Horizons reinvigorates the open world with a more dynamic, rewarding, and accessible gameplay experience, as well as enhanced PvE challenges. It also introduces significant quality-of-life improvements, new customization options, and two new Albion Journal categories.[/i][/quote]
[h3]New Open World Objectives[/h3]

New dynamic objectives appear for a limited time across the open world, cycling through active and inactive phases. Players must explore the world to uncover these areas while they're active, as they reveal themselves only when closely approached.

[b]Dynamic Encampments[/b]

Dynamic Encampments are temporary camps settled by mobs from each Faction, who protect valuable Caches:[list]	[*]These Encampments come in two sizes: Solo for individual players, and Group for parties of about 5 players[/*]	[*]Approaching an active Encampment activates a quest for the player or party that finds it, to earn a certain amount of Fame from clearing its mobs:	[list]		[*]Fame requirements scale with an Encampment’s tier and region type		[list]			[*]Quest progress is not affected by Premium or Fame bonuses[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Party progress is shared, as long as members stay within the camp's vicinity		[list]			[*]Fame is divided among party members, meaning larger groups will need to defeat more mobs to complete the quest[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Once a quest has been started, you can leave the region and return to the camp within 60 minutes without losing your progress, provided the camp hasn’t gone inactive[/*]		[*]Camps in Yellow and Red Zones are unrestricted PvP areas[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Clearing an Encampment rewards the player or party with access to a Cache containing valuable loot, as well as Might and Favor	[list]		[*]Loot distribution and rarity is instanced for each player[/*]		[*]If unclaimed, loot is automatically removed from these Caches 10 minutes after a camp is completed[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]When a camp becomes inactive, all mobs, map markers, caches, and quest progress are immediately removed[/*][/list]
[b]Lair Maps[/b]

Lair Maps can spawn in mob camps - including Dynamic Encampments - giving players the chance to uncover a hidden Boss Lair belonging to the corresponding Faction:[list]	[*]These maps are unlocked by defeating Faction mobs within a radius around them, independent of the Dynamic Encampment’s quest[/*]	[*]Boss Lairs correspond to the size of the camp, whether solo or group	[list]		[*]Solo Lair Maps have a higher spawn rate in Solo Dynamic Encampments than in other open-world mob camps[/*]		[*]Group Lair Maps only spawn in Group Encampments[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Once a player interacts with the map, it disappears for everyone else[/*]	[*]Defeating the Lair’s Boss unlocks an additional chest, with its rarity only revealed once completed[/*][/list]
[b]Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/b]

A significantly higher density of resources now spawn in certain areas of the open world for a limited time, shifting locations on a daily basis.     

[b]Open World Coffers[/b]

New Coffers, similar to those found in the Mists, now spawn across the open world. These have a short unlock timer, offering quick opportunities for those nearby during their active phase.

[b]Further Notes[/b]

Hideouts and furniture cannot be placed where open world objectives may appear[list]	[*]Characters, Hideouts, and furniture will be removed from these areas when the update goes live:	[list]		[*]Characters and Hideouts, along with all their contents, will be automatically relocated[/*]		[*]Guilds are able to move their Hideouts for free for up to three days after relocation[/*]		[*]Furniture in the open world will be destroyed[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Outlands Changes[/h3]

[b]S.A.F.E. Portals[/b]

S.A.F.E. Portals can now be found in the Portal Towns of the Outlands, offering solo players a quick teleport to random locations within the Outlands. These portals provide a convenient way to reach the new dynamic objectives in higher-tier regions.[list]	[*]Destinations are random within each Portal Town's assigned section of the Outlands, with no overlap between S.A.F.E. Portal ranges:	[list]		[*]A map overlay highlights the portal’s assigned region, making it easy to identify the destination range[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Portal use requires a fee:	[list]		[*]This fee increases with each subsequent use within a limited time to discourage players from fishing for specific locations[/*]		[*]After using any S.A.F.E. Portal, there is a 30 second cooldown before another portal can be opened[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*] Personal portal mechanics:	[list]		[*]After paying the fee, the player is teleported instantly and appears through a personal S.A.F.E. Portal, receiving a region change protection bubble upon arrival[/*]		[*]The personal S.A.F.E. Portal location is indicated exclusively on the owner’s world and region maps, but it is visible in the game world when the owner is nearby[/*]		[*]The personal S.A.F.E. Portal remains open for 90 minutes, providing enough time for exploration and a safer, instant teleport back to the originating Portal City[/*]		[*]Using the personal S.A.F.E. Portal to return to the Portal City is free[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]S.A.F.E. Portals close under the following conditions:	[list]		[*]Its duration expires[/*]		[*]It is used to return[/*]		[*]The player dies, uses Journey Back, or travels to another safe location[/*]		[*]The player collects any items from containers or performs trades with another player[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Region Difficulty and Reward Modifiers[/b]

Rewards and mob power now increase progressively based on region quality, making higher-quality regions more challenging and rewarding:[list]	[*]There is now a bonus to gathering and fishing Fame in the Outlands, based on the quality of the Region[/*]	[*]Fame from gathering, fishing, and defeating mobs, as well as Silver and loot from mobs and chests, all scale higher towards the center of the Outlands[/*]	[*]Mobs have increased health and damage in higher-quality regions	[list]		[*]This does not apply to resource and territory mobs (such as Hide Animals and Territory Guards)[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Outlands region maps now include a dropdown with information showing reward bonuses and mob strength modifiers[/*][/list]
[b]Outlands Player Count Indicator[/b]

A new player count indicator has been added to Outlands regions, offering a rough estimate of the number of players present.
[quote][i]This feature helps smaller groups gauge the presence of larger groups, allowing players to engage in fights of a more appropriate scale with increased confidence. We will closely monitor the impact of this addition.[/i][/quote]
[h3]Other Open World Changes[/h3]

[b]Royal Continent Changes[/b][list]	[*]Some Tier 6 regions can now be found in Yellow Zones, and some Tier 5 regions in Blue Zones, giving players access to a broader range of content before stepping into full-loot PvP zones[/*][/list][quote][i]These changes are carefully balanced with the new Region Modifier system and the increased availability of Dynamic Resource Hotspots in full-loot PvP zones, ensuring the high-end economy remains intact while still offering more content for newer or risk-averse players.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Tier 7 resources now spawn in Tier 7 Red Zones[/*][/list]
[b]Other Changes[/b][list]	[*]Kill details are now suppressed for 5 minutes for everyone except the killer and the victim[/*]	[*]During a region’s Prime Time, the Next Activity Chest Value overlay now displays the current chest value instead of the upcoming one[/*]	[*]The value of Hidden Treasures has been increased by roughly 400%[/*][/list]
[h3]Mob Power Changes[/h3]

[quote][i]Player power has grown with every update, while mobs have lagged behind. This update reworks mob power progression from Tier 5 and up to match current player strength.[/i][/quote][list]	[*]Mobs from Tier 5 and above now receive incremental power boosts, starting with a 9% increase at Tier 5 and 42% by Tier 8[/*]	[*]These adjustments do not apply to:	[list]		[*]Avalonians in the Roads of Avalon[/*]		[*]Tracking targets[/*]		[*]Demons in Hellgates and Corrupted Dungeons[/*]		[*]Elite enemies in Randomized Dungeons and World Boss Areas[/*]		[*]Territory Guards[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]As mob power increases, corresponding rewards (Fame, loot, and Silver) will scale as well to offer more substantial incentives for taking on these tougher foes[/*]	[*]Note that these changes are distinct from the mob power changes mentioned above (in ‘Region Difficulty and Reward Modifiers’)[/*][/list]
[h3]Group Content Changes[/h3]

[quote][i]Albion’s group content is meant to challenge teams, but players have often found it more profitable to farm this content alone. These changes aim to make these activities more rewarding and enjoyable for groups.[/i][/quote]
[b]Reward Changes[/b]

Rewards for most group and raid activities have been adjusted:[list]	[*]Rewards now scale with group size, increasing significantly as more players are involved[/*][/list]
[b]Group Randomized Dungeon Changes[/b][list]	[*]Group Randomized Dungeon entrances now close a short time after a player enters	[list]		[*]Royal Continent: 60 seconds[/*]		[*]Outlands: 90 seconds[/*]		[*]As with Solo Randomized Dungeons, a channel is now required to enter[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Fame and loot rewards for groups of 3 or more players have been increased by approximately 50%[/*][/list]
[b]New Crystal Creatures[/b]

This update introduces two new Crystal Creatures to the Outlands, aimed at groups of about 5 players – the Crystal Beetle and the Crystal Cobra.[list]	[*]Crystal Beetle	[list]		[*]A powerful, winged enemy which can punish its attackers with lightning strikes and magical energy[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Crystal Cobra	[list]		[*]A vicious and intimidating reptile which can spit devastating, poisonous venom[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Crystal Creature Adjustments[/b][list]	[*]All Crystal Creatures, including Crystal Spiders, now spawn much more frequently; their spawn rate is adjusted based on the overall Guild Season point output[/*]	[*]Each individual Crystal Creature now yields less loot and Might, to partially counterbalance their significantly increased frequency	[list]		[*]Loot rewards have been reduced by 56%, and Might by 83%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Crystal Creatures no longer grant Favor, so that their rewards can be more focused on loot[/*]	[*]Crystal Creatures are now only marked on the map when players are nearby[/*][/list]
[h3]Quick Settings Presets[/h3]

Quick Settings Presets allow players to save different configurations of in-game options and instantly switch between them with customizable shortcuts:[list]	[*]Presets can be accessed and managed from the bottom-left corner of the main in-game Settings menu[/*]	[*]Each preset can include settings from the following categories:	[list]		[*]General[/*]		[*]Graphics[/*]		[*]Audio[/*]		[*]Interface (including the new HUD Editor layouts)[/*]		[*]Controls[/*]		[*]Social[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Players can either start a fresh preset, or duplicate an existing one	[list]		[*]A preset can then be customized by modifying settings as needed[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Up to 14 presets can be saved for specific playstyle needs or activities, such as PvP, ZvZ, PvE, or gathering[/*]	[*]Custom names and key bindings can be assigned to each preset for quick switching[/*]	[*]Presets can be exported to share with friends, guildmates, or other players[/*][/list]
[h3]HUD Editor[/h3]

The new HUD Editor allows players on both mobile and desktop to fully customize nearly all aspects of their in-game interface, allowing for a highly customizable experience tailored to individual needs and playstyles.

[b]Customization Options[/b][list]	[*]The HUD Editor can be opened from the ‘Interface’ section of the in-game settings menu[/*]	[*]When entering the Editor, all HUD elements are highlighted on the screen, even those not currently active[/*]	[*]Players can freely move and adjust most elements	[list]		[*]Selecting Align to Elements snaps components to other UI elements[/*]		[*]Selecting Align to Grid reveals a grid for precise placement[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Each element can be clicked to open a dedicated settings window	[list]		[*]Here, adjust anchor points, scale, and opacity can be adjusted[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Some elements are part of predefined groups, allowing for simultaneous movement and scaling for easier organization	[list]		[*]Each individual element within these groups can still be adjusted independently[/*]		[*]Custom groups can be created[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Some elements have additional specific settings for further customization	[list]		[*]For example, the Status Effects bar can be configured to adjust its layout in rows and columns[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]On mobile, the offset to the screen edge can also be adjusted[/*][/list]
[b]Saving and Sharing Layouts[/b][list]	[*]After making adjustments in the HUD Editor, players can save their custom HUD layouts[/*]	[*]Up to 10 layouts can be saved for different activities[/*]	[*]These can be easily switched with the new Quick Presets feature[/*]	[*]Once saved, layouts can be quickly accessed from the ‘Interface’ settings menu[/*]	[*]To share a layout, players can copy it to the clipboard and share it	[list]		[*]This layout can be imported and saved directly into the HUD Editor[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Layouts are platform-specific and can only be shared between players on the same platform (PC or mobile)[/*][/list]
[b]Changes to Interface Settings[/b][list]	[*]The scale of the HUD layout is now adjusted independently from the window scale	[list]		[*]Window scaling now refers exclusively to UI windows like menus and popups[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Due to low demand, the default layout ‘Spells on Right’ has been removed	[list]		[*]Players who wish to use this setup can recreate it manually using the HUD Editor[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[h3]Inventory and Storage Improvements[/h3]

This update brings a number of significant improvements and changes to the Inventory, Bank, and Chest UIs:[list]	[*]The equipped items display above the player’s inventory can be condensed into a compact view	[list]		[*]This allows more inventory space to view carried items[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Item sizes in the inventory can be customized, allowing more items to be visible at once[/*]	[*]Items in a player’s inventory can be sorted by the following categories	[list]		[*]Weight[/*]		[*]Tier[/*]		[*]Estimated Market Value[/*]		[*]Estimated Value by Weight[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Items can now be repaired from inside bank tabs, with the option to Repair All items in one click[/*]	[*]A new Move All button allows for easy transfers between inventory, chests and bank tabs[/*]	[*]Item search is now also available in the inventory UI[/*]	[*]The average item power of your equipped items is now displayed in the header of the inventory UI[/*]	[*][DESKTOP] When mounting or dismounting transport mounts, a visual indicator in the inventory and the HUD now shows your load capacity change[/*][/list]
[h3]New Albion Journal Categories[/h3]

Two new categories have been added to the Albion Journal:

[b]Social and Guild[/b][list]	[*]This category challenges players to participate in group and guild activities, encouraging players to work together in large-scale battles, guild missions, and other social events[/*][/list]
[b]Islands[/b][list]	[*]This category introduces missions that revolve around managing your personal and guild islands, including farming and island upgrades[/*][/list]Each category comes with its own unique rewards, which are unlocked at different stages of progress.

[b]Other Journal changes[/b][list]	[*]New subcategories and missions have been added:	[list]		[*]A new PvE subcategory for Dynamic Encampments[/*]		[*]New Exploration missions focused on S.A.F.E. Portals and Open World Coffers[/*]		[*]New Gathering missions related to Dynamic Resource Hotspots[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Improved automatic Journal mission recommendations and mission order[/*]	[*]Adjusted various mission conditions to enhance early-game progression[/*]	[*]Achievement mission progress elements in the Albion Journal UI are now fully clickable[/*][/list]
[h3]Additional Changes and Improvements[/h3]

[b]Mists Changes[/b][list]	[*]The Fame penalty applied to mobs within Mists Camps, due to them being quest NPCs with very high respawn rates, has been increased from 60% to 90%	[list]		[*]Our intention is for camps to be played once before exhausting their value and needing to move on, but due to the high concentration of champion-level enemies in the new Dynamic Encampments, their potential for becoming a Fame camp was too great due to their high respawn rate[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Removed quest completion Fame[/*]	[*]Significantly increased the amount of Tomes of Insight within Personal Chests, to counter the lost Fame from mobs and quest completion	[list]		[*]These changes should entirely counterbalance each other so that there is no change to the total amount of Fame from Mists Camps[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Ranking Improvements[/b][list]	[*]New categories to Player Rankings are available:	[list]		[*]PvP Fame - Open World[/*]		[*]PvP Fame - Mists[/*]		[*]PvP Fame - Corrupted Dungeons[/*]		[*]PvP Fame - Hell Gates[/*]		[*]PvP Fame - Roads of Avalon[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Open World[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Mists[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Roads of Avalon[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Hardcore Expeditions[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Solo Dungeons[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Group (Veteran) Dungeons[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Large Group (Raid) Dungeons[/*]		[*]PvE Fame - Static Dungeons[/*]		[*]Tracking Fame[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Fiber[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Hide[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Ore[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Stone[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Wood[/*]		[*]Gathering Fame - Fishing[/*]		[*]Journal Missions Completed[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Fame gained prior to the Horizons Update will not count towards these new categories, but will still count towards the old ranking categories[/*][/list]
[b]Player Markers[/b][list]	[*] [DESKTOP] Players can now double the size of all markers through the party menu	[list]		[*]This ensures better visibility during large-scale battles[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Marked nametags will no longer disappear prematurely when the tagged player runs north of the screen	[list]		[*]This matches the behavior of off-screen tags in other directions[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]VFX Reworks[/b][list]	[*]The gathering animation for Wood Axes has been reworked, providing a more visually dynamic and polished look to the woodcutting process[/*]	[*]Animations for the Deadly Chop and Battle Rush abilities have been improved for all Two-Handed Axe variants[/*]	[*]The Infernal Monstrosity and Bound Molten Demon have received a visual overhaul, with updated attack animations and spell effects[/*]	[*]The first Heretic Mine Expedition has received environmental improvements[/*][/list]
[b]Other Changes[/b][list]	[*]The pursuit range of Siphoning Mages has been reduced[/*]	[*]Dropped Banners no longer reduce Fortification protection[/*]	[*]The Energy destruction rate on Territory raids has been doubled from 5% to 10%[/*]	[*]The Enchantment level of Random Dungeon Maps now matches the Enchantment level of the dungeon it spawns[/*]	[*]Destiny Board highlighting has been polished, and is less glaring when zoomed in[/*]	[*][MOBILE] The ‘Virtual Controller’ and ‘Tap Controls’ style settings in the ‘Controls → General’ section of the in-game Settings menu are now defaults for recommended Control options[/*]	[*][MOBILE] Added a new server selection UI[/*]	[*][DESKTOP] While in half-mounted radius, players now run to their mount before starting the mounting action, aligning with the existing Mobile behavior[/*][/list]
[h3]Combat Balance Changes[/h3]

[b]Axes[/b][list]	[*]Bloody Reap (Infernal Scythe)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 25s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Fire Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Pyroblast (one-handed Fire Staff)	[list]		[*]Initial channel damage: 190 → 140[/*]		[*]Channel damage after 0.6s: 266 → 240[/*]		[*]Channel damage after 1.2s: 342 → 340[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Holy Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Generous Heal (all Holy Staffs)	[list]		[*]Heal: 132 → 100[/*]		[*]Cooldown: 2s → 1.5s[/*]		[*]Now increases all healing received by the target by 5% for 4s, stacking up to 3 times[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Holy Flash (all Holy Staffs)	[list]		[*]Heal: 130 → 117[/*]		[*]Max targets: 5 → 10[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Holy Beam (all Holy Staffs)	[list]		[*]Channel duration: 6s → 3s[/*]		[*]Cooldown: 16s → 10s[/*]		[*]Healing now starts at 60 and increases by 5 every 0.5s (previously started at 30 and increased by 30 per tick)		[list]			[*]Total possible healing: 840 → 525[/*]		[/list]		[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Nature Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Rejuvenating Flower (all Nature Staffs)	[list]		[*]Empower Time: 0s → 0s, 2s → 1.5s, 4s → 3s[/*]		[*]Spell effect area radius: 1m → 1.5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Cleanse Heal (all Nature Staffs)	[list]		[*]Max targets: 5 → 10[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Quarterstaffs[/b][list]	[*]Concussive Combo (all Quarterstaffs)	[list]		[*]The third hit is now an AoE with a radius of 4m		[list]			[*]Third hit damage: 130 → 85[/*]		[/list]		[/*]		[*]Now increases Threat Generation by 50[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Hurricane (Iron-clad Staff)	[list]		[*]Cooldown reduced by 3s (cooldown scaling by Item Power is unchanged)[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shapeshifter Staffs[/b][list]	[*]Bloody Roar (Bloodmoon Staff)	[list]		[*]Life steal: 7% → 6%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Swords[/b][list]	[*]Mighty Blow (Broadsword)	[list]		[*]End position offset: -3m → -2.5m[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Armors[/b][list]	[*]Wind Wall (Knight Armor)	[list]		[*]Now purges all enemies hit[/*]		[*]Cooldown: 30s → 40s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Shoes[/b][list]	[*]Raging Blink (Stalker Shoes)	[list]		[*]Recast cooldown: 25s → 30s (single cast cooldown remains 25s)[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Mark of Sacrifice (Hellion Shoes)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 20s → 15s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Shield Charge (Knight Boots)	[list]		[*]Cooldown: 25s → 20s[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
[b]Mounts[/b][list]	[*]T3 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 55%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T4 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 60%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T5 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Gallop Speed: 110% → 115%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T6 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 70%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 115% → 120%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T7 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 75%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 120% → 125%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T8 Riding Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 80%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 125% → 135%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Spectral Bonehorse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 80%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 128% → 137%[/*]		[*]Time until Gallop: 4s → 3s[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T5 Armored Horse	[list]		[*]Gallop Speed: 110% → 115%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T6 Armored Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 70%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 115% → 120%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T7 Armored Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 75%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 120% → 125%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]T8 Armored Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 80%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 125% → 135%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Morgana Nightmare	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 80%[/*]		[*]Gallop Speed: 128% → 137%[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*]Gallant Horse	[list]		[*]Base Speed: 65% → 75%[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]

tags.feature: New dynamic objectives appear for a limited time across the open world, cycling through active and inactive phases.
Dynamic Encampments are temporary camps settled by mobs from each Faction, who protect valuable Caches
Lair Maps can spawn in mob camps - including Dynamic Encampments - giving players the chance to uncover a hidden Boss Lair belonging to the corresponding Faction
Dynamic Resource Hotspots
New Coffers, similar to those found in the Mists, now spawn across the open world.
S.A.F.E. Portals can now be found in the Portal Towns of the Outlands, offering solo players a quick teleport to random locations within the Outlands.
A new player count indicator has been added to Outlands regions, offering a rough estimate of the number of players present.
Some Tier 6 regions can now be found in Yellow Zones, and some Tier 5 regions in Blue Zones, giving players access to a broader range of content before stepping into full-loot PvP zones
Tier 7 resources now spawn in Tier 7 Red Zones
Kill details are now suppressed for 5 minutes for everyone except the killer and the victim
During a region’s Prime Time, the Next Activity Chest Value overlay now displays the current chest value instead of the upcoming one

tags.balance_change: The value of Hidden Treasures has been increased by roughly 400%
Mobs from Tier 5 and above now receive incremental power boosts, starting with a 9% increase at Tier 5 and 42% by Tier 8
As mob power increases, corresponding rewards (Fame, loot, and Silver) will scale as well to offer more substantial incentives for taking on these tougher foes
Rewards for most group and raid activities have been adjusted
Fame and loot rewards for groups of 3 or more players have been increased by approximately 50%

tags.feature: This update introduces two new Crystal Creatures to the Outlands, aimed at groups of about 5 players – the Crystal Beetle and the Crystal Cobra.

tags.balance_change: All Crystal Creatures, including Crystal Spiders, now spawn much more frequently; their spawn rate is adjusted based on the overall Guild Season point output
Each individual Crystal Creature now yields less loot and Might, to partially counterbalance their significantly increased frequency
Loot rewards have been reduced by 56%, and Might by 83%
Crystal Creatures no longer grant Favor, so that their rewards can be more focused on loot

tags.feature: Quick Settings Presets allow players to save different configurations of in-game options and instantly switch between them with customizable shortcuts

The new HUD Editor allows players on both mobile and desktop to fully customize nearly all aspects of their in-game interface, allowing for a highly customizable experience tailored to individual needs and playstyles.

tags.balance_change: The scale of the HUD layout is now adjusted independently from the window scale
Due to low demand, the default layout ‘Spells on Right’ has been removed

tags.feature: This update brings a number of significant improvements and changes to the Inventory, Bank, and Chest UIs
Two new categories have been added to the Albion Journal
New subcategories and missions have been added

tags.balance_change: The Fame penalty applied to mobs within Mists Camps, due to them being quest NPCs with very high respawn rates, has been increased from 60% to 90%
Removed quest completion Fame
Significantly increased the amount of Tomes of Insight within Personal Chests, to counter the lost Fame from mobs and quest completion

tags.feature: New categories to Player Rankings are available
[DESKTOP] Players can now double the size of all markers through the party menu

tags.balance_change: Marked nametags will no longer disappear prematurely when the tagged player runs north of the screen

Animations for the Deadly Chop and Battle Rush abilities have been improved for all Two-Handed Axe variants
The Infernal Monstrosity and Bound Molten Demon have received a visual overhaul, with updated attack animations and spell effects
The first Heretic Mine Expedition has received environmental improvements
