notes.title: Patch 5 Brings Black Market and Mobile Improvements
notes.content:
Today's patch brings numerous fixes and quality-of-life improvements to gameplay in Albion. Here's a bit of what's new:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d0e8d2346aa1f918cb6a8893642235c7b67f4b92.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Black Market: Persistent Crafting Info and Improved Performance[/h3]
Items sold to the Black Market [b]will now retain their "crafted by" info[/b]. This means that a great deal of item loot from mobs and in treasure chests will now show who originally crafted the item. In addition to helping active crafters make a name for themselves, persistent item info adds to the depth and continuity of Albion's ever-changing world. This patch also includes performance improvements to Black Market item distribution, correcting an issue where "split" party loot mode would sometimes not work when looting items.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/96cdf2724eb1fc9dc03d959d79105c8b8710bb24.png[/img]
[h3]A Dynamic "Hotkey" and Other Mobile Improvements[/h3]
Starting with Patch 5, the mobile version includes [b]an additional "Custom Button" next to the spellbar[/b], with one fixed option ("Inspect") and four additional customizable buttons that can be set via the Settings menu. This button allows for everything from Autorun to party member selection to emotes, and is among the most-requested features for mobile devices. This button is still in the experimental stages, so give it a try and let us know your thoughts on our [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Board/138-Mobile-Version/][b]mobile forum[/b][/url].

Additional improvements include the ability to connect a mouse for desktop-style chat scrolling, the ability to send feedback and bug reports via a new UI, an "Increase Brightness" slider in Settings, and various bug fixes.
[h3]General Changes and Fixes[/h3][list]	[*]The health increase for Demonic Shards in Corrupted Dungeons that was intended for Patch 4 is now live.[/*]	[*]The combat log now displays combat data for mounted players.[/*]	[*]Repair Tables can once again be placed in Expeditions.[/*]	[*]Maxed-out specialization nodes now display the correct item power bonus.[/*][/list]
For the complete list of changes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/RISE%20OF%20AVALON%20PATCH%205][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Population Update: September 2020
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1435a0abc9d9f35e1e8dddb78605e19dc1d2fbdb.jpeg[/img]

Back in May, we reported on the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/population-update-may-2020][b]massive population growth[/b][/url] that Albion Online saw in the first part of 2020, starting with the Queen Update in January and growing further with worldwide quarantine measures during the COVID-19 pandemic. Now, even as many of these measures are easing, the ingame population continues to grow: this month we surpassed the lockdown population peak to achieve [b]a new Daily Average User count of over 125,000 players[/b].

This boost comes in large part from the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/rise-of-avalon][b]Rise of Avalon Update[/b][/url], which launched on August 12 with a host of massive new features like [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], and [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b]. The update also introduced [b]Chinese and Korean language support[/b] to the game, which has brought a huge influx of new players from these regions and grown the Albion Online community into a truly global one.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/099bf4db76d93344e515ee2d7d4f84c419e2b5bc.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Expanding the Royal Continent, Working Toward the Mobile Launch[/h3]
As mentioned in our last update, we've been focusing not only on supporting the content introduced with the Queen and Rise of Avalon updates, but also on improving the gameplay experience for all players as population numbers increase.

In tandem with new features and upgrades coming to the world of Albion over the coming months, we've set our sights on an [b]expansion of the Royal Continent[/b]. The ongoing growth of the player base has made Albion's blue, yellow and red zones fuller than ever, and we're currently hard at work on a comprehensive plan to expand these Royal zones while deepening the gameplay experience they offer.

We're also hard at work improving and streamlining the [b]mobile version[/b] of Albion Online, with continual improvements to mobile-based controls and menus being rolled out since the Queen launch, and more to come. We'll soon have further updates on the mobile version, including the next steps towards a [b]Play Store beta launch[/b] in the final leadup to the [b]official Apple and Google store launches[/b], which will finally fulfill our vision of a truly cross-platform MMORPG experience with platform-optimized content updates. For now, though, we're focusing on making the mobile experience as fun and intuitive as possible.

Thanks for being part of the ever-growing Albion Online community!

notes.title: Albion's Tenth Guild Season Starts Saturday
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/98ffd8608c3a40e479136cd15122c6c996c7155b.jpeg[/img]

Saturday marks the beginning of Albion's [b]tenth Guild Season[/b], a major milestone that would not have been possible without the support of the Albion community worldwide. This season will be the first to include the new [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b] and [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], and we're very excited to see how guilds make use of these new features. 

For the complete Guild Season schedule, check out [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/134086][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4f448ed36d6d40aab11f0b319376f8e259ad0836.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Claim Your Goliath Horseeater[/h3]
Guilds that reach a high enough rank during the season can claim fantastic rewards including an [b]avatar[/b], [b]avatar ring[/b], and the fearsome new [b]Goliath Horseeater mount [/b]with root, immobility, and poison spells. This mount will be awarded to members of guilds that reach [b]Silver Rank or higher[/b] during the season. The winning guild will receive a statue among the past Guild Season winners in [b]Conquerors' Hall[/b], and the first through fifth ranked guilds will also receive a 90-day [b]Fame Bonus[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/09c288b1b920e1e898b1fd9cf69ceaa104151739.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Watch Live on AlbionTV[/h3]
As always, you can watch the season start live: the action kicks off on [url=https://www.twitch.tv/albiononline][b]AlbionTV[/b][/url] this [b]Saturday, August 29 at 17:30 UTC[/b], when hosts [b]Shozenwon, Lewpac [/b]and[b] Bogul[/b] bring you full coverage of Invasion Day.

At [b]18:00 UTC[/b], guilds can claim territories and launch attacks. Those in the North and South American time zones can also tune in for the second round of territory resets on [b]Sunday, August 30 at 00:30 UTC[/b] with hosts [b]Shozenwon, Robinhoodrs[/b] and [b]Bogul[/b] covering the next round of claimable territories starting at [b]01:00 UTC[/b].

Fights are broadcast live with a 15-minute time delay.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4612d65b913b2af4cc105414e85aa77bc69a0c97.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Relive the Offseason Crystal Tournament[/h3]
Last weekend we hosted the first-ever Offseason Crystal Tournament, hopefully the first of many. If you missed it, you can read a rundown of the tournament and watch its thrilling conclusion [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/june-esports-wins-offseason-crystal-tournament][b]here[/b][/url] - or if you want to avoid spoilers, you can jump straight to our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MJ81SchJaaU][b]Youtube channel[/b][/url] and watch the final match directly!

notes.title: Patch 2 Brings Corrupted Dungeon Changes
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8d6686b9790ba692156cc798ee7365c2a7c68e02.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update went live on August 12, bringing numerous major new features to the world of Albion. One such feature is [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], which have already been accessed [b]over one million times[/b] since the update went live. Based on this tremendous amount of new data and community feedback, we've made some adjustments to how [b]Infamy[/b] works:
[list]	[*]Players now lose [b]half as much Infamy[/b] when killed, and gain slightly less when victorious[/*]	[*]A [b]flat Infamy bonus[/b] has been added to PvP wins based on dungeon level[/*]	[*]Slayer dungeon unlock is now [b]permanent and retroactive[/b][/*]	[*]Matchmaking system adjusted and improved[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8ba54240c49529047e1f196781978e4402dbc750.png[/img][h3]New Season 9 Statue[/h3]
Congratulations to Guild Season 9 winners [b]Elevate[/b] on their decisive victory! You can visit [b]Conquerors' Hall[/b] in all major Royal Continent cities to see the new statue in their honor, which appears both at the entryway and inside and also honors second- and third-place winners [b]Bloco de Rua[/b] and [b]RANG[/b].
[h3]Other Changes[/h3][list]	[*][b]5 new Castles[/b] and [b]20 new Castle Outposts[/b] added to the Outlands[/*]	[*][b]Arena / Crystal League / City Fight Scoreboards [/b]now update more reliably[/*]	[*]Increased overall spawn numbers for [b]Hellgates[/b][/*]	[*]Various [b]Combat Balance Changes[/b] and [b]bugfixes[/b][/*][/list]
For the full list of changes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/RISE%20OF%20AVALON%20PATCH%202][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Season 10 Brings Incredible New Rewards
notes.content:
Albion Online's Tenth Guild Season starts on [b]Saturday, August 29[/b]. Guilds that reach a high enough rank during the season can claim fantastic rewards including an [b]avatar[/b], [b]avatar ring[/b], and the fearsome new [b]Goliath Horseeater mount[/b]!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4f448ed36d6d40aab11f0b319376f8e259ad0836.jpeg[/img]

The Goliath Horseeater strikes fear into the hearts of other battle mounts with its powerful web, which can render them completely immobile. It also has AoE root and poison spells that slow and weaken enemy forces. This mount will be awarded to guilds who reach [b]Silver Rank or higher[/b] during Season 10, with increasingly higher stats (and increasingly epic appearance) with each successive tier.

The winning guild will receive a statue among the past Guild Season winners in Conquerors' Hall, which since the Queen update can be accessed via all major cities. Qualifying guilds will also receive a Fame Bonus and furniture items, as listed in the tables below:

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a65be31afa049cdffc902affd7abcbe7a3a79718.jpeg[/img]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4e48ba324e753d1a368d25569aa76d79f588375d.jpeg[/img]
[h3]New This Season: Roads of Avalon + New Weapons[/h3]
The launch of the [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update on August 12 brought numerous new features to the world of Albion. The [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are an ever-shifting road network accessed via the open world that allows guilds to place [b]Hideouts[/b] away from the politics of the Outlands. Avalon lacks territories that give Season Points, but guilds can still choose to compete in other ways from an Avalon-based Hideout.

Additionally, the new line of fifteen [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b] introduced with Rise of Avalon will have far-reaching effects on small- and large-scale battles alike, and will update the combat meta for both [b]open-world territory battles[/b] and the 5v5 combat of the [b]Crystal League[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/0fa477affce4d5810bd7894de950cd326046e7f5.jpeg[/img]

Gear up and prepare for a whole new season – and check out the full rundown of important [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/134086][b]Season 10 dates[/b][/url] on our forum.

notes.title: Rise of Avalon is Live!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d177f0da272447a218e72a7f9351cb0c32e61d15.jpeg[/img]

Today is the day: the [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update is finally here! This update brings massive new features and improvements to the world of Albion - and to mark the occasion, we've created a brand-new trailer:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=psUwESfA6yc
Read on for more of what's coming with Rise of Avalon:
[h3]Explore an Ancient Kingdom[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/870a1b152a9283be67c942d4c0b8ee2c470e54f7.jpeg[/img]

Enter the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], a sprawling network of magical pathways that bring new opportunities for travel, transport, and combat. notes.title: First Look: The Rogue Adventurer Bundle
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/e5c32698f0aafab646979f08445e46a65c64ee90.jpeg[/img]

The [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update arrives August 12, bringing numerous major new features to the world of Albion. This update also introduces a new premier vanity skin set: the [b]Rogue Adventurer[/b]. This bundle includes [b]nine vanity unlocks [/b]in a striking black-and-green color scheme to transform your character into a mysterious, shadowy rogue. Costume items can be used on male or female characters, with unique looks (and even unique voices) for each.

In addition, this bundle includes an [b]Armored Horse Mount Skin[/b] with a matching black-and-green theme. On top of that, it also includes [b]guild versions[/b] of the Rogue Adventurer armor, cape, and mount skins that allow you to show off your currently active guild logo and colors.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a6149ef7de4f8ee125ffaa936428a17d39a6668f.jpeg[/img]

The centerpiece of the Rogue Adventurer Bundle is the [b]Poison Bottle[/b]. This costume weapon includes two premium animated emotes activated by spells: [b]Poisonous Spirits[/b] and [b]Dangerous Juggling[/b].

notes.title: The Divine Challenge Returns with a New Mount
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ee8123ef823b04921923ea97e407d1ba8061b520.jpeg[/img]

The Divine Challenge is back, with a whole new mount! For the entire month of August, earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your very own [b]Divine Owl[/b].
[h3][b]Simply Divine[/b][/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d83bf046c0279d2ecc98aa9e2f8ace278a723242.png[/img]
[b]DIVINE OWL:[/b] This month's Challenge introduces a new mount, the [b]Divine Owl[/b]. This ghostly white flying mount has a brisk base move speed as well as a new ability, [b]Foresight[/b], a shield that absorbs damage and grants a temporary speed boost when broken. (Note: like all mounts, the Divine Owl can only move in navigable ground areas and cannot fly over obstacles.)

[img]https://i.imgur.com/4RhCStZ.png[/img]
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Divine Challenge avatar ring[/b], which will frame your chosen avatar in a heavenly golden aura. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Vanity Token.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/5e8qvan.png[/img]
[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Divine Challenge chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes and Silver, you'll also have a chance to unlock mystical furniture items like the [b]Mage Statue, Magic Rune Circle[/b], and [b]Glass Sphere[/b].

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount / avatar ring reward. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while you can!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Roads of Avalon, Part 3
notes.content:
In our last two Dev Talks on the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], Game Director Robin Henkys introduced this major feature, discussed [b]travel and transport[/b] in the Roads, and gave a brief rundown of what you'll find in the [b]Wilderness [/b]outside the road network. In this third and final Dev Talk on the subject, he discusses [b]living within the Roads of Avalon[/b], an exciting new opportunity for guilds looking for a Hideout of their own. (For more on the Roads of Avalon, check out [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-roads-of-avalon-part-1][b]Part 1[/b][/url] and [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-roads-of-avalon-part-2]Part 2[/url].)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rij2UFVmwfo
No time to watch, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]Placing and Defending Hideouts[/h3]
While most zones within the Roads of Avalon consist of the road network itself, some are almost completely Wilderness. In these special zones, you can find [b]energy crystals[/b] that keep the mists at bay and allow placement of [b]Hideouts[/b]. Guilds can place Hideouts at these crystals during the [b]prime time[/b] visible on the zone map. As always, unfinished Hideouts are vulnerable during the [b]first and the last minutes[/b] of construction.

Once established, a Hideout will be protected just like in the open world. However, since there are no territories in the Avalonian wilderness, [b]any guild with the required amount of Siphoned Energy[/b] can break a Hideout’s defenses at the beginning of the zone’s prime time. They can then attempt to attack the Hideout, but as usual, once a Hideout loses a defense point it will become invulnerable until the next day’s prime time.

This is significant, because [b]no gateway connection to the zone will remain for a whole day[/b], meaning the attacking side must stay in the zone to continue their attack. And as each gateway only lets in a few players at once, even initial attacks are challenging. Other guilds can of course place their own Hideouts in the region, but these will have to be built and defended as usual.

In short, destroying a Hideout in Avalon is significantly more challenging than it might be in the Outlands, making it an attractive option for smaller guilds who want a Hideout of their own.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/817348698287c66736db119ef15733a27550e389.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Challenges of Living in Avalon[/h3]
[b]1. Limited resources and PvE content[/b]

Players will have to explore the surrounding Roads to find gateways to the open world to bring in resources and gear, or to export goods they produce with the [b]crafting bonuses[/b] of their Avalon Hideout. Each Avalon Wilderness region has its own unique set of crafting bonuses, and while none of them outcompete the deep Outlands, they can still be very attractive for crafters.

[b]2. Limited capacity and shifting nature of Avalonian gateways[/b]

If your guild has too many members, you will be competing for the capacity of the gateways, and if your players are not careful, you may get stranded somewhere in Avalon with no easy way back to your Hideout.

[b]3. Lack of territories for Season Point generation[/b]

While you can of course still compete in the Crystal League, complete the Guild challenge, and raid territory mages from your Hideout, you will find it [b]hard to claim and hold territories[/b].

That may be a good thing, however, as it means your Avalon Hideout is not likely to become a target of guilds competing for power in the Outlands.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/584899db5566b7a4c4d6c69d8e81e45ba1e45e1f.jpeg[/img]
[h3]In Conclusion[/h3]
There's no lack of action for guilds living in Avalon. The constantly shifting gateways bring opportunities for exploration and conflict to your front door, especially when a gateway opens to another Wilderness region with an active guild living in it, and we're very excited to see how players adapt to this unique environment

This concludes our series of videos on the Roads of Avalon. Thanks for watching, and we'll see you ingame when the Rise of Avalon update goes live on August 12!

notes.title: Rise of Avalon Launches August 12
notes.content:
On August 12, 2020, the [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update will bring massive new features including the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b], and more.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d177f0da272447a218e72a7f9351cb0c32e61d15.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Enter a Mysterious New Realm[/h3]
The [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are a massive, shifting network of ancient pathways, entered via gateways that spawn in the open world. They present a wealth of new options for travel, transport, trade, and launching (or escaping) attacks. Outside the roads themselves, the immense [b]Wilderness of Avalon[/b] offers a whole new realm to explore, with treasures, resource sites, and new creatures and Avalonian enemies to conquer. And smaller guilds looking for a home away from the politics of the Outlands can even [b]place Hideouts and live[/b] in the Roads of Avalon.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9750c0d2e177b0704bc7e526483897bf2af816bc.png[/img]
[h3]Face Your Demons[/h3]
[b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b] allow single players to take on challenging solo PvE in a fiery realm populated with [b]demons, traps[/b], and [b]corrupted beings[/b]. Defeat hordes of enemies for treasure and Infamy, or invade other players' dungeons and engage in [b]1v1 combat[/b] to gain Infamy and loot and rise through the leaderboards.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5d789d6f3ed6d87ae84e2cccf70e666c5f5d0c93.png[/img]
[h3]Wield the Power of Avalon[/h3]
A new line of [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b], each with their own unique skills, brings new dimensions to combat in Albion Online. These weapons can be crafted with new [b]artifacts[/b] and [b]Avalonian Shards[/b], and include skills such as:
[list]	[*][b]Lucent Hawk (Bow):[/b] shoot up to four high-impact, long-range skillshots in a row[/*]	[*][b]Majestic Smash (Two-Handed Sword):[/b] knock all enemies around you into the air, then follow with a heavy vertical attack[/*]	[*][b]Soul Link (Nature Staff):[/b] temporarily link two targets together, with effects based on targets' alignments relative to the caster[/*][/list]
Additionally, the [b]Destiny Board[/b] has been expanded and[b] PvE progression[/b] has been overhauled and updated.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a5f35843009c36d42111e69c8ff235ffb0e84417.png[/img]
[h3]UI Improvements, New Vanity Bundle, and Much More[/h3]
Additional features include numerous major [b]UI quality-of-life improvements[/b], an all-new [b]Rogue Adventurer Skin[/b] bundle, reduced [b]crafting times[/b], further [b]mobile optimizations[/b], and much, much more.

For further details, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/rise-of-avalon][b]Official Update Page[/b][/url].

notes.title: Happy Third Anniversary, Albion Online!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/233351cc2504a09032e9d2ec94bf341d95ff9dc7.jpeg[/img]

It's been three years since Albion's official launch on [b]July 17, 2017.[/b] Since then, the game, game world, and community have grown in ways we never could have imagined. Over the past months, the game world has undergone massive changes, the player base has reached its highest level yet, and there's much more to come with the massive new [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update releasing next month.

Of course, there are also various ingame events taking place to celebrate the occasion, including a [b]Fame Boost[/b] and a limited-time [b]classic Keeper dungeon[/b]. For more details on these events, click [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/in-game-anniversary-events][b]here[/b][/url].

Let's look at some of the major events and happenings of the past year:
[h3]Introducing the Avalonians[/h3]
Last fall, as Guild Season 7 drew to a close, a new presence began stirring in the Outlands. A [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/something-stirring-outlands][b]mysterious teaser trailer[/b][/url] hinted at the form and scale of this new threat, and soon after, its true nature became clear: an ancient force known as the [b]Avalonians[/b] had returned to Albion.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/261b48acfafcfeb0b3620f2b264d79b4a36ba394.jpeg[/img]

The Avalonians were introduced in stages during a unique [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/avalonian-invasion-has-begun][b]Standalone Guild Season[/b][/url] that brought Avalonian World Bosses, new tools and foods crafted with powerful [b]Avalonian Energy[/b], and even a new mount, the [b]Avalonian Basilisk[/b]. As the strength of the Avalonians grew, their intent became clear: to invade Caerleon and reclaim all of Albion for themselves. The season culminated in the chaotic [b]Battle of Caerleon[/b], in which Avalonian Mages and Constructs laid siege to the city before ultimately being driven back.

Check out [b]Equart's[/b] video summary of the event:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t184VajpRKY
[h3]The Queen Update[/h3]
The end of the Avalonian Invasion corresponded to the launch of the [b]Queen Update [/b]in January 2020, Albion's largest content update since launch. First and foremost, the update brought a [b]completely new Outlands continent[/b], shaped by the magic of the Avalonians. Where the old Outlands spread lower- and higher-tier zones across the whole continent, resources and rewards in the new Outlands increased towards the center. Guilds could build their own open-world homes in the form of [b]Hideouts,[/b] self-contained underground bases that allowed guilds to claim their own corner of the new Outlands.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b25299ad7e57bdf024827c54529298fcd65518aa.png[/img]

With Queen, those looking for a new type of high-level challenge could seek out [b]Elite Randomized Dungeons[/b], where larger groups could face off against mighty Avalonian enemies and claim artifacts needed to craft powerful [b]Avalonian Armors[/b]. The update also brought a whole new guild warfare system, where territory control was now determined via massive [b]open-world battles[/b]. And those looking for 5v5 combat could battle it out in the new [b]Crystal League[/b], with victors able to claim valuable rewards and boost their territory's tower level.
[h3]Reaching a Milestone[/h3]
The Queen Update was by far the most successful Albion Online content update since launch, confirmed by consistent population growth since launching in January, and a record-high of over 500,000 monthly users in April 2020. Nearly six months in the making, Queen was nothing less than a complete revisioning of Albion's high-level endgame, although the new features and systems it introduced affected players of all levels and playstyles.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9e84ebc0711a79cb9eb8264690acb0d7f67610f2.jpeg[/img]

For us, as the developers of the game, increased player numbers meant increased responsibility to all our players. In addition to creating a dedicated team for performance optimizations, as well as adding new talent to our ever-growing development team.
[h3]COVID-19: The Albion Community Responds[/h3]
In April 2020, with the COVID-19 pandemic raging and countless members of both the Albion community and greater worldwide community affected, we launched the [b]Staff of Hermes[/b] [b]Charity Pack[/b]. Included in this limited-time pack were a unique healing-themed offhand costume item and avatar ring, with 100% of the money collected going to the COVID Solidarity Fund.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/f4122e7bf98463f0442433203225ff29957493d8.jpeg[/img]

The response was tremendous: in the four weeks this special pack was available, the Albion Online community came together and raised an incredible [b]€42,644.94[/b]. The outpouring of support for this cause was truly inspiring, and the [b]"[url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/over-40000-raised-for-charity]staffies[/url]"[/b] sent in by those who had bought the pack contributed to the overall feeling of community and goodwill.
[h3]A Whole New Mobile Experience[/h3]
The [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/season-9-patch-is-here][b]Season 9 Patch[/b][/url], launched in May, brought far-reaching mobile improvements to the world of Albion. Systems that had previously been designed only for larger screens were completely reworked for mobile devices, and mobile gameplay was improved with everything from [b]context-based cursors[/b] to [b]customizable HUDs[/b] to [b]drag-cast spells[/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/d00121fcbbc3e0ee963c0545599df06f975e5ce9.jpeg[/img]

In the months since these major changes were implemented, our team has focused on optimizing mobile performance, with a major Android stability fix launched with [b]Queen Patch 16[/b] and further improvements on the way. Mobile optimizations will continue for the foreseeable future, with the eventual goal of releasing Albion Online in both the Apple and Google Play Stores.
[h3]Looking to the Future[/h3]
With each passing year, the story of Albion gains new depth and complexity. If you're in the mood to reminisce further, you can always revisit our [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/happy-second-anniversary-albion-online][b]Second[/b][/url] and [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/albion-online-turns-one][b]First Anniversary[/b][/url] retrospectives for a look at the major events of the first two years.

And finally, as we celebrate another year in the world of Albion, we want to give our most heartfelt thanks to you, the Albion Online community, for your support. We can't wait to see what the coming year (and beyond) will bring to the world of Albion – we'll have more exciting news and previews of upcoming features very soon, and we'll see you ingame when the [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update goes live in August!
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nJh0W3_sIis

With Queen, those looking for a new type of high-level challenge could seek out Elite Randomized Dungeons, where larger groups could face off against mighty Avalonian enemies and claim artifacts needed to craft powerful Avalonian Armors.
The update also brought a whole new guild warfare system, where territory control was now determined via massive open-world battles.

notes.title: In-Game Anniversary Events and Fame Boost
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4e600b03e2bbd29e83ba79e18a4b7fbd185fae39.jpeg[/img]

It's been three years since Albion Online's official launch... and while it's certainly a good time to [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/happy-third-anniversary-albion-online][b]take a look back[/b][/url] at everything that's happened since then, it's an even better time to celebrate! Log in now and enjoy a [b]week-long Fame Boost[/b], free [b]fireworks[/b], and a classic [b]Keeper Dungeon[/b] from Albion's beta.
[h3]The Mists of Albion Are Back[/h3]
What better way to celebrate another year in the world of Albion than a Fame Boost? Between now and maintenance on July 24, get [b]25% additional Fame[/b] for all ingame activities.

Here are the details:
[list]	[*]At the end of maintenance on [b]Friday, July 17[/b], the [b]Mists of Albion[/b] buff will be automatically enabled for all players[/*]	[*]This buff automatically grants [b]an additional 25% Fame[/b] for all activities[/*]	[*]The buff does not apply to Fame earned via PvP kills and Tomes of Insight, and does not boost the rate at which Challenge Points are earned[/*]	[*]The Fame boost ends at [b]10:00 UTC[/b] on [b]Friday, July 24[/b][/*][/list]
With the [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update coming in August, now is the perfect time to level up your combat, crafting, and gathering!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b60a8ba2927bf21533f7e650d5961df5d714b321.png[/img]
[h3]A Classic Returns[/h3]
From now until July 31, you'll have a chance to revisit the [b]Defenders of the Past[/b] dungeon, a classic Keeper dungeon from Albion's beta. This dungeon has retained its classic terrain and enemy layout, and has been updated with current shrines, loot, and rewards. In addition, those who complete this dungeon will have a chance to score the brand-new [b]Red Anniversary Banner[/b].

Here are all the details:
[list]	[*]Defenders of the Past will [b]spawn randomly in T4-8 zones[/b] in both the Royal Continent and the Outlands[/*]	[*]The dungeon will spawn in both [b]solo[/b] (green) and [b]group[/b] (blue) versions, with enemies and loot balanced accordingly[/*]	[*]The dungeon entrance will appear as a [b]portal flanked by Anniversary Banners[/b][/*]	[*]The final boss chest will give a chance to receive the [b]Red Anniversary Banner[/b] along with other loot[/*][/list]
This limited-time dungeon will only be playable until [b]July 31 at 10:00 UTC[/b], so head out into the open world and revisit a unique piece of Albion's past!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/31d18c24920bed2ff9308c8677bddbd725007fb0.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Decorations, Fireworks, and a Forum Contest[/h3]
Albion's cities have been decked out with special anniversary decorations – and to help celebrate, we've sent red, blue, and yellow [b]Anniversary Fireworks[/b] to all players. Just log in between now and [b]July 31 at 10:00 UTC[/b] to receive an in-game mail with your rewards. (Note: the mail will only be sent to characters created before July 17.)

And last but not least, we're running a "[b]Strike a Pose[/b]" contest over on the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/132840][b]forum[/b][/url]. Get decked out in your best armor and costumes, find your favorite ingame spot, and get creative, and you could win fabulous prizes! Prizes will be given for the best [b]solo, group[/b], and [b]guild[/b] entries.

Remember, the Fame Boost and forum contest end on [b]July 24[/b] and the classic dungeon and free fireworks end on [b]July 31[/b], so log in today and join the celebration!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Roads of Avalon, Part 2
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32445805/0b27d5c7ed2ba1ebf48097164e49acf91e48e47e.png[/img]

In our last Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys introduced the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], a massive new system coming with the next update. In this video, he discusses what you'll find when you leave the Roads and head into the Wilderness. (To watch Part 1, [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-roads-of-avalon-part-1][b]click here[/b][/url].)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JKoORR1oyJE
No time to watch, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]Beyond the Roads[/h3]
A zone map of Avalon shows that the Roads form a very distinct [b]rune / symbol[/b] shape. This makes it easier to recognize areas you've already visited and helps you find your way through the ever-shifting network. There are also paths outside of the Roads, which are called the [b]Wilderness of Avalon[/b].

The Wilderness hosts a variety of different locations:
[list]	[*][b]Forest paths[/b][/*]	[*][b]Resource sites[/b][/*]	[*][b]Avalonian camps[/b][/*]	[*][b]Randomized Dungeon entrances[/b][/*][/list][h3]Location Details[/h3]
[b]Forest Paths[/b]
These simple paths wind through the forests and ruins of Avalon. You can use them as shortcuts, or to avoid the main roads if you're concerned about encountering other explorers.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/be6d6db12f45ba27c288206463438eab5d85e8eb.jpeg[/img][/h3]
[b]Resource Sites[/b]
These locations have a high concentration of resources as well as [b]elemental spirits[/b] guarding them. Unlike in the open world, elemental spirits in Avalon also appear in [b]Veteran and Elite versions[/b] that are harder to defeat but give much more raw material. You may even encounter new [b]Tier 7-8 Aspects and Guardians[/b], which yield extremely valuable resources and may be enchanted all the way to level 3.

Resource sites are marked on the map, but it is up to you to discover their Tier and the strength of the spirits protecting them.

[b]Avalonian Camps[/b]
In certain locations, Avalonians and their constructs are collecting artifacts and treasure from the deserted ruins. Players can attempt to take these treasures, but the chests will only open once all enemies at the site have been defeated. These camps appear from Tier 4-8 in the following difficulties:
[list]	[*][b]Regular [/b](solo players)[/*]	[*][b]Veteran [/b](small groups)[/*]	[*][b]Elite [/b](groups of about ten players)[/*][/list]
Avalonian Camps are also marked on the map, but again, you will have to explore them to discover their Tier and what sort of treasure they hold.

[b]Randomized Dungeon Entrances[/b]
These entrances lead to the same Randomized Solo, Group, and Elite dungeons as you'll find in the open world, but with [b]a significant buff to Fame and loot[/b]. They are also significantly rarer than those that spawn in the open world.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/dd31cb7819af86755c7e8d92022bccfa43a379b3.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Solo or Small Group?[/h3]
There’s a lot of valuable treasure and Fame to be found in the Wilderness of Avalon. Some can be claimed on your own, but some is so valuable and difficult to acquire that you may want to tell your friends or guild about it. As the path you found to get there will probably disappear within a few hours, you'll have to be quick to tell others, and if you claim valuable treasure or resources you'll still have to safely bring them home or to the Marketplace.
[h3]Next Up: Living in the Wilderness[/h3]
That's all for today – in our next Dev Talk we’ll discuss how you can [b]build your own Hideout[/b] in Avalon and what it takes to live in a constantly-shifting labyrinth of ancient gateways and paths. Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Roads of Avalon, Part 1
notes.content:
The [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update arrives in August, bringing a host of new features to the world of Albion. In our newest Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys introduces the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b], a new system that will massively expand the gameworld and bring new opportunities for travel, exploration, and even settlement.

Note: Due to the complexity of this feature, today's Dev Talk is the [b]first of three talks [/b]on this feature.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jt1stGAcR7o
No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]What are Roads of Avalon?[/h3]
The [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are a network of ever-changing paths through the ancient kingdom of Avalon. They allow players to do three things:
[list]	[*][b]travel [/b]across vast distances in Albion[/*]	[*][b]explore [/b]a new environment full of resources and treasures[/*]	[*][b]live [/b]within a new environment away from the Outlands[/*][/list]
They are ideally suited to [b]small group gameplay[/b], since they have unique mechanics that limit the number of players that can enter at one time.

This video covers the first topic, [b]travel[/b], and is split into two parts: how to [b]find and enter[/b] a Road, and how to use it to [b]get around the world of Albion[/b].
[h3]Finding and Entering Roads[/h3]
To enter the Roads, you will have to find a [b]gateway to Avalon[/b]. They have a limited capacity for how many travellers can pass through them in each direction, and must [b]recharge[/b] before additional players can enter or leave. The smallest will only let two players pass before its capacity is depleted, while the larger ones will allow small to medium size groups to pass.

The gateways also have a [b]limited lifetime[/b], so be sure to check how much time a gateway has left if you plan to return to where you started.

Once you enter a gateway, you’ll find yourself in the ancient kingdom of Avalon, specifically its road network. These ancient roads were built aeons ago by the Avalonians, who are now reactivating the mechanisms that power the gateways and the paths that connect them.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8ddb3a5a77680279443f297e59bb6be682322123.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]Traveling via Roads of Avalon[/h3]
The Roads themselves connect different possible gateway positions, and are kept [b]free of enemy creatures[/b] by Avalonian magic. You can also use the power imbued in the roads to [b]speed you along[/b] as you move between gateways.

Each gateway connects to one of three places:
[list]	[*]an Outlands zone[/*]	[*]a Royal Continent zone[/*]	[*]a different section of the Roads of Avalon[/*][/list]
Exploring will uncover [b]shortcuts[/b] through the world of Albion, which you can use for numerous purposes, including:
[list]	[*]transport[/*]	[*]trade[/*]	[*]outmaneuvering enemies[/*]	[*]accessing resources and dungeons far from your starting position[/*][/list]
You will have to keep track of the [b]remaining lifetime[/b] of each gateway you pass through, as the Roads of Avalon are constantly shifting and any given gateway may soon disappear forever, only to re-open to a different location in Albion.
[h3]Next Up: The Wilds of Avalon[/h3]
This concludes our introduction to the Roads of Avalon. Join us for the next Dev Talk, where we’ll discuss what happens when you leave the Roads and venture into the wilderness beyond. Thanks for watching!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Corrupted Dungeons
notes.content:
The [b]Rise of Avalon[/b] update arrives in August, bringing major new gameplay features to the world of Albion. One such feature is [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], a new type of single-player dungeon that will bring new dimensions to solo play in Albion Online. In this Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys discusses what these dungeons are and how they work.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9V0yKOzmitE
No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...

The all-new [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b] arriving with the next update are a response to those players who have been asking for more [b]solo PvE and PvP content[/b] for Albion Online. But what are they exactly, and how do they work?
[h3]The Basics[/h3]
To find a Corrupted Dungeon, you’ll need to explore the open world and find a [b]Corrupted Dungeon Entrance[/b]. These spawn like regular Solo Randomized Dungeons, but they look a good deal more sinister.

When entering a Corrupted Dungeon, you can choose your difficulty level:
[list]	[*][b]Hunter[/b]: lower rewards, knockdown PvP rules, relatively low Item Power softcap. A good difficulty for anyone learning the basics of 1v1 PvP in Albion.[/*]	[*][b]Stalker[/b]: full-loot PvP rules with significantly higher rewards, but still a low Item Power Softcap. A good level for veteran PvP players.[/*]	[*][b]Slayer[/b]: even greater rewards, full-loot PvP, a bigger PvE challenge, and a much higher Item Power softcap. This is the elite level aimed at advanced players.[/*][/list][h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a44912111053fe63f9ae885f954524d4f92f5b34.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]What's Inside?[/h3]
After choosing your difficulty level and entering the dungeon, you’ll find yourself in a place infested with demons and corrupted creatures. To complete the dungeon, you'll have to cleanse these creatures. Each creature slain will award [b]Infamy[/b] points. Different enemies will yield different amounts of infamy based on their difficulty.

When you’ve collected enough Infamy points, the final boss in the dungeon appears. By defeating it, you can lay claim to the loot rewards of the dungeon. In addition, the Infamy gained will remain with you, showing your place in the [b]Infamy rankings[/b] as well as [b]permanently boosting your rewards[/b] in Corrupted Dungeons.

Finally, at the end of a dungeon run, a portal to another Corrupted Dungeon appears and allows you to start another dungeon right away - or you can leave and take your loot back to the city.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/904c4b7ce4853669f8b97934328854dce9ee693c.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]How Does PvP Work?[/h3]
In every corrupted dungeon is a [b]demonic shrine[/b] which players can use to sign themselves up to invade other players. Once a player has signed up, the game will regularly check for a potential invasion target. If such a target is found, the invading player will be pulled from their dungeon into another player’s dungeon.

The defending player now has two options:
[list]	[*]they can rally and [b]fight the invader[/b], or[/*]	[*]they can try to destroy the [b]demonic shards[/b] which appeared in their dungeon along with the invader.[/*][/list]
If they succeed in destroying enough of these shards, the Invader is banished and the defender can continue playing their own dungeon.

If either player kills the other, the victim loses some of their infamy, and the killer gains some of it. This allows players to gain very high infamy numbers and rise in the ranks for their own  prominence - and for significant boosts to future dungeon rewards.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/84842a373ff910c54c88d3365b549323a5ab636d.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]Special Features of Corrupted Dungeons[/h3]
To add tactics and depth to these encounters, there are a number of [b]special features[/b] players can use to try to outsmart their opponents:
[list]	[*]NPC positions are marked on the minimap, allowing you to guess your opponent's position based on the creatures they’ve already slain[/*]	[*]Watcher demons will mark any player they encounter on the minimap for their opponent to see[/*]	[*]And last but not least, there are a large number of [b]traps and hazards[/b] which you will need to avoid, or actively use to outsmart and defeat your opponent[/*][/list][h3]In Conclusion[/h3]
As you can see, there's a lot to this feature, and we hope you’re looking forward to exploring and fighting in the Corrupted Dungeons when the Rise of Avalon update launches.

That's all for today - you can also look forward to our next Dev Talk, in which we’ll go in-depth with the [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] and their impact on the world of Albion Online.

tags.feature: The all-new [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b] arriving with the next update are a response to those players who have been asking for more [b]solo PvE and PvP content[/b] for Albion Online.
To find a Corrupted Dungeon, you’ll need to explore the open world and find a [b]Corrupted Dungeon Entrance[/b].
When entering a Corrupted Dungeon, you can choose your difficulty level:
Hunter: lower rewards, knockdown PvP rules, relatively low Item Power softcap. A good difficulty for anyone learning the basics of 1v1 PvP in Albion.
Stalker: full-loot PvP rules with significantly higher rewards, but still a low Item Power Softcap. A good level for veteran PvP players.
Slayer: even greater rewards, full-loot PvP, a bigger PvE challenge, and a much higher Item Power softcap. This is the elite level aimed at advanced players.
After choosing your difficulty level and entering the dungeon, you’ll find yourself in a place infested with demons and corrupted creatures.
To complete the dungeon, you'll have to cleanse these creatures.
Each creature slain will award [b]Infamy[/b] points.
Different enemies will yield different amounts of infamy based on their difficulty.
When you’ve collected enough Infamy points, the final boss in the dungeon appears.
By defeating it, you can lay claim to the loot rewards of the dungeon.
In addition, the Infamy gained will remain with you, showing your place in the [b]Infamy rankings[/b] as well as [b]permanently boosting your rewards[/b] in Corrupted Dungeons.
Finally, at the end of a dungeon run, a portal to another Corrupted Dungeon appears and allows you to start another dungeon right away - or you can leave and take your loot back to the city.
In every corrupted dungeon is a [b]demonic shrine[/b] which players can use to sign themselves up to invade other players.
Once a player has signed up, the game will regularly check for a potential invasion target.
If such a target is found, the invading player will be pulled from their dungeon into another player’s dungeon.
The defending player now has two options:
they can rally and [b]fight the invader[/b], or
they can try to destroy the [b]demonic shards[/b] which appeared in their dungeon along with the invader.
If they succeed in destroying enough of these shards, the Invader is banished and the defender can continue playing their own dungeon.
If either player kills the other, the victim loses some of their infamy, and the killer gains some of it.
This allows players to gain very high infamy numbers and rise in the ranks for their own prominence - and for significant boosts to future dungeon rewards.
To add tactics and depth to these encounters, there are a number of [b]special features[/b] players can use to try to outsmart their opponents:
NPC positions are marked on the minimap, allowing you to guess your opponent's position based on the creatures they’ve already slain
Watcher demons will mark any player they encounter on the minimap for their opponent to see
And last but not least, there are a large number of [b]traps and hazards[/b] which you will need to avoid, or actively use to outsmart and defeat your opponent

notes.title: The Undead Challenge Returns
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3e242a1b947baf56706d069dee545e1a8275630a.jpeg[/img]

The dead just won't stay buried! For the entire month of July, take the [b]Undead Challenge[/b] to unlock fantastic rewards. Earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your very own [b]Spectral Direboar[/b].
[h3][b]The Afterlife Goes On[/b][/h3]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Emqzvgr.png[/img][b]SPECTRAL DIREBOAR:[/b] This month's Challenge brings back the popular [b]Spectral Direboar[/b], a ghostly mount with a unique spell, [b]Glimpse of the Other Side[/b], which renders you temporarily invisible. Use it to evade your enemies... or to launch a sneak attack!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TR1A3xK.png[/img][b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Adventurers who rack up enough total Challenge Points will also earn the [b]Undead Challenge avatar ring[/b], featuring a spooky skull-themed design that will strike fear into the hearts of your foes. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this avatar border for one character, or can be traded to the Vanity Merchant for one Vanity Token.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1e0fca1206375091962832c1c6ba85f1937fa559.png[/img][b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Undead Challenge chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes and Silver, you'll also have a chance to unlock spooky furniture items like the Candelabra, Lantern, and Memorial of the Fallen, as well as rare and valuable [b]Undead Vanity Skins[/b].
 
As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount / avatar ring reward. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while you can!

notes.title: Dev Talk: Avalonian Weapons
notes.content:
The next major content update for Albion Online, [b]Rise of Avalon[/b], will arrive in August (watch the new teaser trailer for the update [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/rise-of-avalon-coming-this-august][b]here[/b][/url]). In our newest Dev Talk, Combat Designer Michael Schwahn discusses the all-new [b]Avalonian Weapon[/b] lines that are coming to the game.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LBkTCxPu5sg
No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Read on...
[h3]Overview[/h3][list]	[*]Albion Online's first [b]major weapon expansion[/b] since the release of Level 3 artifacts[/*]	[*]The weapon lines were first conceived when we began designing the [b]Avalonian faction[/b][/*]	[*]Includes 15 artifact weapons (one for each weapon family) and 3 offhands[/*]	[*]Each item will be available from [b]T4 to T8[/b], for a total of [b]90 new weapon models [/b][/*]	[*]Will completely [b]shift the meta[/b][/*][/list]
But how exactly will they change the meta, and who are they for? First off, unlike Level 3 Artifacts, Avalonian Weapons are useful for a [b]wide variety of applications and situations[/b], from solo play to small-group PvP to large battles. The weapons will come with a wide variety of [b]exciting new mechanics[/b] that will keep combat in Albion fresh and unpredictable.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b698b1c223eff1ea64a8cbf54c5638db734cc3a9.jpeg[/img]

Let's take a look at some examples:

[b]1. Lucent Hawk (Bow)[/b]

Upon activation, you can shoot up to four high-impact, long-range skillshots in a row. You only have a short time window between each shot to fire the next arrow. This ability temporarily turns you into a deadly sniper, but you'll have to be very careful to not get interrupted, or you'll lose the remaining shots.

[b]2. Majestic Smash (Two-Handed Sword)[/b]
Next we have the two handed sword, the [b]Kingmaker[/b]. Its ability lets you swing your blade and knock all enemies around you into the air, then follow with a heavy vertical attack which deals massive damage along a line. If you're correctly positioned when using this ability, you'll be rewarded by hitting multiple targets with it, dealing tons of extra damage on top of the CC effects.

[b]3. Inner Shadow (Cursed Staff)[/b]
This ability can be cast on [b]any player[/b] (ally or enemy). It draws a shadow ghost out of the player, which inflicts an AoE attack. The type of shadow depends on the armor of the [b]target[/b]:
[list]	[*][b]Cloth Armor[/b]: summons a mage shadow which creates a lightning area that deals damage[/*]	[*][b]Leather Armor[/b]: shadow creates a life steal aura which heals the caster[/*]	[*][b]Plate Armor[/b]: summons a tank that slows enemies and shreds their armor after a short delay[/*][/list]
Since the summoned shadow depends on the armor of the target and not the caster, it allows for a lot of versatility and interesting decision-making during combat.

[b]4. Line Breaker (Spear)[/b]
The Avalonian Spear is a one-handed lance. After a short cast time, you charge at your enemies, during which you are unstoppable and immune to any kind of CC. When you hit an enemy, you purge all their buffs and deal a large amount of damage.

As this is a [b]one-handed weapon[/b], you can combine it with all sorts of offhands for different effects. In fact, many of the new weapons are one-handed to allow for more interesting offhand combinations on higher artifact gear.

[b]5. Soul Link (Nature Staff)[/b]

This ability temporarily links two targets together. The effect of the link depends on the targets' alignments relative to the caster:
[list]	[*][b]2 Allies[/b]: damage taken is now [b]evenly shared[/b] between the two targets, and their healing received is also [b]shared and amplified[/b][/*]	[*][b]Ally / Enemy[/b]: some of the enemy’s Healing Received is stolen and transferred to the ally[/*]	[*][b]2 Enemies[/b]: damage taken is evenly shared, and also [b]amplified[/b][/*][/list]
As you can see, these unique new abilities bring exciting new opportunities to combat in Albion. Keep in mind these abilities are still in production, and the final behavior may still change during testing.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1677fdaf97e99e95a7ee19477a13808e9c1cdb30.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Crafting[/h3]
So how can you obtain these new weapons? The weapons can be crafted with the use of new [b]Artifacts[/b]. In addition to being obtained directly, these artifacts can also be forged from [b]Avalonian Shards[/b].

Essentially, the crafting works just like with the Avalonian Armors. However, with the next update we will also increase the availability of Avalonian Shards, and you will be able to find Shards when exploring the upcoming [b]Roads of Avalon[/b].
[h3]Destiny Board[/h3]
With the Rise of Avalon update, we are splitting the Destiny Board artifact specialization nodes into [b]one node per artifact[/b]. This applies to both [b]combat and crafting[/b]. The Fame requirements will be adjusted so that each artifact specialization node levels [b]at the same pace as a regular node[/b].

All the existing Fame that players already have in their artifact specialization nodes will be evenly distributed into the specialization nodes for the individual items in that node. This means if you have the Artifact Sword Combat Specialist at level 70, the Fame of that node will then be split evenly into the three new specialization nodes for the individual items: Clarent Blade, Carving Sword, and Galatine Pair. The new node for the Avalonian Sword would start at zero.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c666be2ddf88b11e28f238ab6cdce2907b87aad1.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Balancing[/h3]
In addition to these exciting new weapon lines coming with the next update, we are also adjusting the 1v1 combat balance for the new [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], which feature 1v1 PvP. We'll discuss these dungeons much more in-depth in an upcoming video.

That's all for today - thanks for listening, and stay tuned for more Dev Talks in the coming weeks!

notes.title: Rise of Avalon - Coming This August
notes.content:
It's official: the next major update for Albion Online, [b]Rise of Avalon[/b], will launch in August! Watch the teaser trailer here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nJh0W3_sIis
Here's short synopsis of some of the major features:
[h3]Avalonian Weapons: The Next Step in Combat[/h3]
New weapons that use the long-dormant technologies of the mighty Avalonians will bring tremendous shifts to combat in Albion Online. From the fearsome [b]Avalonian Cannon[/b] with its continually movable beam to the [b]Avalonian Cursed Staff [/b]that summons an enemy's cursed inner spirit, these weapons will shake up Albion's combat meta and keep battles fresh, fun, and unpredictable.
[h3]Roads of Avalon: In the Footsteps of the Ancients[/h3]
[b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are paths that have been hidden in the mists of Albion for millennia. This mystical new realm will soon be yours to explore, offering new wonders... and new dangers. In addition to creating unique and ever-changing [b]connections[/b] throughout the world, they will be a source for valuable loot and resources for those willing to delve deep into the unknown. And for those looking to live outside the political sphere of the Outlands, the Roads of Avalon will even have spots where [b]Hideouts[/b] can be constructed.
[h3]Corrupted Dungeons: Face Your Demons[/h3]
The sanctified Roads of Avalon will have their dark counterpart in the new [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b], realms of darkness and fire brought forth by demonic forces. These new dungeons close once entered, offering a new type of single-player PvE experience. But beware: they can also be [b]invaded[/b] by other players seeking to hunt down those facing the demons, leading to 1v1 PvP fights among demonic foes and hazards.

A whole series of Dev Talks on these new features are in the works, which we'll be releasing over the coming weeks, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Queen Patch 14 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/242d972fdb91518d8e10467f95fa0b3fe66c79c1.jpeg[/img]

As our Game Director discussed in our latest [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/development-progress-update][b]video[/b][/url], while we've been hard at work preparing new features, we've also been supporting and enriching the current [b]Queen Update[/b]. Today' patch brings further adjustments and refinements to the [b]Smart Cluster Queue[/b] system introduced with Queen, closing a loophole that allowed large armies to lock out smaller ones, alongside other fixes and improvements.
[h3]Smart Cluster Queue Adjustments[/h3][list]	[*][b]Queue Removal Protection status[/b]: players removed from a zone now receive a protected status that allows them to wait for one queue cycle[/*]	[*][b]Early Retreat Debuff[/b]: players who enter via the queue and immediately leave now cannot re-queue for 10 minutes[/*]	[*][b]Queue Cycle Time[/b]: increased from 90 to 120 seconds[/*][/list]
These changes are designed to better balance armies of different sizes, and to more effectively implement the goals of this system. For a more in-depth discussion of these changes, please [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/131458][b]see[/b] [b]this forum post[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9b8153d392cfdcd06d0850b6a780411dbd673461.jpeg[/img]
[h3]Mobile Improvements and Fixes[/h3]
Patch 14 brings further improvements and fixes for mobile, including the ability to [b]drag-paste items into chat[/b] and fixes for [b]drag-context menus and spell tooltips[/b]. The game now has more mobile players than ever, and over the coming months we will continue to improve the overall mobile experience in Albion Online. If you have feedback about the mobile version, or just want to keep up on news and announcements, check out the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Board/138-Mobile-Version/][b]Mobile Forum[/b][/url].

As always, for a full list of changes and fixes, check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%2014][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Development Progress Update
notes.content:
In our newest video, Albion's Game Director Robin Henkys checks in from his home office with an update on the game's development progress. After catching up with everything that's happened over the past months, he looks forward to Albion's next major content update and covers some of the major features it will contain.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Rok0ZCFRz3k
No time to watch, or prefer a written summary? Then read on...
[h3]The Queen Update[/h3]
January saw the launch of the massive and highly successful Queen update, which brought an entire new Outlands continent and numerous new high-level gameplay options to the world of Albion. Since then, we've been working nonstop to support this update, and to date we've release thirteen patches with numerous fixes and improvements:
[list]	[*]Fixing [b]critical technical issues[/b], especially for Windows 7 users[/*]	[*]Improving [b]loot and rewards[/b][/*]	[*][b]Adjusting ingame systems[/b] to make them more fun and rewarding[/*]	[*]Conducting a massive [b]Alliance test[/b] with penalties for holding more territories[/*]	[*]Updating the way [b]portals [/b]work[/*]	[*]Introducing a completely reworked [b]mobile UI [/b]and working on the stability of the mobile version[/*][/list]
We're of course continuing to support this update in various ways, including fixing exploits within the Smart Cluster Queue system and making adjustments and improvements to mount stats.
[h3]What's Next?[/h3]
Of course, everyone's here to find out what's happening with the next update. We've made a ton of progress toward the next update, far too much to cover in a single video, and soon we'll be releasing a whole series of Dev Talks with in-depth information about each topic.

Today we'll take a brief look at each of the major features that are coming. These features are in the final stages of development, and are about four weeks from being finished. With such massive features, though, we want to really take our time to make sure their implementation is as flawless as possible, so we want to make sure we test them properly. This means the next update will likely happen [b]after the end of Season 9[/b], and will be in place for the start of Season 10.

So what are some of the major features coming?
[h3]Avalonian Weapons[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b1d5017bda55579d9c1675f4863abd06727a162c.png[/img]

One of the most anticipated features of the new update is the new [b]Avalonian Weapons[/b]. There will be [b]fifteen new weapons[/b] with entirely new spells, and even more excitingly, with [b]all-new mechanics[/b]. Examples:
[list]	[*]Avalonian Cannon: allows retargeting while the weapon is still firing[/*]	[*]Mimic: allows you to steal an enemy's ability and use it against them[/*][/list]
The new Avalonian Weapons will shake up the meta quite a bit, and unlike the current Artifact Weapons, they will be useful for all levels of play, from small-scale to large-scale combat.

These new weapons will be covered in much more detail in an upcoming Dev Talk.
[h3]Corrupted Dungeons[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c2846ae4ef560e19147d4353690996efe56aa468.png[/img]

Another major feature coming with the next update is [b]Corrupted Dungeons[/b]. For those who missed the last Dev Talk, Corrupted Dungeons are like regular dungeons that have been [b]infected, reshaped, and taken over[/b] by demons. When a player enters, the entrance closes behind them, meaning no one can [b]directly[/b] follow them in. However, there is a way to invade these dungeons by making a pact with the demons, allowing you to hunt down players who are trying to cleanse these dungeons.

Corrupted Dungeons offer [b]an entirely new dimension of 1v1 PvP[/b] in Albion, as well as [b]an entirely new one-player PvE experience[/b] with completely new dungeon layouts, hazards, and mobs. These dungeons will also be covered at length in an upcoming Dev Talk.
[h3]Roads of Avalon[/h3]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7f5d2e5789c5768c96e7716bf3ab3056482eacf8.png[/img]

The [b]Roads of Avalon[/b] are a massive new game feature that opens up [b]three entirely new ways of playing[/b]:
[list]	[*]They create [b]connections[/b], allowing you to find shortcuts through the world for travel, trade, and relocating.[/*]	[*]They allow [b]exploration[/b], and will contain lots of exciting new creatures to fight and resource spots to exploit.[/*]	[*]And most excitingly, players will have the opportunity to [b]live within the Roads[/b] via Hideouts, shielded somewhat from the politics of the Outlands and developing their own unique style of play.[/*][/list]
We'll have a whole mini-series of Dev Talks explaining these different features of the Roads of Avalon soon.

Thanks for joining for this special from-home talk – hopefully our upcoming videos will be from the office once again. Stay tuned for more Dev Talks coming soon!

notes.title: Queen Patch 13 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c34601151414454e09d9db18cdaaa59617fe1f99.jpeg[/img]

The thirteenth patch of the Queen update is now live, bringing optimizations to the Arena system and more chances to find Solo Randomized Dungeons in blue and yellow zones. Here's what's new:
[h3]Arena Improvements[/h3]
The overall Fame earned from an Arena win has been [b]doubled[/b], from 20,000 Fame to 40,000 Fame per player on the winning team. And to make the Arena more lucrative for healers, winning players in a healing role will now receive an additional [b]Adept's Tome of Insight[/b] worth 10,000 Fame on top of the regular rewards.

Additionally, the Arena signup and notification UIs have been improved and streamlined, and clearly show the available daily rewards for each role. If you haven't played an Arena match in a while, or have yet to visit the Arena, now is the perfect time!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1bf4f5eeb38d5d9136326ba8d4dc94f4b2e740e1.png[/img]
[h3]More Solo Randomized Dungeons in Safe Zones[/h3]
In order to give beginner and intermediate-level players greater access to Solo Randomized Dungeons, the entrances of these dungeons in blue and yellow zones will now [b]disappear a short time after the last player enters[/b]. Once a given entry portal is removed, a new entry portal is free to spawn elsewhere in the world. This will increase the overall number of "fresh" dungeons in these zones, giving newer players greater access to the full dungeon experience while still allowing players to run solo dungeons together and follow others into a dungeon within a reasonable time window.
[h3]Zerg Changes and More[/h3]
Players waiting in a Smart Cluster Queue now [b]contribute to the total Disarray headcount[/b] in the cluster for which they are queueing, while the overall curve for the Disarray debuff now [b]accelerates more slowly[/b].

Quality-of-life improvements now include a [b]Destiny Board view prompt[/b] when a certain building type is not yet unlocked, plus improved descriptions for spells with scaled effects due to stacks.

As always, for the full details, you can check out the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/QUEEN%20PATCH%2013][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

And to make the Arena more lucrative for healers, winning players in a healing role will now receive an additional Adept's Tome of Insight worth 10,000 Fame on top of the regular rewards.

Players waiting in a Smart Cluster Queue now contribute to the total Disarray headcount in the cluster for which they are queueing, while the overall curve for the Disarray debuff now accelerates more slowly.

notes.title: Population Update: May 2020
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/9e84ebc0711a79cb9eb8264690acb0d7f67610f2.jpeg[/img]

The [url=https://albiononline.com/en/update/Queen][b]Queen Update[/b][/url], released January 20, 2020, was by far the most successful Albion Online content update since launch, confirmed by consistent population growth since January and a record-high of over [b]500,000 monthly users[/b] for the month of April. Nearly six months in the making, Queen was nothing less than a complete revisioning of Albion's high-level endgame, although the new features and systems it introduced affected players of all levels and playstyles.

On a more bittersweet note, player numbers have also been affected by the lockdown and quarantine measures worldwide. We know many in the Albion Online community have been touched by the current pandemic, and are facing numerous present and future challenges. Games in general have seen a tremendous surge in popularity over the past months, and Albion Online is no exception – and as unfortunate as the reason behind it may be, we're grateful for those in our community who have stepped up to support each other, help out new players, [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/over-40000-raised-for-charity][b]raise funds for charity[/b][/url], and make the Albion community even stronger during these uncertain times.

For us, as the developers of the game, increased player numbers mean [b]increased responsibility to all our players[/b] to ensure the game's performance remains optimal, and that gameplay remains fun, accessible, and fresh. To make sure we keep up with the increased resource demands of a growing population, we're designating [b]dedicated performance developers[/b] to make sure the game runs as smoothly as possible, and implementing [b]game design changes, balancing, and improvements[/b] with a larger player base in mind (such as the recent increase in Solo Randomized Dungeon spawns with Patch 11).

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3f62750de37449b1711f0b1a93cc50fb439ded80.jpeg[/img]

Another positive effect of this uptrend (which started even before the Queen launch) is that it allows us to further expand our development team. Those looking to join the Sandbox Interactive team, or who know others who might be interested, can check out a list of available positions on our [url=https://albiononline.com/en/jobs][b]jobs page[/b][/url].

Thanks for your loyalty to, and support of, Albion Online over the past year. We're happy to welcome new players to the world of Albion, and very excited to bring some [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-whats-next][b]major new features[/b][/url] to the ever-growing world of Albion.

notes.title: Season 8 Wrapup
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/ad18578bbd5379a49f0b6c28095cbcb6876448e1.jpeg[/img]

[b]Guild Season 8[/b] saw major changes to guild warfare in Albion Online, as well as a massive change to the land of Albion itself in the form of [b]a whole new Outlands continent[/b]. The interplay of these new regions and systems presented both challenges and opportunities for guilds of all sizes and opened up the playing field for a new champion to take the crown. Congratulations to [b]Sex with Ex[/b] for emerging victorious among a highly competitive field of challengers and claiming their first-ever season victory!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/15231728415aaf88abf426d514ba3231c7b9ff07.jpeg[/img]

Season 8 started on February 1, directly after the release of the Queen update. Veteran guild [b]Conflict[/b] took an early lead on Invasion Day, with last season's second-place winners [b]Black Order[/b], [b]HustlinHitmans[/b], three-time champions [b]Blue Army[/b], and last season's third-place winners [b]RAQ [/b]rounding out the top five. But already within the first week, newcomers [b]Sex with Ex[/b] had risen through the ranks to first place, where they would remain by fending off numerous challenges throughout the remainder of the season.

With the new Crystal League in play, [b]Final Order[/b] managed to break into the top five over the following weeks until being supplanted by [b]Agresor[/b]. After the first Territory Reset (on Leap Day 2020), the top 3 stood at [b]Sex with Ex[/b], [b]Black Order[/b], and [b]Conflict[/b].

On March 6, the AO Daily Show aired [b]an interview with Arista[/b], GM of Sex with Ex, in which he shared their hardworking approach to staying on top in an open-world-based season - click [url=https://www.twitch.tv/videos/562909711?filter=highlights&sort=time][b]here[/b][/url] to watch.

By mid-March, [b]Agresor[/b] had broken into the top three, on their eventual way to edging out [b]Black Order[/b] for second place overall. The final ranking was cemented after the Territory Reset on March 28, despite a last-minute push by Agresor to take first place by winning the final Level 8 and 9 Crystal League matches with hand-picked 5-man teams. Ultimately, the final Crystal League showdowns, while thrilling (and lucrative for the participants), weren't enough to upend the final rankings.

Congrats again to [b]Sex with Ex[/b] and all the top-ten teams:

notes.title: The Season 9 Patch is Coming
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5d596d414e91aae98bb32a524960b8383695d0a1.jpeg[/img]

On Tuesday, May 5, Queen Patch 11, also known as the [b]Season 9 Patch[/b], will go live. This patch includes numerous updates, changes, quality-of-life improvements, and bug fixes that affect nearly every aspect of gameplay. Here are some of the major changes it will bring:
[h3]A Whole New Mobile Experience[/h3]
Patch 11 brings the first version of an all new way to play Albion on mobile devices. These new mobile features apply to both iOS and Android, and include the following:
[list]	[*]A [b]virtual joystick[/b] for movement that snaps to the initial press position[/*]	[*][b]Auto-targeting[/b] of attacks and spells[/*]	[*][b]Context-based interactions[/b] with the world[/*]	[*]Updated [b]HUD layout[/b][/*]	[*]Default [b]in-game zoom level[/b] increased[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/94f439a9e18e7f4a2701c83d18e829b14fd72460.jpeg[/img]

For more details about these changes, including work-in-progress screenshots, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/128104-Mobile-Beta-Changelog-Queen-Patch-11-Update/][b]this forum post[/b][/url].
[h3]Outlands Banks[/h3]
The shady underworld organization behind the Black Market has branched out, and now offers [b]personal bank space at numerous Outlands locations[/b]. 

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/5df965f269b954064d8d63e8a6746ea614dae14f.jpeg[/img]

Any given Outlands Bank location can be unlocked with a one-time Silver payment and used forever, and any number of locations can be unlocked. But watch out: while these banks may offer protection for your gear, they're situated in full-loot PvP zones.
[h3]Guild Season Changes[/h3]
Patch 11 brings wide-reaching changes to guild warfare in Albion. First and foremost is the new [b]Season Point and Energy Storage[/b] system, where higher-level territories hold onto a portion of all generated Season Points and Siphoned Energy until the end of the current season phase. The amount of Season Points and Energy the territory holds onto increases with its proximity to the center of the Outlands, encouraging clashes between large guilds and alliances while offering smaller guilds increased rewards for conquering and holding a territory.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/884089b17cf05c7025ddad83a9b12051b7238230.jpeg[/img][/h3]
Other Guild Season changes include:
[list]	[*]Season Points from Veteran and World Bosses[/*]	[*]Crystal League Tokens now purchasable up to Lv.3[/*]	[*]Updated Crystal League schedule and reward pools[/*]	[*]Adjustments to Energy, Fame and Silver penalties for larger alliances[/*][/list][h3]UI and Map Improvements[/h3]
Patch 11 will introduce a wide range of quality-of-life improvements to make navigating the world of Albion much easier. UI improvements include an updated mail system, improved building interface, clearer carry capacity display, and new icons for numerous weapon skills. The world map visuals have been improved and reworked, and zones can now be viewed by prime time.
[h3][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/b5b2f8a2b2d8d159cca1c686885dd97df91956da.jpeg[/img][/h3][h3]Additional Improvements[/h3][list]	[*]Increased Fame and Silver from high-level enemies[/*]	[*]Terrain adjustments to improve player visibility[/*]	[*]Updated mount and farming sounds[/*]	[*]Faster potion crafting[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
Alongside these updates, we've also been hard at work on several major upcoming features, including [b]Corrupted Dungeons [/b]and [b]Roads of Avalon[/b]. If you missed our Game Director's latest Dev Talk on these topics, you can check it out [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-whats-next][b]here[/b][/url].
