notes.title: Player and Item Migration with the Queen Update
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/16b7aec4c97ea3ec5a7841121d77c2109d4b6d35.jpeg[/img]

The Queen update arrives on [b]January 20, 2020[/b]. With this update, the [b]Outlands [/b]will be completely reworked, and with very few exceptions, [b]all territories and siege camps in the Royal Continent will be removed[/b]. We have put a number of measures in place to assist with this transition, but as there is the potential for item loss, please read the following changes carefully.
[h1]Migrating Players and Items[/h1]
[b]1. Players:[/b]
[list]	[*]Players in the [b]Outlands [/b]will be moved to the city with the portal closest to them. Even though the Caerleon portals will no longer exist, for this transfer, Caerleon is included among these cities.[/*]	[*]Players in [b]affected zones in the Royal continent[/b] (i.e. those that had [b]territories or siege camps[/b]) will be moved to the nearest zone entrance.[/*][/list]
[b]2. Banks and Battlevaults:[/b]
[list]	[*]All personal items in [b]banks and battlevaults[/b] in the Outlands, or in a removed Royal Territory or Siege Camp, will be [b]moved to the Royal City that is closest or has the closest portal[/b].[/*]	[*][b]Guild banks in territories[/b] will be moved to the owning guild's [b]Guild Island Bank[/b].[/*]	[*]Territory bank [b]tabs [/b](and their corresponding access rights) will be copied to the Guild Island Bank.[/*]	[*]If the guild doesn't own a Guild Island, [b]the items will be destroyed[/b].[/*][/list]
[b]3. Islands:[/b]
[list]	[*]Personal and guild islands [b]will be movable[/b] during the month following the Queen update. This is currently slated for January 20 10:01 UTC to February 20 10:00 UTC.[/*]	[*]Only islands created prior to the launch of the Queen update are eligible to be moved.[/*]	[*]Islands moved during the last island move are still eligible to be moved once more after the Queen update.[/*][/list]
[b]4. Items that will NOT be moved:[/b]
[list]	[*]Items currently for sale or in the completed tab of [b]Marketplaces in Guild Home Territories [/b]will [b]not[/b] be moved. This means that any items in Marketplaces in the Outlands when Queen goes live [b]will be lost[/b].[/*]	[*]Contents of placeable chests, as well as all placed furniture items, [b]will not be moved[/b] and will be destroyed.[/*]	[*][b]Farmable items left in territories[/b] will be destroyed.[/*]	[*][b]Buildings left in territories[/b], including farms and pastures, will be destroyed.[/*][/list]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/4f393a4cbb15580ed778f197571cc44677461722.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Amnesty for Low Reputations[/h1]
With the changes to the Outlands, and particularly the destruction of the Caerleon Realmgate, movement restrictions due to reputation will be mitigated as follows:
[list]	[*]Players below -15000 reputation [b]will have their reputation adjusted to -15000[/b] to allow movement within [b]yellow and red zones[/b].[/*]	[*]However, as Caerleon will no longer have a Realmgate to the Outlands, if a Dreaded player enters Caerleon (after re-lowering their reputation in a neighboring red zone), their [b]only options[/b] are to wait for their reputation to increase or fast travel to another city.[/*][/list]

notes.title: Refer One Friend and Get an Armored Bonehorse Skin!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/c3963410874d3ad3c4b1a126977e6d301a9d0665.png[/img]

Starting December 1, our special referral offer is back: for just [b]one referral[/b], you can get your very own [b]mount skin[/b]! The [b]Armored Bonehorse[/b] skin gives any Armored Horse base mount a fearsome undead look - and once you've unlocked it, it can be used by [b]all characters[/b] on your account forever!

On top of that, as with the last season you can earn [b]huge amounts of Fame[/b] for your third and fifth referrals: three referrals scores you a [b]T7 Pile of Tomes[/b], worth a whopping [b]100,000 Fame[/b], and five referrals gets you a [b]T8 Pile of Tomes[/b], granting a colossal [b]200,000 Fame[/b]. And as always, your first-ever referral grants an additional T8 Pile of Tomes [b]along with the Armored Bonehorse skin[/b]!

The current referral season lasts until maintenance on [b]February 1[/b], so you've got until then to refer your friends and claim your rewards.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a69055098a00635554a906ccdfa4322fbd5ce5cc.png[/img]
[h1]How to Earn Seasonal Referral Rewards[/h1][list]	[*]Send your referral link, which you can find [url=https://albiononline.com/en/profile/referral/overview][b]here[/b][/url], to a friend. (You must be logged into your account on the website to view this page.)[/*]	[*]Your friend registers an account and starts playing Albion Online (preferably along with you!).[/*]	[*]The first time your friend purchases at least 30 days of Premium, they will trigger a reward for you.[/*]	[*]On top of that, for your very first referral ever, you'll receive a [b]T8 Recruiter's Pile of Tomes[/b], worth a whopping [b]200,000 Fame[/b].[/*][/list]

notes.title: The Yuletide Challenge is Back!
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/018abb2522e1b1feab3288d50274986151fbcafc.jpeg[/img]

Winter has descended on the land of Albion, Avalonians are stalking the Outlands – and the next Adventurer's Challenge is here! For all of December, the [b]Yuletide Challenge[/b] lets you earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your own [b]Snow Husky[/b]. And for this month only, weekly chests include [b]Avalonian Energy[/b], which lets you craft powerful new items at the Energy Manipulator.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GFhcqPG.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Let it Snow[/b][/h1]
[b]SNOW HUSKY:[/b] This month, you'll have another chance to claim the charming [b]Snow Husky[/b], a handsome canine companion that will carry you through Albion's harshest terrain. Along with its strong base move speed, its Hunting Instinct spell gives a short but powerful speed burst.
 
[b]AVATAR RING:[/b] Along with the Snow Husky, adventurers who reach this month's total point goal will unlock the [b]Yuletide Challenge Ring[/b], which will give your avatar a cheery holiday look any time of year. And remember: unclaimed Adventurer's Challenge Rings can also be traded in for Adventurer's Tokens (details below).

[b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] Unlock Yuletide Challenge chests to get a mix of holiday-themed prizes, along with the regular goodies like Silver bags, Fame Tomes, and resources. Each chest has a chance to give the [b]Yule Outfit [/b]costume set, [b]Decorated Trees[/b], and [b]Present Box[/b] furniture items, along with...
 
[b]AVALONIAN ENERGY:[/b] This month only, Yuletide Challenge chests will contain [b]Avalonian Energy[/b], the powerful and mysterious new resource that is the source of the Avalonian faction's power. Use it to upgrade your food and tools, and even create a new mount, at the Energy Manipulator!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/a1435efc56738227796e1d1f6fe5378edc8a17a1.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Adventurer Tokens[/h1]
As a reminder, you can now trade any unused Adventurer's Challenge Avatar Rings, whether or now you already own the ring, for [b]Adventurer Tokens[/b] at the Vanity Merchant. These tokens can then be redeemed at the same merchant for the new [b]Adventurer Avatar[/b] or [b]Adventurer Avatar Ring[/b], with more options coming soon.

notes.title: Percival Patch 11 is Here
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/7f14f2a3213092000075494289c2f833e336e6dd.jpeg[/img]

The [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/outlands-report-1-threats-and-opportunities][b]Avalonian Invasion[/b][/url] is in full swing, guilds are battling it out in a unique standalone season... and [b]Percival Patch 11[/b] is here! Today's patch brings several important updates to combat in Albion, in particular:
[list]	[*]The [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119764-Disarray-Zerg-Debuff/?postID=964642#post964642][b]zerg debuff[/b][/url] values have been updated to more effectively reward smaller armies[/*]	[*]Zerg debuffs no longer apply [b]during GvGs[/b], regardless of how many allied players are in the territory[/*]	[*][b]Healing Sickness[/b] duration has been increased [/*]	[*][b]Siege Ballista[/b] damage has been increased[/*]	[*]Numerous other melee, ranged, and magic skills have been updated [/*][/list]
Michael Schwahn, Combat Designer for Albion Online, describes the intent behind these changes: "We wanted to shake up the healer meta a bit, and to push the siege ballista as a viable counter to other battle mounts. We also felt it was time to reduce the utility of Parry Strike, in order to open up more of a variety with bruiser builds." These changes will play out over the remainder of the standalone season, which [b][url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119885-Standalone-Event-Season-Schedule/]runs until January 20[/url][/b].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/25013791e08866c048f55e7fc25bd17ac2e12be3.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Additional Changes[/h1]
In a first for the world of Albion, [b]Uncle Frost[/b] now appears as a boss in certain rare dungeons! Group and solo [b]Keeper Randomized Dungeons[/b] in all zones have a chance to end in a special [b]Yuletide Dungeon[/b], where you'll face off against this mysterious foe. Beat him to unlock Christmas-themed loot, including a chance at holiday-themed [b]mount skins[/b].

Also with today's patch, a new [b]Adventurer Avatar[/b] is available at the Vanity Merchant. This new item joins the [b]Adventurer Avatar Ring[/b] in a growing list of vanity items – trade in unclaimed Adventurer's Challenge Avatar Rings for Adventurer Tokens to unlock these new items!

For a complete list of changes, please see the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20PATCH%2011][b]official changelog[/b][/url].

Numerous other melee, ranged, and magic skills have been updated

notes.title: The Avalonian Invasion Has Begun!
notes.content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fOYRjRICFEQ
A fearsome new presence has appeared in the Outlands: the [b]Avalonians[/b]. This ancient order from Albion's past has returned to reclaim their land, using a mysterious energy drawn from deep in the earth. While their ultimate plan is unknown, it will have world-altering consequences for Albion.

The Avalonian forces stalking the Outlands are currently limited... but as the season proceeds, they are sure to increase not only in number, but also in variety. Prepare yourself for a battle that will alter the very foundations of the world of Albion.
[h1]Important Dates[/h1][table]			[tr]			[td][b]November 13[/b][/td]			[td][b]Avalonian Mobs appear in the Outlands[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]November 16[/b][/td]			[td][b]Standalone Guild Season Start - Territories become claimable, Avalonian Mage World Bosses appear[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]December 7[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #1[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]December 21[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #2[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 4[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #3, Scores Doubled[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 11[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #4, GvGs End[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 13[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #5[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 15[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #6[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 16[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #7[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 17[/b][/td]			[td][b]Territory Reset Day #8[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 19[/b][/td]			[td][b]End-of-Season Event[/b][/td]		[/tr]		[tr]			[td][b]January 20[/b][/td]			[td][b]Season Ends[/b][/td]		[/tr]	[/table][h1][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/80446ce5b780652ce6ebe0181b767f5c2ee05ea7.jpeg[/img][/h1][h1]New Food, Better Tools, and a Unique Mount[/h1]
The mysterious energy harvested by the Avalonians gives them near-divine powers. Defeat Avalonian mobs and world bosses to claim this energy for yourself, and then bring it to the [b]Energy Manipulator[/b] in any of the Royal Cities to enhance various foods and tools or create an all-new mount. Avalonian foods combine [b]meat-based stews and sandwiches[/b] with Avalonian Energy to add one additional stat that varies depending on the food. Avalonian tools give improved gathering yields for all resources, including fish. And finally, combine a Saddled Swamp Dragon with enough Avalonian Energy to produce the fearsome [b]Avalonian Basilisk[/b], a fast, strong mount with a powerful [b]electric discharge spell[/b] that reduces enemies' attack and move speed.

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/42ac60c2541eaddfd5c300eec465efc2a46adbd1.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Take Down Avalonian Mages for Season Points[/h1]
This season, your guild will have a new way to earn season points: by taking down [b]Avalonian Mage World Bosses[/b]. These mysterious members of the Avalonian order have harnessed energy into powerful beam attacks that deal massive damage. These bosses appear on the world map, and can be killed for Season Points starting with the beginning of the season on Saturday, November 16. (Recommended for groups of 10.)

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/8a8fa64bb7ad30eb51bb02d973764b5ff6f7b065.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Earn One-of-a-Kind Seasonal Rewards[/h1]
A unique season deserves unique rewards. The higher your guild ranks, the better the rewards - check out what you can earn:
[list]	[*][b]Crystal Rank:[/b] Avalonian Avatar + all following rewards[/*]	[*][b]Gold Rank:[/b] Avalonian Avatar Ring + all following rewards[/*]	[*][b]Silver Rank:[/b] Small Caerleon Realmgate Furniture Object + all following rewards[/*]	[*][b]Bronze Rank:[/b] Outlands Map Carpet + all following rewards[/*]	[*][b]Iron Rank:[/b] Pile of Tomes[/*][/list]
Additionally, guilds that finish in [b]first, second or third place overall[/b] will be immortalized in a one-off memorial statue in Caerleon. This statue will not be part of Conquerors' Hall, and will instead appear in a unique location of significance. And as always, the first-place season winner will have a crystal ornament added to their guild logo.

notes.title: Zerg Debuff & Alliance Point Sharing
notes.content:
[url=//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/54b6a46e02401d88745838230d89dd87a213653e.jpeg][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/1069441cb9ef20cf9fbd32b34c0dfada5b2ea513.jpeg[/img][/url]
[h1]Disarray - Zerg Debuff[/h1]
The new Outlands map coming with the Queen update will bring [b]open-world territory fights[/b] to Guild Seasons. A major part of this new territory control system is [b]zerg[/b] [b]debuffs[/b], which will cause allied groups larger than a designated size to be less powerful, with the debuff increasing the larger the group gets. We've been hard at work on this system, and we already plan on introducing it[b] [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/something-stirring-outlands]with the new season on November 13[/url][/b].

For the most up-to-date information on zerg debuffs from our development team, see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119764][b]the post on our forums[/b][/url].

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/default/media/3dab2fcb4449523ba06f5e29d5d13972656fd394.jpeg[/img]
[h1]Alliance Point Sharing[/h1]
Additionally, we are planning to deploy another new feature with this standalone season: [b]alliance point sharing[/b]. Under this system, season points scored by a guild will be split between the guild and their alliance, with the alliance's share distributed [b]between all guilds in the alliance[/b]. For more details and the most up-to-date information about alliance point sharing, please see [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119765][b]this forum post[/b][/url].

We look forward to seeing how this affects the game in the upcoming standalone Season and we look forward to your feedback!

notes.title: The Grim Challenge Returns
notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/ec1560b9441b828936377c59c79adf7e38cc0ecf.jpeg[/img]

Allhallows is already in full swing, and November has arrived - it's time for the next Adventurer's Challenge! For all of November, the [b]Grim Challenge[/b] lets you earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your own [b]Pest Lizard[/b]. We've also introduced [b]Adventurer's Tokens[/b], which let you trade in unclaimed Avatar Ring unlock items for a selection of new rings. Read on for all the details!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/45b3cb66836e268789ff59a6fe7f6c5113029808.gif[/img]

[h1][b]Pestilential Prizes For Intrepid Adventurers[/b][/h1]
[table][tr][td][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/37098394fc221f53b22942d5c2018a17b86b1dca.png[/img][/td][td][b]PEST LIZARD:[/b] This month, you'll have another chance to claim the [b]Pest Lizard[/b], a fast-moving mount with two different poison-based attacks that confuse and disorient enemies. (Note: while not officially Battle Mounts, Pest Lizards are not usable in GvGs.)[/td][/tr][tr][td][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/fd248429c8bb16fadb892cc6075439f63762bd27.png[/img][/td][td][b]AVATAR RING:[/b] The Grim Challenge Avatar Ring gives your avatar a dark, creepy aura. This non-tradable item permanently unlocks this exclusive avatar border for one character - and starting this month, unclaimed Avatar Ring unlocks can be traded in for [b]Adventurer's Tokens[/b] (details below).[/td][/tr][tr][td][img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/403acbde708b8ce245e5ff5afda91a0ee51037c4.png[/img][/td][td][b]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] Unlock Grim Challenge chests to get a mix of pestilential prizes. In addition to the regular goodies like Silver bags, Fame Tomes, and resources, you'll have a chance to get the [b]Plague Doctor [/b]costume set and the [b]Tomb of the Unknown[/b] and [b]Memorial of the Fallen[/b] furniture items.[/td][/tr][/table]

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/b26dc2833fb43fcddcd069440770aa004ad0e838.png[/img]

[h1][b]New This Month: Adventurer's Tokens[/b][/h1]
Since adventurers who took part in last year's Grim Challenge may have already unlocked this month's Avatar Ring, we've given all players the option to trade in Avatar Rings [b]that have not yet been unlocked[/b] for [b]Adventurer's Tokens[/b] at the Vanity Merchant. Here's how it works:

Log in, head out into the open world, and unlock these fabulous prizes - and don't forget about the week-long [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/get-ready-fall-fame-boost][b]Fame Boost[/b][/url] running November 4-11!

notes.content:
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/8b73f60129616fbfeec6ad790cade4364e367bfc.jpeg[/img]

Feel the chill in the air, and the cold touch of grasping, undead hands:  [b]Allhallows[/b] is here! This three-week event brings a new themed dungeon to explore, a deadly high-octane mount race, and other surprises. Read on to see what's coming...
[h1]New Dungeon: Hallowed Ground[/h1]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/c3ea8e3ab76c85d1f8f6159b207f53f887700c70.png[/img]

This limited-time, [b]Halloween-themed group dungeon[/b] features eerie pumpkin-lined corridors and a cornucopia of creepy-crawly critters, plus the mysterious new foe known only as [b]Bob[/b]. Some say his family was killed by gankers when he was just a baby, asleep on a bag of pumpkin seeds. He grew up in a kennel, raised by a cruel pumpkin farmer who twisted his body and mind. Now he returns to seek vengeance on Albion's unsuspecting human souls...

[b]Hallowed Ground[/b] offers valuable loot, including a very rare chance for mount skins like the [b]Jack o' Donkey [/b]and [b]Horse Macabre[/b] along with other items. The dungeon has a small chance of spawning in [b]all T4-T8 zones[/b], with rewards scaling depending on the tier – so form a party, put on your spookiest dungeon-crawling garb, and get ready for a fight!
[h1]Will You Survive the Death Race?[/h1]
[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/ba460781cf6ea2d3fcab37b1dbafd018cc2d3ced.png[/img]

Next week, you'll have the chance to compete against your fellow players in a heart-pounding race with Halloween-themed rewards! It all goes down on a deadly course lined with flame traps, where one misstep can spell defeat... but for those who cross the finish line first, glory awaits.

Here's how it will work:
[list]	[*]There will be a total of [b]3 race events[/b][/*]	[*]The first two will be on [b]October 29 [/b]at[b] 18:00 and 22:00 UTC[/b][/*]	[*]The winning 15 players from each race will qualify for the [b]Finals[/b][/*]	[*]The Finals will take place on [b]October 30 [/b]at[b] 20:00 UTC[/b][/*]	[*]The first two races are [b]Blue Zone rules[/b]; the Finals are [b]Black Zone rules[/b][/*]	[*]Participants [b]must be in Caerleon[/b] at these times to join the races, and [b]must bring their own Mule mount[/b][/*]	[*]Further details on exactly how to participate in the race will follow[/*][/list]
Rewards for qualifiers:
[list]	[*]Each of the 30 finalists gets a [b]Jack O' Donkey Skin[/b][/*][/list]
Rewards for winners:
[list]	[*]1st Place: [b]Horse Macabre Skin + 21,000 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]2nd Place: [b]Horse Macabre Skin + 10,000 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]3rd Place: [b]Horse Macabre Skin + 3,750 Gold[/b][/*]	[*]4th - 10th Place: [b]Horse Macabre Skin[/b][/*][/list]
Grab a trusty mule and get ready to race for prizes and glory!

[img]//assets.albiononline.com/uploads/media/my-context/media/6e957cb16081f31814b41d06d208b41e2655b0c6.png[/img]

To round out the festivities, [b]Halloween decorations[/b] have returned to Albion's cities, a week-long [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/get-ready-fall-fame-boost][b]Fame Boost[/b][/url] runs from November 4-11, and a creepy presence has appeared on the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/119825][b]forums[/b][/url]. [b]Allhallows[/b] will haunt Albion from now through maintenance on [b]November 13[/b], so take advantage of these limited-time opportunities while you can!

notes.title: Percival Patch 7 is Here
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6kp5Ici.png[/img]

Today we launched [b]Percival Patch 7[/b], which brings changes to Albion's Silver sinks, quality-of-life improvements to building and transmuting, updated resource spawn rates, and more. So what's new?
[h1]More Silver Sinks[/h1]
With today's patch, we've increased the [b]Silver costs assessed by the system[/b] for various activities. These system-based costs serve as Silver sinks, which keep the overall quantity of Silver in the world of Albion consistent, and prevent runaway inflation of the Silver-to-Gold ratio. With the introduction of [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b] in the Oberon update, the amount of Silver in the game increased tremendously, leading to inflated Gold costs for those looking to trade in their Silver. These updated costs mean the amount of Silver leaving the economy is once again in line with the amount entering it.

This patch brings the following cost changes:
[list]	[*]Increased repair costs of all items by 100%, but halved knockdown damage (from 10% to 5%), meaning repair cost of knockdowns remains the same[/*]	[*]Increased Market Order Fee from 1% to 1.5%[/*]	[*]Increased Market Tax from 4% to 6% (from 2% to 3% with Premium)[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of buying additional bank tabs by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of buying and upgrading islands by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of converting Fame to Fame Credits by 50%[/*]	[*]Increased the cost of using the fast travel feature by 50%[/*]	[*]Reduced the rate at which Silver offers are generated by the Black Market by 10%[/*][/list][h1]Transmutation Changes[/h1]
In addition to the changes listed above, we've rebalanced the cost structure for [b]transmutation.[/b] Transmutation was always intended as a natural ingame sink, but was previously so expensive that it was almost never used. This patch [b]lowers[/b] overall costs for transmutation, while also making the transmutation process [b]four times faster[/b], in order to make it more appealing. With decreased Silver (and time!) costs for transmutation, this previously overlooked activity should become a more viable option.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/P1E0msv.png[/img]
[h1]Builders Rejoice![/h1]
Along with the increased speed of transmutation, constructing, upgrading, and repairing buildings is now [b]twice as fast[/b]. Construction and maintenance already require a great deal of resources, so we've decided to make the actual processes of building creation and upkeep less time-consuming for players who have already made the necessary resource commitment.
[h1]Keeping Albion Balanced[/h1]
Last but not least, we've also made some changes to keep the game's [b]gathering and combat[/b] balanced. Resources and "resource critters" in tier 2, 3, and 4 blue zones now take[b] twice as long[/b] to respawn, to avoid flooding the market with low-tier resources. On the combat side, we've made various changes, including [b]reducing the impact of Damnation bomb squads[/b] in ZvZs and removing the option to stack Quarrier Boots via Self-Ignition, which gave gankers an undue advantage.

You can read the detailed list of changes in the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20PATCH%207][b]official patchnotes[/b][/url].

notes.title: Dev Talk: The New Outlands
notes.content:
[b]Queen[/b], the next major content update for Albion Online, will bring wide-ranging changes to the world of Albion. Foremost among these is [b]a complete redesign of the Outlands continent[/b]. Along with new game systems like Hideouts and Open-World Territory Conquests, this redesigned continent will bring new sandbox possibilities to high-level play in Albion.

In our most recent Dev Talk, Game Director Robin Henkys and Level Designer Dominik Müller discuss the what, the how, and the why of the reworked Outlands:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ONquGyh6jc
No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Read on for all the details:
[h1]Updating the Outlands[/h1]
In our last Dev Talk, we discussed the massive improvements coming with the Queen update. Today we’re going to go more in-depth with the key change: the [b]new Outlands map[/b].

With Albion’s next major update, we're going to change the shape of Albion’s gameworld for good: we’re bringing in an all new Outland map which will revolutionize high-level gameplay and deliver the foundation for Guild Hideouts, as well as the new Open-World Territory Conquests.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/f2RreBs.jpg[/img]

Before we get into how awesome the new map is, we’ll first cover what happens when the old Outlands go away. Many of you are probably wondering what will happen to your stuff and how this process will go down. We don’t know the exact timing of this change yet, but we will announce it at least a month in advance, ideally a month and a half. We’d love to do it earlier, but with the complexity of this change we just can’t be sure of the timing until we’re pretty much ready to go.
[list]	[*]When the time of the world change is announced, you’ll have to start thinking about evacuating your belongings from the Outlands.[/*]	[*]We’re planning to automatically evacuate any items you have in [b]personal banks[/b] and [b]guild vaults in territories or siege camps[/b] - players will have access to these items in the Royal cities.[/*]	[*]However, any [b]buildings[/b] and [b]contents of furniture chests[/b] will be lost if you do not evacuate them by the time of the change.[/*]	[*]We’re also trying to find a way to evacuate [b]laborers [/b]and [b]Marketplace contents[/b], but we’re not sure if and how these will work yet - the exact rules will be announced with the final announcement of the world change timing.[/*][/list]
Apart from items, we’re of course evacuating [b]players [/b]as well: any players remaining in the Outlands at the time of the change will find themselves in a city on the Royal Continent and will be able to use the Outland portals to travel to the new Outlands.

Now we’ve got that out of the way, let's talk about the big change itself: the new Outland map.

Our designer Dominik Müller has been busy the last couple of months planning the details of this change. I asked him to show you what he's been working on, what you can expect from Albion’s new Outlands, and why this is such a big deal.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/gOfOtv5.jpg[/img]
[h1]Dominik Müller Talks World-Building[/h1]
When we created the old Outlands, we had a very [b]symmetrical and clean[/b], and therefore very [b]balanced [/b]map in mind. It was defined by repetition: "next to this T5 area there must be a T6 area, and therefore a castle.”

The new Outlands will be far more complex, as we are breaking many of our current conventions. We want to change the way players see the world, and move away from repeating patterns. The world has become a lot more varied: now you can find T8 areas next to T5 areas, or a mountain area surrounded by steppe, or your castle far away from the center of the Outlands.

Yet you can still learn and understand the map, as there remain clearly visible and tangible rules: for example, the closer I am to the center of the map, Avalon, the higher the density of high-tier areas and the greater the possibility for high-value activities. But of course, the higher the value of an area is, the harder it will be to defend.
[h1]Strength and Vulnerability[/h1]
What exactly does this do for us? Well, first, it literally reshuffles the board, as big contestants become more vulnerable with greater power creating a constant flux, while there will be smaller skirmishes around more achievable areas thus creating a map interesting for everyone.

As you can imagine, there are many things to consider:
[list]	[*]How deep in the Outlands do I want to live?[/*]	[*]Do I have access to all the resources I need?[/*]	[*]Do I have access to a good farming spot?[/*]	[*]Do I have sufficient access to farms to produce food?[/*]	[*]Can I make an impact on the season from here?[/*]	[*]How well-protected am I here?[/*]	[*]Who are my neighbors? Will there be conflicts - or the chance for an alliance?[/*][/list][h1]New Cities and Portal Systems[/h1]
For those without a guild or a Hideout, there will also be [b]three new Outlands "cities"[/b]. These are essentially small towns (similar to the "starter" towns), consisting of a Marketplace and a Bank. They are located in the middle zones, between the portals at the edges of the continent and the high-tier areas at the center, and offer safe spots to trade and regear.

With Caerleon's portal breaking down, the Royal cities will also rise in importance, as their portals are now the only way to reach the new Outlands. They will use a [b]triple portal system[/b], which should allow for safer entry into the black zones, while also allowing the portal areas to remain a feasible hunting ground.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/OxG2pPp.png[/img]
[h1]New Time Zones[/h1]
We also took this chance to greatly increase the number of different prime times for zones. There are now [b]seven prime times[/b] in total, and I'm happy to announce that these will include viable times for our Asian and Australian players. [b]Prime times will occur at 0:00, 3:00, 5:00, 12:00, 15:00, 18:00, and 21:00 UTC. [/b]The number of areas in a given prime time directly relates to our player numbers during these times, ensuring that content will be distributed as fairly as possible between players.

This redesigned continent will have a ton of opportunities for conflict and new stories, and will allow players of different levels and with different interests to lead all sorts of lives all over the Outlands. I can't wait for this map to be filled with life, and see what you guys will do with it. 
[h1]Much more to come - give us your feedback![/h1]
We're very excited about the new Outlands map, and are very much looking forward to seeing the new strategies and gameplay styles which will arise from it. We are also very interested in hearing your [b]feedback [/b]on the new Outlands, so please share your thoughts with us via our [url=http://forum.albiononline.com][b]forums[/b][/url].

We’ll keep you updated on the progress of building the new Outlands in upcoming Dev Talks, but that's all for today. Stay tuned for more videos on the next major update!

notes.title: The Harvest Challenge Returns!
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/se4bazv.jpg[/img]
[h1][b]Take the Harvest Challenge[/b][/h1]
Fall has come to the world of Albion - and the [b]Harvest Challenge[/b] is back! For the entire month of October, earn Challenge Points to collect limited-time rewards. This time around, on top of your very own [b]Spectral Bat[/b] mount, you can get an [b]all-new avatar border[/b] and Halloween-themed [b]costume items[/b]:

[b][img]https://i.imgur.com/JNwYorj.png[/img]THE BAT IS BACK:[/b] This month's Challenge offers all players another chance to claim the amazing [b]Spectral Bat[/b]. In addition to its spooky spectral looks, this winged menace comes with a powerful [b]Blink[/b] spell that allows you to jump to a target location in the blink of an eye. (Note: like all mounts, the Spectral Bat cannot fly over obstacles or gaps.)

[b][img]https://i.imgur.com/7oqxJNW.png[/img]NEW AVATAR BORDER:[/b] This month you can also unlock the [b]all-new 2019 Harvest Challenge avatar border[/b] featuring a pair of eerie, grinning skeletons. This non-tradable permanently unlocks this spooky avatar border for one character, allowing you to show it off all year round!

[b][img]https://i.imgur.com/o2OfuSX.png[/img]SEASONAL SPECIALS:[/b] All month long, reach weekly goals to unlock [b]Harvest Challenge Chests[/b]. In addition to valuable rewards like Adventurer's Tomes, Silver, resources, and other loot, you'll also have a chance to unlock spooky vanity items like [b]Pumpkin Heads [/b]and[b] Skeleton Costumes.[/b]

As always, you can earn Challenge Points by [b]gathering, fishing, farming, and killing monsters[/b]. Points count simultaneously toward a daily bonus, a weekly unlockable chest, and the monthly mount and avatar ring reward. So log in, head out into the open world, gather points, and claim these rewards while they last!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FMHROdj.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Talk: Queen Update Introduction
notes.content:
In our most recent Dev Talk, Robin Henkys, Game Director of Albion Online, offers a first look at some of the huge changes coming to the Outlands with the next major content update, [b]Queen[/b]. Much of the Outlands rework is still in the early stages of development, but we want to introduce various parts of it now to give a "big-picture" view of this long-anticipated change. While the next update will have numerous additional features, the Outlands rework is central to our vision of bringing a true hardcore sandbox experience to our players.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5bmUuyQo_o

No time to watch the video, or prefer a written summary? Read on for all the details of his talk.
[h1]Filling in the Roadmap[/h1]
In our last Dev Talk, we set out how we're still proceeding with the roadmap we laid out earlier this year. This is still true, and in addition we have more exciting new content planned which we’ll talk about in the future.

Today, though, we want to get more specifically into our plans for the [b]Outlands [/b]and what we’re working on for the next content update, code-named [b]Queen[/b]. The Outlands rework is a major milestone of the Roadmap, and it consists of [b]five major improvements[/b] we’re planning to introduce in the next update:
[list]	[*]An [b]entirely new Outlands map[/b][/*]	[*]The ability to freely build [b]Guild Hideouts[/b] in the Outlands to live deep in the wilds of Albion[/*]	[*]A [b]new method for territory control[/b] which allows all guild members to help capture a territory instead of being limited to five players[/*]	[*][b]Improved 5v5 Crystal Realm battles[/b] with the ability to participate even if you don’t own a territory, but with additional bonuses for those who do[/*]	[*][b]Zerg debuffs[/b] and the [b]smart cluster queue[/b][/*][/list]
All these changes listed together makes for some big changes coming to Albion Online, so let's take a closer look at each of them and explain what they are, what function they serve in the game, why we’re excited about them.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/GVy3ITY.png[/img]
[h1]1. The New Outlands Map[/h1]
When we first designed our current [b]Outlands map[/b], our main concern was adding as much distance between the low and high Outlands as possible. This created a "stretched" map, with the highest-value areas at one end and the weakest areas at the other.

In reality, though, we saw guilds settling wherever there was available space. The overarching problem was that guilds had no reasonable means of progression to the top area, [b]Mercia[/b].

Here's how the new Outlands map will be different:
[list]	[*]In the new Outlands, [b]the most valuable areas in the game will be at the center of the map[/b], leaving it open to attack and raids from all sides[/*]	[*]Not only the center of the map will be highly attractive: high value areas will also be [b]mixed into the entire world[/b] to create local hotspots of fighting and conflict[/*]	[*]The number of territories in each zone will be reduced from two to one (see section 3 below for more info)[/*][/list]
Also, with the launch of this new world,[b] the Caerleon portal will collapse[/b] and the Outlands will no longer be accessible from Caerleon. As with the last portal change, players will be given another opportunity to move their islands should they want to. We plan on revisiting the role of Caerleon in a future update.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Gv9DKwd.jpg[/img]
[h1]2. Hideouts[/h1]
You may have heard us talking about Hideouts before. We’re very excited about them, and today we'll give you an introductory overview to this major new feature.

[b]What are Hideouts, and how are they placed?[/b]
[list]	[*]Hideouts are [b]buildable bases[/b] guilds can place [b]anywhere in the Outlands[/b][/*]	[*]They start out as a [b]Hideout Building Kit[/b], a craftable item that is quite heavy and needs to be transported to the location you want to place the Hideout[/*]	[*]Once placed, the Hideout construction site [b]has to be defended[/b] for a short time before becoming invulnerable for about a day[/*]	[*]The next day, just before construction finishes, the Hideout [b]becomes vulnerable for another short period[/b] before it finally becomes established[/*]	[*]These attack phases prevent guilds from aggressively “sneaking” Hideouts into their enemies’ backyards[/*][/list]
[b]Once a Hideout is established, how does it work?[/b]
[list]	[*]Once the Hideout is established, it can be entered by [b]anyone the owning guild grants permission to[/b][/*]	[*]Inside, you can [b]build crafting stations, store your equipment, set a respawn point and have a Marketplace[/b][/*]	[*]Hideouts can be [b]upgraded[/b][/*][/list]
Basically the Hideouts allow any guild to have a fully functional base anywhere in the Outlands. You could even grant visiting rights to all players and build [b]your own Outlands city[/b] with public crafting stations, Marketplaces, and so on. We're very excited about the tremendous sandbox potential of this system, and we look forward to seeing what players do with it.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/orZftm5.jpg[/img]
[h1]3. Open-World Territory Battles[/h1]
The next change is likely the most controversial, but it is one that we have been thinking about for a very long time. Along with the introduction of Hideouts, we are removing the 5v5 GvG battle system from territory control, and replacing it with a battle system that allows all members of a guild to contribute to help claim territories.
[list]	[*]Under the new system, attacking a territory requires you to [b]declare a challenge in the open world[/b]. At any point during the day, you can ride to your enemies’ territory, kill their guards and challenge control of the territory.[/*]	[*]This will [b]schedule a battle[/b] during the prime time on the following day. During the next day’s battle, the defenders can try to remove the attacker’s claim by channeling the territory tower.[/*]	[*]The attackers, on the other hand, can claim the territory by channeling the tower themselves.[/*]	[*]Note that it is entirely possible for [b]multiple groups to challenge control of the same territory at the same time[/b], enabling three-plus way battles for territory control.[/*]	[*]Finally, since armies can attack multiple territories at the same time, bringing all your forces to bear on the same territory may not be the smartest move.[/*][/list]
This change finally enables all players of a guild to support their guild’s bid for territory control. It also removes territory control from those players simply seeking the thrill of 5v5 battles, who may not actually care about territories and simply want thrill of the battle itself.

For these players, and everyone who loves high-risk 5v5 action in Albion, we have a special treat: an [b]expanded Crystal Realm Battle system[/b] with many opportunities for high-end PvP action.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/q49Ht3Z.png[/img]
[h1]4. Expanded Crystal Realm Battles[/h1]
Under the new, expanded Crystal Realm Battle system, players can participate in [b]high-stakes 5v5 fights, regardless of whether their guild holds a territory[/b].

Instead, players earn their participation by acquiring a [b]Crystal Realm Token[/b]. These tokens exist in multiple levels, and at different times during the day, the week, and the month, battles of different levels matching these tokens will take place. Players who wish to participate in these battles will need to collect a group of five players, each of whom has a token of the same level.

If they win, they earn a [b]significant reward[/b] and the token they were using is [b]upgraded to the next level[/b]. If they lose, their token is [b]destroyed[/b].

The exciting thing about this system is that it allows [b]players without strong guilds[/b] to still participate in exciting, high-risk 5v5 fights, while still ensuring [b]guilds with strong 5v5 players[/b] will continue to reap benefits.

Players can sign up for a Crystal Realm Battle in two different ways:
[list]	[*]They can go to the [b]Energy Manipulator NPC[/b] in any city or upgraded Hideout, or[/*]	[*]They can go enter the Crystal Realm via the tower of an[b] owned territory[/b].[/*][/list]
Whichever way they choose, they are thrown into a Crystal Realm Battle and face off against another team. However, if they sign up via a territory tower and win, they will [b]upgrade the power of the territory crystal[/b], which has the following effects:
[list]	[*]It adds a [b]general gathering buff [/b]for all guild members gathering within the affected territory[/*]	[*]The [b]percentage of enchanted resources[/b] around the territory is increased[/*]	[*]It [b]buffs the territory guards[/b], making it harder for enemies to attack the territory in the open world[/*][/list]
This territory upgrade effect means that you can still benefit significantly from having a strong 5v5 team in your guild.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/niFKHC6.png[/img]
[h1]5. Zerg Debuffs and the Smart Cluster Queue[/h1]
With so many features coming that involve open-world battles, you’re probably wondering how we’re going to deal with all the players these massive battles will involve.

[b]1. Smart Cluster Queue System[/b]

The Smart Cluster Queue system prevents large armies from blocking entire zones by overcrowding them. Essentially, this system analyzes how many players from one side are attempting to enter a zone, and calculates based on the players' gear and status how much they're contributing to the fight. It then checks how many players the other side has and how many want to enter the same area, and auto-balances the zone based on the number of players on each side. Excess players are moved to nearby zones, where they can continue the fight in secondary battles.

[b]2. Zerg Debuff[/b]

This system adds an "inefficiency" tradeoff to bringing too many people to a fight. Whenever more than 25 allied players are in the same zone, these players will suffer from an “inefficiency” debuff that decreases their combat effectiveness slightly. The more players in your army, the more this debuff increases. This means you will have to choose an optimal army size based on your guilds’ size and abilities, and should not simply collect the largest army in one place.

***

We’ll continue providing more details on each of these features as development continues, hopefully with a dedicated video for each feature. With this talk, you should at least have a good overview of what changes are coming with the Queen update, and how they will work together to completely redefine the experience of living in the Outlands and fighting for territories.

For now, we hope you're excited for these new opportunities for epic large-scale and 5v5 fights, and the ability for guilds of all sizes to live in the Outlands. That's all for today - thanks for watching, and stay tuned for more Dev Talks over the coming weeks!

notes.title: The Percival Midseason Patch is Here
notes.content:
Today we launched Percival Patch 5, also known as the Percival Midseason Patch. Here's a rundown of some of the changes and improvements it brings:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Ykv6B1K.png[/img]
[h1]Meta Changes and Updated Spells[/h1]
The patch brings changes across a wide range of weapon and armor spells, with some specific goals in mind. "One of our primary goals with this patch was to reduce the impact of dive comps," says Michael Schwahn, Combat Designer for Albion Online. "And while we buffed a few underused items, this patch brings quite a few nerfs. The recent trend toward buffing items was shifting the gameplay away from our intended direction, so these changes are intended to ground the gameplay a bit."

The patch also brings several new and updated spells. The new Fire Staff spell,[b] Fire Artillery[/b], launches a cannon-like stationary attack on a target that inflicts ongoing burn damage and stacked debuffs. The Nature Staff spell Poison Thorns has been reworked: now simply called [b]Thorns[/b], it has moved from the W to the Q slot and gives 5 stacks that deal additional magic damage to targets.

Finally, [b]Healing Sickness[/b] is a new debuff intended to prevent solo healers from sustaining their own HP indefinitely. As healing another target immediately cancels the debuff, this change should only affect solo and small-scale PvP.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/sigAEfk.png[/img]
[h1]New Guild Logs[/h1]

notes.title: Dev Spotlight: Dominik Müller
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/1bUCTJt.jpg[/img]

[b]What was your background in games prior to working at SBI? [/b]

Like most devs, I spent a lot of my youth playing games, mainly anything with a ranking. My career in games didn’t start until I was accepted at the London College of Communication to study Game Design. I fell in love with the depth of design behind a good game and made it my profession. Since 2012 I have been developing smaller games, and in 2015 I worked on my first proper game, “Iron Fish” by BeefJack, where I was Level and Narrative Designer. The project was too ambitious for the small team, and the whole thing kind of sank, like, well, an iron fish. So I looked for the next opportunity and went back to Germany, my home country, to start working for SBI.

[b]You've worked at Sandbox since 2016. How has your work on the game evolved over the years?[/b]

It has been almost three years now since I joined the team. I basically went from the guy who would move bushes and grass out of the way to the guy who would design why there is grass in the first place and how the grass should look and what type of grass it is.

I really enjoyed bringing small stories into the world. All over Albion you can find these small elements, such as a working sundial in an Essence template and a pumpkin scarecrow chained to a bed in the asylum in Camlann. At the same time, I played a ton of Albion, mainly doing Hellgates and Fame farms, learning to see the game from a player perspective.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/xwqnkdc.jpg[/img]

As my understanding of Albion grew, so did my ambition, and with a small team of devs I worked on the first event, The Headless Descent. Given my love for quests I also took over the world quest line for the subsequent winter event, and eventually the major overhaul of the tutorial, culminating in my latest and biggest contribution: the complete rework of the starter experience.

[b]Can you give an overview of the Level Design process?[/b]

We work very closely with all other departments. An idea comes to us from Game Design, which is then given an initial structure by Level Design with all the assets that we have, then polished by Art with new assets. I really feel that for such a small team we have an amazingly detailed and vast world. Due to our small size we are greatly limited in what we can do, and have to keep efficiency in mind at all times. But as I like to say, creativity grows with constraints.

And in my humble opinion, Albion is in all facets a great example of that. Many things we do in Level Design are limited by size, as we are using a so-called template system, meaning we are creating a lot of different puzzle pieces that have to fit together. Which makes it vastly complex to create small areas that look unique enough yet also normal enough to make up a “good”-looking landscape.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FsJZ2OZ.png[/img]

We're aware that many parts of the world still seem “copy-pasted” as many of the puzzle pieces are used multiple times, due to the creation of an enormous world in a limited amount of time. We're not too happy with that, but we are dealing with this issue and are improving the world design with every iteration, focusing more and more on the needs of the playerbase and their feedback.

Examples of updated level design can be seen all over the world, most noticeably in the T3 starting clusters which have served as a test run for further changes.

[b]In addition to Level Design, you've also worked in Game Design, and have recently begun working on strengthening Albion's lore. How do these different game development processes relate and connect to each other?[/b]

They are so very similar and yet so very different, which is why I always like to use this simple metaphor: Level Design is the creation of the chess board while Game Design is the creation of the rules. Lore, well, lore ties everything together and gives meaning to the numbers and rules of the game. Without narrative elements one would not threaten to destroy a tower, kill a bishop, or overthrow a king, but merely be playing with wooden pieces.

Due to Albion's sandbox nature, only a bit of lore was needed to keep everything together, but I do believe that with more of a background story all design processes can be enhanced – again using the idea that limitations require innovation. The more lore in the game, the more limited our ideas will be, but they will also have more direction and weight. And thus I became more involved with the lore of Albion, going through very old documentations, our amazing paperback book and other sources to update the story and collect everything we know of our own world. We also added a lot of voice lines to mobs and NPCs such as:
[list]	[*]The Cook: "There is no 'peas' in Albion, only beans."[/*]	[*]The Alchemist: "Death in a bottle, life in a bottle... uhh, I should really label them."[/*]	[*]The Torturer Boss: "The pain... what pleasure."[/*][/list]
These voice lines add a few more specks of color to Albion's palette, and I can’t wait for players to find more and more lore hidden throughout the world.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/qEyO4CU.jpg[/img]

[b]What are the biggest challenges when working on a game like Albion Online?[/b]

To make everyone happy. It is a tough task to choose and pick in what direction to go, knowing exactly how certain players will react to it, knowing that it might still be the best choice. In the end we are creating this world for the players, and it is very hard to do something that might upset a certain player group. In the end it is not possible to create a world everybody always likes, but we will always give our best to make certain to deliver what we can. And yes, sometimes there are bugs and also misjudgements, but they have been done with the purest intentions. And the great thing about an ongoing development process is that it is never over, and things that might have been once broken can return to glory (see hellgates :D, which might be slightly broken again, but well). It is the circle of games, I guess.

[b]For the Oberon update last spring, you redesigned the game's tutorial from the ground up. Can you give some insights into that process?[/b]

This was the fourth time I worked on the tutorial. The first iteration was a streamlining of the starter island to create a natural flow of movement for the player, basically moving rocks and roads.

The second iteration brought a quest line, intended to help the player craft their first set of gear and gather resources.

The third iteration introduced the newly designed starter areas into the game and the first narrative-driven quest line started, which brought my personal favorite reward of the game: the Royal Steed, which is basically a back-alley mule with a royal sigil stitched on the side. This tutorial was far more complex than the previous ones, empowering the player to actually go out into the open world to gather and craft and switch clusters. It was a very inspiring design process going through all the biomes, thinking about how to introduce different resources and tiers to the player while they make their way outward from the starter town.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7s6LKyH.png[/img]

Then the internal announcement of free-to-play arrived, and we knew that a new and improved starter experience was needed. I was given a few months to work on the complete rehaul of the tutorial, with an updated goal: I needed to create instanced content to have enough resources and space for the rush of new players that would be joining the game.

But this also allowed me to bring a deeper narrative layer to the whole thing. Yes, the story of the hero stranded on a beach is not a new invention, but it lent itself sooo very well to Albion. It's the same premise used in our book, and for those hardcore fans out there, many of the characters one meets in the tutorial are out of the book, like Tia, our fearless captain.

So the new tutorial took shape, created out of elements such as lore, gameplay, and introductions to complex mechanics. Finally we explained the Destiny Board and the Marketplace in the tutorial which made the whole thing a bit less flowy, but as we've seen in our stats, a lot more players understand how the game works and stick with it longer.

Briefly, the new tutorial should show you what the game is all about without being too scary. It should display the love of detail, the combat and crafting system, the depth of progression, and how beautiful the world of Albion can be.

And I am deeply sorry that there is no full loot PvP in the tutorial, but come on, let people breathe before you take their T2 gear.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/3ekinKs.png[/img]

[b]What are some of your all-time favorite games? Which games have you learned the most from?[/b]

I am a very competitive player and did quite well in shooters such as Unreal Tournament, Counter-Strike, and MMOs like Guild Wars and WoW. These games taught me how much of a difference a well-placed column or box can make, and how important it is to give players the opportunity to use their knowledge of the environment to gain an advantage.

But my favorite games are the so-called Souls games. I love the brutal skill check and PvP these games have, but what I love most is the level design and lore. Everything in these games is there for a reason, nothing is there just because someone felt like it. If you dive deep enough into discussions with super enthusiasts, you can find a reason behind every stone and every metal type of every armor.

And this is what I eventually would love to achieve for Albion, to create a world where players feel that everything has a reason, and where skill matters most.

[b]Anything else to add?[/b]

Our work might not always be perfect, but Albion is our passion, and as I said above, we are doing this for the players. Sometimes we piss them off, sometimes we please them. But in the end, all we want to do is give you a place to have fun and kill some guys and maybe make you chuckle over the silliness of a T2 mule as a quest reward.

[i]Stay tuned for more Dev Spotlights in the coming weeks.[/i]

notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/f6EuyEI.gif[/img]
[h1][b]Take the Divine Challenge[/b][/h1]
For the entire month of August, take the [b]Divine Challenge[/b] to collect limited-time rewards. Earn points for open-world activities, unlock chests to get valuable loot, and claim your very own [b]mount skin, avatar border,[/b] and more.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/8WssfBv.png[/img]
[b]NEW MOUNT SKIN:[/b] This month's Challenge introduces a brand-new mount skin: the [b]Divine Stag[/b]. Once obtained, this mount skin will permanently unlock the pure white Divine Stag for all characters on your account. (Note that this skin requires an Adep's Giant Stag base mount to use.)

notes.title: Dev Talk: Season 7 and Beyond
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/si7m8BT.png[/img]

In our latest Dev Talk, Robin Henkys, Game Director of Albion Online, discusses the [b]changes [/b]coming with [b]GvG Season 7[/b] and gives a preview of the [b]roadmap beyond Percival[/b].

Please note that you can find a[b] detailed description[/b] of the [b]Season 7[/b] changes as well as a description of our roadmap in the forum or simply by [b]following the links in the description below[/b]!

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QdQFZjzaWdU
[b]Season 7 Changes: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/115466]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/115466[/url]
Roadmap for Percival and Beyond: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/104122]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/104122[/url][/b]

No time to watch the video? Read on for a written summary of his talk.

[h1]Season 7 Changes: The What and the Why[/h1]
In this season, we’re introducing a number of changes and features which aim to achieve [b]two primary goals[/b]:
[list]	[*]Allow [b]more players to contribute[/b] to their guild's Season Points in [b]a wider variety of ways[/b][/*]	[*]Limit the ability of a few guilds and players to [b]dominate the GvG and castle gameplay[/b], allowing [b]a wider range of guilds to compete[/b] in the season[/*][/list]
[b]First Goal: Allow More Players to Contribute[/b]

To achieve the first goal of having [b]more players contribute[/b], we’re introducing [b]Guild Challenges[/b]. Starting with Season 7, every player will be able to collect [b]Challenge Points[/b] for their guild. When the guild hits certain challenge point goals, it will be rewarded with [b]Season Points[/b].

Challenge Points are generated for killing mobs and other open-world activities, just like in Adventurer's Challenges. This means you can now contribute to your guild’s season success, even as a non-PvP focused player. The guild challenge also comes with a [b]ranking[/b], so guild leaders and other guild members can see how many points everyone is contributing to the guild’s goals.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PhyIdNm.jpg[/img]

[b]Second Goal: Leveling the Playing Field[/b]

To achieve our second goal of [b]limiting the ability of a few players to dominate the game[/b], we’re introducing a number of different changes.

First off, we’re introducing [b]Castle Outposts[/b] to the Outlands. These outposts are capturable in a similar way to castles, and will also be paying out a [b]daily Season Point reward[/b] as well as loot chests on weekends.

These will be [b]four times as common[/b] as castles, but only give [b]a quarter of the rewards[/b]. They will pay out their rewards at the same time as castles, opening more opportunities for smaller guilds to claim an outpost for themselves, while larger guilds will tend to fight over the big castles.

In addition, we’ve rebalanced [b]castle capture times[/b] to be much shorter. This makes it harder for an alliance to move their army from one castle to another in response to an attack, and forces them to split their forces if they want to contest multiple castles.

We’re also making some changes to [b]GvG and Crystal Realm fights[/b]:
[list]	[*]First, we’ve [b]consolidated GvG attack times[/b] so more territories now share the same attack times, making it harder for the same players to cover multiple GvGs in one day using alts.[/*]	[*]In addition, we’ve [b]deactivated mercenaries for GvG fights[/b], which limits the projection ability of elite GvG teams onto their own guild’s territories, and makes it less likely for them to show up unexpectedly. (Note that mercenaries are still allowed for Crystal Realm Battles.)[/*]	[*]Finally, we’ve [b]reworked the crystal realm system[/b] to include [b]more tower levels[/b] and to put [b]more emphasis on the win bonus[/b], decreasing the incentive to “stomp” your opponents. This makes it more rewarding to play at the higher end of the tower levels, and as a result should make it easier to compete at the lower end of the tower levels.[/*][/list]
That covers the main changes coming with Season 7, though I encourage you to read the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/115466][b]full forum post[/b][/url] if you’re interested in all the details.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/JZhlDku.jpg[/img]

[h1]What's Next for Albion?[/h1]
For the most part, we’re still following the [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/104122][b]roadmap[/b][/url] we published with the release of Oberon. Essentially, we’re aiming at a [b]completely reworked Outland experience[/b], where guilds actually live in the Outlands in secret bases we’re calling “[b]hideouts[/b]”.

The goal of this roadmap is to solve the issue of [b]large alliances being able to dominate the map[/b], and at the same time fulfill Albion’s dream of [b]allowing as many guilds as possible to build up their own base[/b] in the Outlands.

We’re already deep in planning the new Outlands map, and our plans for the hideouts are also proceeding nicely, but it has become clear that we’ll need to make quite a large number of changes and improvements in order to make living in the Outlands an exciting and fun experience. Therefore, we’re currently planning to split the rollout of this change over [b]the next two content updates[/b] as well as upcoming patches.

We’ll soon be ready to share more details of our plans and what changes you can expect to happen when. That's all for now - we wish you the best of luck for Season 7, and we'll see you ingame!

notes.title: Happy Second Anniversary, Albion Online!
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/A716k2k.jpg[/img]

Today marks two years since the official launch of Albion Online! We're celebrating with free items and a week-long Fame Boost (click [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/in-game-anniversary-celebrations][b]here[/b][/url] for all the juicy details), and have just released the [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/albion-online-soundtrack-release][b]Official Albion Online Soundtrack[/b][/url] across numerous digital platforms.

Anniversaries are also the perfect time to look back on the prior year, and take stock of everything that's happened. And what a year it was...

[h1]Faction Warfare Comes to Albion[/h1]
With the Merlyn update on July 31, 2018, Faction Warfare came to the Royal Continent. This new feature allowed players to join one of five Royal City factions and fight alongside other allied faction members to take outposts from the other cities' fearsome protectors, earning powerful rewards like [b]city faction capes[/b] and [b]faction mounts[/b] in the process:

https://youtu.be/VJX-QLYKXsc
[h1]GvG Season Rewards Introduced[/h1]
Beginning with GvG Season 4 in September 2018, members of guilds that ranked during the season received exclusive rewards. The higher the guild's final rank, the better the reward, culminating in an extremely powerful, crystal-armored version of an exclusive mount that changed with each season, starting with the epic [b]Battle Rhino[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/mXmp8DE.jpg[/img]

Season 4 also saw the introduction of [b]Conquerors' Hall[/b], a new building near the Caerleon Realmgate that serves as a museum of past GvG seasons. Each season's top three teams are immortalized in statue form, with the most recent winner stationed at the building's main entrance.

[h1]A New Challenge Awaits[/h1]
On October 1, 2018, the first [b]Adventurer's Challenge[/b] began. Each of these month-long "personal seasons" has its own unique theme, and offers players a chance to gain points for open-world activities and use them to unlock rewards. The highest-level rewards include epic mounts with unique skills, such as the [b]Spectral Bat[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/FMHROdj.gif[/img]

[h1]Entering a New Realm[/h1]
In November 2018, the [b]Nimue[/b] update arrived, bringing a new type of GvG: [b]Crystal Realm Battles[/b]. These fights took place in an entirely new setting, and opened up Albion's guild warfare system to newer and smaller teams. With the recent Percival update, Crystal Realm Battles can now be fought during the off-season as well, providing even more opportunities for those looking to break into the GvG scene.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kY4fSFD.jpg[/img]

[h1]Albion's Underworld: Randomized Dungeons[/h1]
The Oberon update launched on March 20, 2019. Among other features and upgrades, Oberon brought a huge new [b]Randomized Dungeon[/b] system to the world of Albion. Oberon brought group versions of these procedurally generated dungeons, while solo dungeons arrived with the Percival update in July.

Robin Henkys, Albion's Game Director, describes the current and future impact of this system on the game:

"In addition to the group dungeons that arrived with Oberon and the solo ones that came with Percival, this system holds the potential for other kinds of open-world content in the future. With this system already in the game, we will have the ability to add new types of content: hidden resource nodes, special event dungeons, guild hideouts, and more."

[img]https://i.imgur.com/NSCasZi.gif[/img]

[h1]The Free-to-Play Floodgates Open[/h1]
On April 10, 2019, Albion Online became completely free to download and play. This brought in tens of thousands of new players from all over the world, and opened up Albion to a much greater percentage of the gaming world.

The massive influx of new players, while great for the overall health of the game, presented a new level of technical challenge for the game. For the first few days after the F2P launch, login queues were put in place to avoid overloading the game's starting zones. These were gradually phased out as players finished the tutorial and began making their way into less populated zones, but problems still flared up during peak hours, as well as during large-scale fights. "We knew it would be busy," says Christoph Hombergs, Head of Operations, "but we had no idea of what scale to expect. It definitely exceeded our expectations."

[img]https://i.imgur.com/1hdLQcX.png[/img]

As the player counts began to normalize, login queues were able to be phased out, and performance issues for large fights were fixed. The post-F2P era continues to present challenges for the game, but these are a welcome result of the higher player counts this switch has brought.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/A7K7Ru1.jpg[/img]

The transition wouldn't have been possible without our founders and long-term supporters of the game, who, with the F2P launch, were thanked with ingame gifts. The most notable of these was the unique [b]Specter Wolf[/b].

[h1]Customization Comes to Albion[/h1]
The Percival update also brought the first stages of a wide-ranging new [b]customization system[/b]. Players could now choose from a wide range of hair, beard, face, and underwear options, and could also change their appearance at any time and from anywhere in the world. The options introduced with Percival are only the beginning of character customization in the game. "We're planning on increasing the variety of customization options in different areas over time, including features that aren't present yet," says Lino Claudius, UI Designer for Albion Online. "We want to give players more ways to express and identify themselves with their characters."

[img]https://i.imgur.com/KzOlci4.png[/img]

As a companion system to character customization, [b]mount skins[/b] allowed players to show off rare and valuable mounts that had previously been collecting dust in storage, and a range of new skins were available for those who wanted some wilder options.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/VZXGjSn.png[/img]

[h1]Year Three: Toward a Deeper Gameplay Experience[/h1]
Albion's third year will bring numerous changes and improvements, following the major [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/104122][b]roadmap[/b][/url] that was announced alongside the Oberon update. Its major goals include a complete rethinking of the Outlands, a greater variety of open-world activities for all experience levels and group sizes, PvP "hotspots", improvements to Faction Warfare – all of which will mean more opportunities throughout the world of Albion for all player types. Stay tuned for an updated roadmap coming soon.

For now, though, we want to thank our community for helping us reach this milestone. Happy second birthday to the world of Albion – here's to many more!

notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/6680a76.jpg[/img]
[h1]Percival Update - Ver. 1.15.382 / REV 145855 - 10 July 2019[/h1]

[h1]Features[/h1]
[b]Solo Randomized Dungeons[/b]

Randomized Dungeons balanced for solo players will now appear throughout the open world, and will be distinguishable from group randomized dungeons by their portal-like appearance. Higher-tier solo dungeons can be accessed via special Dungeon Maps, which can be obtained from mob drops or bought from other players through the Marketplace.

[b]New Character Customization Options [/b]

Players now have a larger number of customization options for their characters, including numerous hair, beard, face, and underwear options. Character appearance can now be updated at any time, from anywhere in the world.

For more details on character customization, please see this forum post: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754[/url]

[b]Mount Skins[/b]

Mounts skins can now be used to alter the appearance of a player's active mount. Once unlocked, a mount skin is bound to the account and can be used by all characters. With Percival, numerous rare mounts will be converted to skins, and additional new skins will be unlockable with Gold.

For more details, including a list of pre-Percival mounts that will be converted to skins, please see this forum post: [url=https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754]https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/112754[/url]

[b]New Mobs and Shrines[/b]

New mob types have been added to solo and group Randomized Dungeons for all factions. These include new trap- and nest-type opponents, as well as environmental hazards like explosives. Solo Randomized Dungeons introduce small combat shrines, which give a random combat buff to the first player who activates them, offering advantages in both PvE and PvP.

[b]New Weapon Skills[/b]

Seven new skills have been added to a range of player weapons:
[list]	[*]Axes: Spinning Blades[/*]	[*]Frost Staffs: Ice Shard[/*]	[*]Hammers: Inertia Ring[/*]	[*]Nature Staffs: Rejuvenating Breeze[/*]	[*]Quarterstaffs: Rising Blow[/*]	[*]Spears: Impaler[/*]	[*]Swords: Parry[/*][/list]

[list]	[*]Polished and updated spell effect sounds for Quarterstaffs, Axes, Spears, Daggers, Hammers and Maces based on spell intensity[/*]	[*]Master Volume fader added to Audio Settings UI[/*]	[*]Added new voiceovers to Artifact Foundry NPC[/*][/list]
[b]Other Improvements[/b]
[list]	[*]Character appearance has been greatly improved for unclothed male and female character models[/*]	[*]New language channels have been created for every supported language - players will join the channel that matches their client language[/*]	[*]Date formats can now be set via the "Language" UI[/*]	[*]Up to five emotes can now be assigned to Hotkeys in the Settings menu[/*]	[*]Reworked character location markers and random dungeon markers on worldmap[/*]	[*]Players can now choose whether to automatically transfer newly-purchased items directly from the Marketplace to their inventory (in cases where inventory is full, items will be sent to the "Completed" tab as normal)[/*]	[*]New terrain and level templates created for Solo Randomized Dungeons have been added to Group Randomized Dungeons as well[/*]	[*]Seven new achievements based on Randomized Dungeons and Customization have been added[/*][/list][h1]Changes[/h1]

notes.title: Percival is Live!
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/4uJiFXZ.jpg[/img]

[b]Percival[/b], the seventh major post-launch update for Albion Online, is here! This update brings [b]Randomized Dungeons[/b] balanced for solo players, a new [b]vanity and customization[/b] system, [b]mount skins[/b], new [b]creatures[/b], [b]shrines[/b], and [b]spells[/b], numerous [b]quality-of-life[/b] improvements, and much more. Watch the trailer here:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eGXQLDHkKN0
Read on for more of what's coming with Percival:

[h1]Solo Randomized Dungeons are Here[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/OHTBu3J.jpg[/img]

Whether you're a solo adventurer or a group player waiting for your friends to come online, [b]Solo Randomized Dungeons [/b]are the perfect activity. These new dungeons balanced for single players offer challenging adventures that are never the same twice. Take on a wide range of [b]classic and new enemies[/b], unlock chests, discover new [b]small combat shrines[/b], and descend as far as you dare, or use new [b]solo dungeon maps[/b] to reveal high-tier dungeons with powerful enemies and valuable loot.

[h1]Upgrade Your Looks and Ride in Style[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/Q17xpH9.jpg[/img]

Set yourself apart with a wide range of [b]character customization options[/b], including new hairstyles, beards, and faces. Update your looks at any time from anywhere in the world to give your character its own unique personality. Travel the world in style with new [b]mount skins[/b] that offer appearance upgrades for all major mount types. Choose from dozens of free customization options, or unlock wilder styles with Gold to truly stand out from the crowd.

[h1]Fearsome New Foes, Powerful New Abilities[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/3ilO7VQ.jpg[/img]

Percival introduces a host of [b]deadly new creatures[/b], from ghostly critters to fiery demons to explosive traps, which come with a wide variety of spells and attacks to keep adventurers on their toes. Send them packing with [b]seven new spells[/b] for hammers, spears, staffs, and other weapons that will offer new combat options to a wide range of playstyles and builds.

Other improvements include:
[list]	[*]Expandable Personal Banks[/*]	[*]20v20 City Practice Battles[/*]	[*]Ingame Language Channels[/*]	[*]Extended Crystal GvGs[/*]	[*]New Level Templates for Randomized Dungeons[/*]	[*]...and much more[/*][/list]
For a detailed list of changes, read the patch notes [url=https://albiononline.com/en/changelog/PERCIVAL%20UPDATE][b]here[/b][/url].
