notes.title: Albion Online Dev Talk - Faction Warfare, Part 2
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/D6J2Jqx.jpg[/img]
The [b]Merlyn[/b] update comes to the world of Albion on July 31, bringing an all-new [b]Faction Warfare[/b] system. In this Dev Talk, Robin Henkys, Game Director of Albion Online, follows up his [url=https://albiononline.com/en/news/devtalk-faction-warfare-part-1][b]introductory Faction Warfare video[/b][/url] with a more in-depth look at the various activities and rewards this feature will offer.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YAh8XaJ50OM
No time to watch the video? Read on for a written summary of his talk.

[h1][b]1. Outpost Capturing[/b][/h1]
[b]What are Outposts?[/b]

[b]Outposts [/b]are small military installations found all over the Royal Continent, with their position and status visible on the world map. Initially, an outpost will be controlled by the city closest to it, but this will soon change based on player actions.

[b]Capturing Outposts[/b]
[list]	[*]A outpost is always guarded by a champion of the faction that currently owns it. To take an outpost, players have to defeat the champion and stand uncontested within the control circle for a specified period of time.[/*]	[*]Defeating a champion is not a trivial task. At the very least, it requires three well-coordinated players, but it is more easily done in a group of five or six players.[/*]	[*]Claiming an outpost grants faction points and fame, as well as some Silver from the champion.[/*]	[*]The rewards earned for taking an outpost are split between the participants, so to maximum profits, try to capture an outpost using as few players as possible.[/*]	[*]Once an outpost has been captured, it goes into a cooldown period during which it cannot be recaptured. The cooldown ends when the new owner’s champion spawns.[/*][/list]
[b]Gameplay for Outposts[/b]

In order to ensure enough variety in this activity, and to bring out the character of each faction, we’ve given each champion a unique fighting style and set of abilities:
[list]	[*]The [b]Mountain Champion[/b] is stoic and formidable, summoning the strength of the mountains while fighting.[/*]	[*]The [b]Forest Champion[/b] is agile and confident, relying on his trusted animal companion in battle.[/*]	[*]The [b]Steppe Champion[/b] is sly and cunning, and uses tricks and the power of the desert wind to overcome her opponents.[/*]	[*]The [b]Highland Champion[/b] is rough and brutish, and uses sheer force to take his opponents down.[/*]	[*]And finally, the [b]Swamp Champion[/b] is ancient and wise, and in battle will cast powerful fire spells.[/*][/list]
Of course, the champion is not the only thing you'll need to worry about - before attempting to capture an outpost, it's worth making sure there are no enemy faction players nearby! Given the relatively high number of outposts, you'll often find them unguarded, but it always pays to check.

[b]Design Goals of Outposts[/b]
[list]	[*]As you can see, outpost gameplay is focused on taking enemy outposts rather than defending your own.[/*]	[*]This ensures that players participating in outpost capture do not spend their time waiting to see if opponents will turn up, but instead can move outpost to outpost and earn significant rewards if they go unopposed by other factions.[/*]	[*]Focusing on attack is also a key component of our self-balancing philosophy for Faction Warfare: the more outposts a faction already owns, the fewer attack targets will become available, making it less desirable to work for this faction.[/*][/list][h1][b]2. Faction Trading[/b][/h1]
If you’re less inclined to fight but still want to profit off the Faction Warfare system, you can always participate in [b]trade missions[/b] for your faction. Here's how it works:
[list]	[*]Each city will be the sole source of a unique resource called [b]Fragments of the City Heart[/b]. Players can acquire this resource at the faction leader NPC by spending their earned faction points.[/*]	[*]These city heart fragments are powerful magic resources which can be used as a stand-in resource in refining, effectively bringing down the raw resources needed for refining by a small degree.[/*]	[*]Each city wants to get their hands on the other cities' resources, and to do so has made secret deals with the Black Market Boss of Caerleon. His minions have set up secret smuggling outposts near the cities where they trade in city heart fragments.[/*]	[*]While signed up with a faction, players can acquire a trade pack consisting of that faction's resources..[/*]	[*]This trade pack can be taken to a smuggling outpost near a designated enemy city and exchanged for a pack containing a higher amount of that enemy city resource.[/*]	[*]The pack must be carried the entire time by the faction-flagged player in order to make the exchange. If the item is traded away or lost, the mission will be a failure.[/*]	[*]If a player is killed while carrying a trade pack, the pack will be broken down into city heart fragments which can then be looted.[/*][/list]
There are different sizes of trade packs available, differing in weight, cost, and reward. This allows players to decide between a solo run on a fast horse, a group/escort run on slower, stronger mounts such as oxen, or something in between.

There are two ways you can profit from trade missions:
[list]	[*]All trade missions offer the [b]straightforward profit[/b] of trading a smaller quantity of resources for a larger one.[/*]	[*]Additionally, the resource you’re trading for [b]may be worth more than the one you’re investing[/b]. This of course depends on the player market, which requires comparing prices of different resources for your desired location.[/*][/list]
Faction trading adds to the Faction Warfare system in two ways:
[list]	[*]For [b]traders and transporters[/b], it provides an opportunity to profit from signing up with a faction, which might otherwise not offer enough incentive.[/*]	[*]For [b]PvPers[/b], it adds faction-flagged players who are transporting valuable goods through the world as a target, opening up the opportunity for ambushes, escorts, and all sorts of PVP opportunities with high-value targets.[/*][/list][h1][b]3. Rewards[/b][/h1][h1][b]City Heart Fragments[/b][/h1][list]	[*]As mentioned already, city heart fragments can also be used in [b]refining[/b], where they stand in for a single regular resource of any tier or enchantment level. Each type of heart fragment is limited to that city's most common resource type and can only replace one such resource in any given recipe, so at least some of the actual resource will be required for refining.[/*]	[*]The fact that they can be used at any tier or enchantment level means they are ideally used in place of truly valuable [b]high-end resources[/b].[/*]	[*]They are also required in order to make the corresponding [b]faction cape[/b] (see next section).[/*]	[*]Their use as a stand-in for high-end resources and in the production of faction capes secures their value in the Albion economy, and by extension ensures the [b]ongoing value of faction points[/b].[/*][/list][h1][b]City Crests and Capes[/b][/h1]
City crests can be combined with a regular cape item (as well as a quantity of city heart fragments) to create a [b]faction cape[/b]. Faction capes will be the first set of capes to feature [b]strong passive abilities[/b] which can be used to synergize existing builds.

The idea of these capes is to make an additional item slot available for combat builds, and to strengthen the "You Are What You Wear" system. The effects of this new slot will be noticeable in combat, but as capes will have especially [b]high cooldown times[/b], they will need to work [b]closely in tandem with the rest of a build[/b] to be truly successful.

The cape abilities are as follows:
[list]	[*][b]Bridgewatch Cape: [/b]	[list]		[*]Your first auto attack spawns a sandstorm in front of you, which moves forward and slows enemy attack and move speed.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Fort Sterling Cape:[/b]	[list]		[*]The mountain cape automatically triggers to remove the first stun or silence you receive.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Lymhurst Cape:[/b]	[list]		[*]If you use a spell and are low on energy, the cape triggers an energy-over-time regeneration.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Martlock Cape:[/b]	[list]		[*]When you take damage and are at low health, you automatically receive a short invulnerability shield.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Thetford Cape:[/b]	[list]		[*]Your first auto attack triggers a chain lightning effect which hits up to four enemies near your original target.[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
All of these effects can recur after their cooldown is finished. Cooldown durations, as well as spell strengths, will also scale with item power.
[h1][b]Faction Mounts[/b][/h1]
The final type of item obtainable as a faction reward are baby animals, which can be grown into one of the new [b]faction mounts[/b]:
[list]	[*][b]Bighorn Ram (Martlock):[/b]	[list]		[*]Similar to an ox, but it trades in some transport ability for a higher speed.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Moabird (Bridgewatch):[/b]	[list]		[*]Very fast mount - not quite as fast as a direwolf, but faster than horses, though is quite vulnerable.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Winter Bear (Fort Sterling):[/b]	[list]		[*]Very tough mount with decent speed and good transport ability.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Wild Boar (Lymhurst):[/b]	[list]		[*]Faster than the bear, but not quite as tough and can’t transport quite as much.[/*]	[/list]	[/*]	[*][b]Swamp Salamander (Thetford):[/b]	[list]		[*]Has no gallop ability, but its base speed is higher than any other mount’s, making it hard to slow down.[/*]	[/list]	[/*][/list]
That's all for today, but there's much more to come with the Merlyn update - we hope you're as excited for it as we are. Stay tuned for the next Dev Talk, where we’ll be covering the changes coming to [b]gathering, crafting, and refining[/b] in Albion.

tags.feature: The [b]Merlyn[/b] update comes to the world of Albion on July 31, bringing an all-new [b]Faction Warfare[/b] system.
Faction capes will be the first set of capes to feature [b]strong passive abilities[/b] which can be used to synergize existing builds.
The idea of these capes is to make an additional item slot available for combat builds, and to strengthen the "You Are What You Wear" system.
The cape abilities are as follows:

Bridgewatch Cape: 
						Your first auto attack spawns a sandstorm in front of you, which moves forward and slows enemy attack and move speed.

Fort Sterling Cape:
						The mountain cape automatically triggers to remove the first stun or silence you receive.

Lymhurst Cape:
						If you use a spell and are low on energy, the cape triggers an energy-over-time regeneration.

Martlock Cape:
						When you take damage and are at low health, you automatically receive a short invulnerability shield.

Thetford Cape:
						Your first auto attack triggers a chain lightning effect which hits up to four enemies near your original target.
The final type of item obtainable as a faction reward are baby animals, which can be grown into one of the new [b]faction mounts[/b]:

Bighorn Ram (Martlock): 
						Similar to an ox, but it trades in some transport ability for a higher speed.

Moabird (Bridgewatch): 
						Very fast mount - not quite as fast as a direwolf, but faster than horses, though is quite vulnerable.

Winter Bear (Fort Sterling): 
						Very tough mount with decent speed and good transport ability.

Wild Boar (Lymhurst): 
						Faster than the bear, but not quite as tough and can’t transport quite as much.

Swamp Salamander (Thetford): 
						Has no gallop ability, but its base speed is higher than any other mount’s, making it hard to slow down.

notes.title: Merlyn Arrives on July 31
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/JncaQ0Y.jpg[/img]

Our fourth major content update, [b]Merlyn[/b], arrives on July 31, bringing a huge number of new features, changes, and improvements to the world of Albion.

[h1][b]Faction Warfare[/b][/h1]
Open-world warfare comes to the Royal Continent with an all-new [b]Faction Warfare[/b] system. Sign up with one of five factions, then set out into the wilds of Albion to claim outposts, transport valuable goods, and earn exclusive rewards.
[list][*][b]Outposts and Trading[/b] - Take down enemy factions' outposts by defeating unique faction bosses with their own strengths, skills, and personalities.[/*]	
[*][b]Special Faction Rewards[/b] - New faction resources open up alternative crafting recipes, while faction capes and mounts offer exciting new gameplay opportunities.[/*][/list]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jcdw7hjwess
[h1] [/h1][h1][b]Other Additions and Changes[/b][/h1]
[list][*][b]Refining and Crafting Bonuses[/b] - Each of the Royal Cities now has unique bonuses, based on materials that are rarer in that city's biome.[/*]
[*][b]Resource Redistribution[/b] - Enchanted resources now appear in greater quantities around the Royal Cities, providing new opportunities for gatherers and transporters.[/*]
[*][b]Equipment Overcharge[/b] - Overcharging an item gives it a temporary power boost, at the cost of risking breakage once the overcharge ends.[/*]
[*][b]Marketplace UI Improvements[/b] - In addition to a more streamlined UI, players can now view a more accurate average price display and an in-depth sales history.[/*]
[*][b]New Dungeon[/b] - The new T5 Group Dungeon, [b]Stoneroot Caverns[/b], pits you against hordes of massive Keepers in a sacred underground cave.[/*]
[*][b]New Costumes and Trophies[/b] - New wedding costumes celebrate the first year of Albion Online, and new Laborer Trophies are available for the various gathering nodes.[/*]
[*][b]Additional Improvements[/b] - Merlyn also brings balance and skill updates, easier navigation, bugfixes, and much more.[/*][/list]
For a more detailed list of everything coming with Merlyn, visit our [b]update page[/b]: https://albiononline.com/en/update/Merlyn

Sign up with one of five factions, then set out into the wilds of Albion to claim outposts, transport valuable goods, and earn exclusive rewards.
Take down enemy factions' outposts by defeating unique faction bosses with their own strengths, skills, and personalities.
New faction resources open up alternative crafting recipes, while faction capes and mounts offer exciting new gameplay opportunities.
Each of the Royal Cities now has unique bonuses, based on materials that are rarer in that city's biome.
Enchanted resources now appear in greater quantities around the Royal Cities, providing new opportunities for gatherers and transporters.
Overcharging an item gives it a temporary power boost, at the cost of risking breakage once the overcharge ends.
In addition to a more streamlined UI, players can now view a more accurate average price display and an in-depth sales history.
The new T5 Group Dungeon, [b]Stoneroot Caverns[/b], pits you against hordes of massive Keepers in a sacred underground cave.
New wedding costumes celebrate the first year of Albion Online, and new Laborer Trophies are available for the various gathering nodes.

notes.content:

[h1]Lancelot Patch #9 - Ver. 1.11.362 / REV 119971 - 20 June 2018[/h1]

[h1]Known Issues / Clarifications:[/h1] https://forum.albiononline.com/index.php/Thread/90553-Lancelot-Patch-9-Known-Issues-and-Clarifications/

[h1]Changes[/h1]

[b]Hellgate Changes[/b]
[list][*]Players can now fight their own guild and alliance members in Hellgates when they appear in an enemy party
[*]Yellow Zone 5v5 Hellgates have been adjusted as follows:
[list][*]Fame Factor: 1.5 → 2.5
[*]Loot Factor: 1.75 → 2.25
[*]Silver Factor: 1.75 → 2.25
[*]Improved the loot table for the Hellgate Boss, so that it now drops better loot on average
[/list][*]Fixed a loot table bug for chests in black and red zone 2v2 Hellgates - their rewards were sometimes much higher than intended, and should now be in line with comparable Hellgates
[*]To prevent solo and duo farming, gatekeepers for 5v5 Hellgates (red and black zones) now use a new spell ("Disembowel") when aggro'd by 3 or fewer people
[/list][b]Daily Season Points Adjustments[/b]
[list][*]The daily season points earned for Outlands territories has been adjusted as follows (the cost of placing mages, as well as the energy they drop, has also been updated accordingly):
[list][*]Mercia: 384 → 336 (-12.5%)
[*]Cumbria: 288 → 288 (no change)
[*]Anglia: 192 → 240 (+25%)
[/list][/list][b]Mount/Dismount Audio[/b]
[list][*]To cut down on unnecessary noise in cities, mount/dismount sounds are now only audible to the player performing them within city limits (as these sounds are an important element of PvP, they will remain audible to all players in the open world)
[/list][b]Faction Warfare Preparation[/b]
[list][*]As a teaser for the upcoming content update, builder NPCs have begun constructing faction headquarters in each of the Royal cities
[/list][b]GvG Updates[/b]
[list][*]Added soft item power cap to red zone GvGs (Item Power = 800 / Scaling Factor = 0.2, meaning everything above IP 800 will be scaled down to 20% of its normal power)
[*]To prevent furniture from being used as a blockade during GvGs, outdoor furniture is now hidden during GvG matches, and new furniture cannot be placed during matches
[/list][h1]Balancing Changes[/h1]
Arcane Staffs
[list][*]Time Corridor (Occult Staff)
[list][*]Now also boosts attack speed of allies inside the area
[*]Removed the Damage Over Time effect
[/list][/list]Axes
[list][*]Rending Bleed Stacks (all axes)
[list][*]Healing Reduction: 10% → 7%
[/list][*]Tear Apart (Halberd)
[list][*]Instant Damage: 144.60 → 137.37
[/list][/list]Bows
[list][*]Deadly Shot (all bows)
[list][*]Removed the Cast Speed Increase
[*]It now reduces enemy resistances (stacks up to 3 times)
[*]Damage: 81.43 → 86.52
[*]Cast Range: 11m → 13m
[/list][*]Multishot (all bows)
[list][*]Range: 11m → 12m
[/list][/list]Cursed Staffs
[list][*]Haunting Screams (Cursed Skull)
[list][*]No longer requires Line of Sight
[/list][/list]Daggers
[list][*]Sunder Armor (all daggers)
[list][*]Armor Reduction vs mobs: 0.04  → 0.06
[/list][/list]Fire Staffs
[list][*]Flame Tornado (Blazing Staff)
[list][*]Damage vs Mobs: 47.23 → 43.45
[/list][/list]Frost Staffs
[list][*]Frost Bomb (all Frost Staffs)
[list][*]Hit Delay: 2s → 1.6s
[/list][*]Frost Nova (all Frost Staffs)
[list][*]Hit Delay: 0.2s → 0s
[*]Now completely freezes enemies (Frozen enemies can't attack or cast)
[*]Freeze Duration: 2.44s → 1.26s
[/list][*]Avalanche (Hoarfrost Staff)
[list][*]Cast Time: 1s → 0.7s
[/list][*]Frozen Hell (Icicle Staff)
[list][*]Cast Time: 1s → 0s
[*]Standtime: 0.2s → 0.4s
[/list][*]Ice Crystal (Permafrost Prism)
[list][*]Damage vs mobs: 184.69 → 253.70
[/list][/list]Holy Staffs
[list][*]Holy Explosion (Great Holy Staff)
[list][*]Heal per Tick: 34.75 → 40.67
[/list][*]Holy Touch (Lifetouch Staff)
[list][*]Cast Range: 3m → 6m
[*]Can now be cast even when silenced / stunned
[/list][*]Salvation (Fallen Staff)
[list][*]Delay after Cast: 3s → 2s
[*]Energy Cost: 24 → 18
[/list][*]Holy Orb (Redemption Staff)
[list][*]The orb now always heals for the same amount, no matter the distance
[*]Min Heal: 66.36 → 144.79
[*]Max Heal: 225.63 → 144.79
[*]Projectile Speed: 14.67m/s → 11.00m/s
[*]Cooldown: 10s → 15s
[/list][/list]Nature Staffs
[list][*]Hit & Run (passive)
[list][*]Spells to trigger the effect: 4 → 6
[/list][*]Poison Thorns (all Nature Staffs)
[list][*]Number of Ticks: 10 → 7
[*]Damage per Tick: 11.94 → 12.83
[/list][*]Spirit Animal (Rampant Staff)
[list][*]Spell has been reworked, and no longer stacks up over time.
[*]Instead, the healing strength depends on the number of allies inside the area of each tick.
[*]It also can’t be purged anymore. 
[/list][/list]Quarterstaffs
[list][*]Cartwheel (all Quarterstaffs)
[list][*]Cooldown: 5s → 6s
[/list][*]Forceful Swing (all Quarterstaffs)
[list][*]Auto Attack Damage Reduction vs mobs: 30% → 50%
[*]Radius: 5m → 6m
[/list][*]Mystic Rocks (Staff of Balance)
[list][*]Energy Cost: 0 → 20% of max energy
[*]Slow Strength: 60% → 50%
[/list][*]Hurricane (Iron-clad Staff)
[list][*]Knockback Distance: 1.91m → 5m
[/list][/list]Spears
[list][*]Cripple (all spears)
[list][*]Cooldown: 15s → 20s
[/list][*]Reckless Charge (Spear)
[list][*]Range: 13m → 11m
[*]Enemy airborne duration: 0.6s → 0.5s
[*]Damage: 235.06 → 198.90
[/list][/list]Helmets
[list][*]Energy Regain (all helmets)
[list][*]Channel Duration: 7s → 10s
[*]Energy per tick: 7.10 → 8.10
[/list][*]Force Field (Cloth Cowls)
[list][*]Radius: 5m → 6m
[*]Knockback Distance: 11.67 → 14.22
[/list][*]Energy Shield (Scholar Cowl)
[list][*]Physical Resistance: 0.16 → 0.38
[*]Magic Resistance: 0.16 → 0.10
[/list][*]Perpetual Energy (Royal Cowl)
[list][*]Duration: 10s → 15s
[/list][*]Mortal Agony (Stalker Hood)
[list][*]Armor Reduction: 0.54 → 0.50
[/list][*]Electric Discharge (Judicator Helmet)
[list][*]Cast Time: 0s → 1.2s
[*]Hit Delay: 0.6s → 0s
[/list][/list]Armors
[list][*]Speed Caster (Scholar Robe)
[list][*]Energy Cost Reduction: 40% → 70%
[/list][*]Obsessive Burst (Druid Robe)
[list][*]Damage and Heal Power Increase per Stack: 8% → 7%
[/list][*]Self Ignition (Specter Jacket)
[list][*]Can't be purged anymore
[/list][*]Fury (Soldier Armor)
[list][*]Increased CC Duration per stack: 10% → 6%
[/list][*]Force Shield (Judicator Armor)
[list][*]Healing Received Increase: 50% → 35%
[/list][/list]Shoes
[list][*]Focused Run (Scholar Sandals)
[list][*]Move Speed Increase: 60% → 100%
[/list][*]Defenseless Rush (Royal Sandals)
[list][*]It is now a toggle spell and can't be purged
[*]It no longer reduces resistance by a flat value - instead, while active, the caster's damage taken is increased by 15%
[*]Max Duration: 5s → 7s
[/list][*]Rotten Ground (Cultist Sandals)
[list][*]The area no longer deals damage - it instead reduces enemy resistances
[/list][*]Spectral Run (Specter Shoes)
[list][*]Max Channel Duration: 20s → 16s
[/list][/list]Offhands
[list][*]Offhand scaling reworked: all offhand items now scale in exact relation to item power, i.e. they profit from Destiny Board masteries and item quality bonuses. This is not a straight bonus on top: instead the progression curve has been reworked, so offhand bonus stats should remain at roughly the same values.
[/list]Potions
[list][*]Gigantify Potions
[list][*]Duration: 10s → 8s
[/list][/list]Food
[list][*]Flattened the progression of Combat-Related Stats on food.
[list][*]Food Effect Progression (old percent → new percent):
[list][*]Low-Tier Base: 100% → 100%
[*]Low-Tier Enchanted 1: 150% → 150%
[*]Low-Tier Enchanted 2 / Mid-Tier Base: 200% → 190%
[*]Low-Tier Enchanted 3 / Mid-Tier Enchanted 1: 250% → 230%
[*]Mid-Tier Enchanted 2 / High-Tier Base: 300% → 270%
[*]Mid-Tier Enchanted 3 / High-Tier Enchanted 1: 350% → 300%
[*]High-Tier Enchanted 2: 400% → 330%
[*]High-Tier Enchanted 3: 450% → 350%
[*]Base Stat value from fish-based foods: 75% → 70%
[/list][/list]
[/list]Miscellaneous
[list][*]Cleansing any CC effect now grants a 1-second CC immunity
[/list][h1]Fixes[/h1]
[list][*]Fixed an issue where spells that were simultaneously cast by a player and canceled by another player or mob (via stun, knockback, silence, or other countereffects) were still subject to cooldown time
[*]Fixed a similar issue where the toggle spell button would become stuck if the toggle spell failed due to knockback, silence, or other countereffects
[*]Fixed an issue where the passive skill Weakening could be used without unlocking the corresponding Destiny Board node
[*]Fixed an issue where Desecrate would sometimes fail to inflict DoT on struck enemies
[*]Improved performance of fishing minigame on clients with low FPS
[*]Fixed an issue where ghoul mobs were immune to CC damage while channeling Acid Waste
[*]Fixed an issue for some spells where the graphical spell indicator was bigger than the actual spell effect
[*]Fixed an issue where the combat log sometimes listed the source of an effect as "unknown"
[*]Fixed an issue where DoT effects would keep you in passive combat even when the mob had reset
[*]Improved hit detection for the Claymore charge spell
[*]Cripple now removes the move speed buff for Rotten Ground and Frost Walk
[*]Damage vs. Players and Damage vs. Mobs stats have been removed from Enchanted Facebreaker Shield
[*][Russian version] Numerous fixes and updates to Russian terminology, particularly related to Destiny Board masteries
[*]Numerous additional graphical, animation, texture, audio, UI, and localization fixes
[/list]
